title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke. METHODS: In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter. RESULTS: Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047). CONCLUSION: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings. EDITORIAL COMMENT: A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

title: Epidemiology of 376,383 arteriovenous fistula creations for hemodialysis over 9 years within the Brazilian Unified Public Health System and the Private Healthcare Sector.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease represents a growing public health challenge worldwide, particularly in low- and middleincome countries. In Brazil, where most patients with end-stage renal disease depend on the public healthcare system for dialysis and transplantation, ensuring adequate vascular access - with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) being one of the available options - is critical to sustaining treatment. Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine trends in AVF creation for hemodialysis across Brazil from 2015 to 2023, assessing differences in frequency, geographic distribution, and sectoral disparities between the public and private healthcare sectors. METHODS: A retrospective population-based analysis was conducted using anonymized data from national administrative databases: DATASUS (public sector) and D-TISS (private sector). The majority of AVF creation procedures were included. Statistical analyses considered regional adjustments and were performed using SPSS v.20, with significance set at p < 0.001. RESULTS: Over the nine- year period, 376,383 AVF procedures were recorded, with 90.57% occurring in the public sector. While the absolute number of AVF creations increased, the ratio of AVFs per 1,000 dialysis patients showed a declining trend. Regional disparities were evident, with the Southeast and South regions presenting higher procedure rates compared to other areas. The private sector consistently reported lower creation rates. CONCLUSION: Although, separately, dialysis and AVF rates have risen steadily in Brazil, the relative rate between them has shown a decreasing trend over the years. The predominance of AVF procedures in the public system is more pronounced.

In Brazil, where most patients with end-stage renal disease depend on the public healthcare system for dialysis and transplantation, ensuring adequate vascular access - with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) being one of the available options - is critical to sustaining treatment. Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited.

title: Postoperative Outcomes Following Autologous Breast Reconstruction in Patients Receiving Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators and Aromatase Inhibitors: A Multicenter Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The perioperative management of endocrine therapy remains controversial in patients undergoing autologous breast reconstruction. Because selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) and aromatase inhibitors (AIs) differ in their mechanisms of action and adverse-effect profiles, we evaluated their associations with postoperative outcomes separately in a large multicenter propensity score-matched cohort. METHODS: This retrospective TriNetX study included patients undergoing autologous breast reconstruction. Preoperative exposure was defined as a documented SERM or AI prescription within 3 months of reconstruction. Exposure cohorts were mutually exclusive, and controls excluded both endocrine therapy classes. Separate 1:1 propensity score matching incorporated demographic, comorbidity, oncologic, treatment, venous thromboembolism, and antithrombotic covariates. Outcomes were assessed within 90 days. RESULTS: After matching, 1993 SERM-exposed patients were compared with 1993 controls and 3167 AI-exposed patients with 3167 controls. SERM exposure was not significantly associated with evaluable 90-day outcomes, including coded postoperative debridement (3.01% vs. 2.56%; RR, 1.18; 95% CI, 0.81-1.73; p = 0.39). AI exposure was associated with increased coded postoperative debridement (4.45% vs. 3.38%; RR, 1.33; 95% CI, 1.03-1.72; p = 0.028), while other evaluable outcomes were not significantly different. AI exposure was also associated with greater debridement hazard (HR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.12-1.87; p = 0.0049). CONCLUSIONS: Documented SERM exposure was not significantly associated with evaluable postoperative outcomes, whereas AI exposure was associated with increased coded postoperative debridement. Because debridement codes lack anatomical specificity, this finding is exploratory and does not establish flap-specific compromise. These separate analyses do not establish differences between endocrine therapy classes or support recommendations regarding perioperative continuation or discontinuation.

Because selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) and aromatase inhibitors (AIs) differ in their mechanisms of action and adverse-effect profiles, we evaluated their associations with postoperative outcomes separately in a large multicenter propensity score-matched cohort. METHODS: This retrospective TriNetX study included patients undergoing autologous breast reconstruction.

title: Spectral Photon-Counting Detector CT for Comprehensive Evaluation of Carotid Plaque and Stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Conventional energy-integrating detector (EID) CT is limited in differentiating soft-plaque components due to overlapping attenuation values and is frequently affected by calcification-related blooming artifacts that obscure the vessel lumen and may overestimate stenosis. Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) can provide enhanced spatial resolution and spectral discrimination compared with conventional EID-CT, potentially improving carotid plaque characterization and mitigating artifact-related limitations. This study systematically evaluated image quality, plaque component attenuation, and stenosis visualization across spectral PCD-CT reconstructions. METHODS: We retrospectively included patients who underwent PCD-CT for carotid stenosis assessment. Four monoenergetic (ME 40, 55, 70, and 85 keV), PureLumen (PL), and virtual noncontrast (VNC) reconstructions were analyzed. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), edge sharpness, plaque area, degree of NASCET stenosis, and attenuation of plaque components (intraplaque hemorrhage, lipid-rich necrotic core, fibrotic tissue, calcification) were compared using repeated-measures ANOVA with Bonferroni correction. RESULTS: Our study included 27 patients (16 men, age: 74.5±9.1 y) with 50 plaques. CNR, SNR, and noise decreased with increasing ME levels ( P <0.001). PL yielded CNR and sharpness comparable to ME55, whereas VNC exhibited a near-zero lumen signal. Stenosis remained consistent across ME reconstructions (44% to 45%, P =1.00), but significantly reduced for PL (38%, P <0.001). Lower-energy reconstructions (ME40/ME55) improved the separation of attenuation values between the lumen and the various plaque components. CONCLUSION: Low-energy PCD-CT reconstructions enhance CNR and sharpness while maintaining consistent plaque and stenosis measurements. The PL algorithm may improve the assessment of calcified plaques, where conventional reconstructions may overestimate stenosis. PCD-CT shows promise for advanced plaque composition evaluation, but further validation against MRI and histology is warranted.

Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) can provide enhanced spatial resolution and spectral discrimination compared with conventional EID-CT, potentially improving carotid plaque characterization and mitigating artifact-related limitations. This study systematically evaluated image quality, plaque component attenuation, and stenosis visualization across spectral PCD-CT reconstructions.

title: Cardiac Complications following Creation of Arteriovenous Access in Medicare Beneficiaries with ESKD.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs) are the preferred long-term hemodialysis access for the majority of patients, but produce hemodynamic changes that contribute to cardiac complications including heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and atrial arrhythmia. This cohort study leverages nationwide claims data to examine adverse cardiac events associated with AVGs and AVFs among patients with ESKD. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using 100% Medicare fee-for-service claims to identify adults with ESKD undergoing AVF or AVG creation from 2017-2024. The primary outcome was hospitalization for a composite adverse cardiac event (heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or atrial fibrillation or flutter) within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included the composite outcome through 5 years, its individual components, all-cause hospitalization, and flow-reduction procedures. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models. Independent variable analyses were conducted for the primary outcome. RESULTS: We identified 210,002 accesses (mean age 66.3 years; 43% female) including 147,709 (70%) AVFs and 62,293 (30%) AVGs. AVG recipients had a greater burden of baseline comorbidity and cardiovascular disease. Through 1 year, the cumulative incidence of hospitalization for an adverse cardiac event was 40% (AVF 39%, AVG 44%, P < .001), constituting 61% of all-cause hospitalizations. Heart failure predominated (AVF 33%, AVG 37%, P < .001), followed by atrial fibrillation or flutter (AVF 19%, AVG 21%, P < .001), and pulmonary hypertension (AVF 8%, AVG 9%, P < .001). Older age (≥ 50 years), AVG creation, pre-existing pulmonary hypertension, and atrial arrhythmia were independently associated with a higher hazard of the primary outcome (P < .05). CONCLUSIONS: The high rate of hospitalization for adverse cardiac events in the first year after arteriovenous access creation supports consideration of strategies (e.g., lower-flow forearm access, flow-volume surveillance) to mitigate the hemodynamic consequences of long-term arteriovenous access.

title: The complexity of provoked venous thromboembolism: one treatment plan does not fit all.
abstract: The decision of whether to continue patients diagnosed with venous thromboembolism (VTE) on anticoagulation after the initial treatment period is often nuanced. Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. Transient risk factors are further divided into major factors, such as joint replacement, or minor factors, such as prolonged travel, which determine the magnitude of risk for an initial VTE. In addition, major transient risk factors generally carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE than minor transient risk factors. However, many patients will also have ≥1 persistent VTE risk factor, which further increase the risk for recurrence. Some persistent risk factors, such as inflammatory bowel disease, are associated with a sufficiently high risk of recurrent VTE, for which guidelines recommend indefinite anticoagulation. There are multiple other persistent risk factors that carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE, such as chronic renal insufficiency and obesity. The HI-PRO (High-Risk Patients with Provoked Venous Thromboembolism) trial sought to assess the efficacy and safety of extended thromboprophylaxis for the prevention of recurrent VTE in patients with an initial provoked VTE and at least 1 persistent risk factor. The study found a lower risk of recurrent VTE in the thromboprophylaxis cohort, challenging the traditional time-limited treatment for provoked VTE, but heterogeneity of the study population and small sample size preclude identification of which subsets of patients could safely discontinue anticoagulation. We consider the conundrum of provoked VTE in this review.

title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear. METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS). RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory. DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT. TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04140110; the Registration Date, October 22, 2019.

title: Ruptured giant vertebrobasilar aneurysms: illustrative cases.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Giant vertebrobasilar aneurysms are rare and have a poor natural history. Compared with smaller aneurysms, giant aneurysms have a significantly higher risk of rupture, and a posterior circulation location is itself an independent predictor of rupture regardless of size. Clinical presentation and symptomatology are highly variable, often with nonspecific symptoms progressing insidiously, resulting in delays of diagnosis. There are also significant treatment challenges. The authors describe their experience in 2 cases. OBSERVATIONS: Both patients presented with symptomatic brainstem compression. One patient presented with headache, gait difficulties, left face numbness, and facial droop. The other presented with left-sided trigeminal pain, sixth nerve palsy, blurry vision, and unsteady gait. Both patients developed catastrophic subarachnoid hemorrhage within days following presentation, before planned intervention, with rapid progression to death. LESSONS: Consistent with prior reports, both patients presented with symptomatic brainstem compression, which may have reflected aneurysm growth or instability. These data, along with prior reports, emphasize the poor clinical outcomes associated with symptomatic brainstem compression due to giant vertebrobasilar aneurysms, as well as the urgent and timely need to treat them despite no prior hemorrhage. Higher clinical suspicion is warranted, and further advances in endovascular technologies are necessary to provide reliable, improved clinical outcomes. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26399.

title: Neurological and Medical Complications in Brain Tumor Patients. 2026 Update.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Patients with brain tumors have a plethora of potential complications that arise from both the tumor and its therapeutic management. These complicate clinical management and produce morbidity and occasionally mortality. In this review we discuss the most common neurological and medical complications that include tumor-related epilepsy, vasogenic edema, infection, thromboembolism, endocrine abnormalities and cognitive impairment and its management. This review is an update to the 2020 article by Schiff and Alyahya. RECENT FINDINGS: IDH mutant gliomas cause neuronal hyperexcitability via D-2 -hydroxyglutarate production; use of IDH inhibitors may lower the rate of seizures in this patient population. Pneumocystis prophylaxis with antibiotics has been traditionally recommended with radiation and concurrent temozolomide chemotherapy but newer data suggest no difference in hospitalization or survival. Podoplanin produced by tumor cell releases into the circulation, often via extracellular vesicles, activates platelets and may contribute to venous thrombus formation. Direct oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) are the treatment of choice for venous thromboembolism, with high quality of evidence and a strong recommendation in cancer-associated thrombosis. Though brain tumor patients were underrepresented in clinical trials, retrospective studies support its safety in this population. Brain tumor patients are prone to complications arising from both the tumor and the treatment strategies. Management requires a multidisciplinary strategy with supportive medications including antiseizure medications, corticosteroids, anticoagulants for thromboembolism, and neurocognitive rehabilitation. Early recognition and timely intervention can reduce the morbidity associated with these complications leading to better patient outcomes.

title: Preprocedural angiographic difference in cerebral circulation time and clinical outcomes after successful reperfusion for middle cerebral artery occlusion.
abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate whether the affected-to-contralateral difference in cerebral circulation time (ΔCCT) on preprocedural digital subtraction angiography is associated with early neurological and 90-day functional outcomes after endovascular treatment (EVT) and successful reperfusion. METHODS: Patients with acute M1 or non-distal M2 middle cerebral artery occlusion who underwent EVT and achieved successful reperfusion (mTICI ≥2b) were retrospectively included. Semi-automatically measured ΔCCT was evaluated in relation to the primary outcome of 24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) improvement and the exploratory outcomes of early neurological deterioration (END) and a 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score ≥ 3. Models were adjusted for age, sex, baseline NIHSS score, collateral status, and occlusion location. RESULTS: Among 132 patients, the median ΔCCT was 1.31 s (IQR, 0.97-1.67 s). Each 1-standard-deviation increase in ΔCCT was associated with 3.39 points less 24-hour NIHSS improvement (adjusted β = -3.39, 95% confidence interval [CI] -4.79 to -1.98; P < 0.001), higher odds of END (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.11, 95% CI 1.92-5.42; P < 0.001), and higher odds of a 90-day mRS score ≥ 3 (aOR 1.58, 95% CI 1.06-2.41; P = 0.028). CONCLUSION: Among patients with M1 or non-distal M2 occlusion who achieved successful reperfusion, a longer pre-EVT ΔCCT was associated with less early neurological improvement and, in exploratory analyses, higher odds of END and an unfavorable 90-day outcome. Its generalizability to broader EVT populations requires further evaluation.

title: Synthesis of Fluorinated and Iodinated Cyanoacrylates and Their Application to Novel Liquid Embolic Compositions.
abstract: Liquid embolic agents are used for permanent vascular occlusion, but Histoacryl lacks intrinsic radiopacity and exhibits strong microcatheter adhesion. In this study, iodinated and fluorinated cyanoacrylates were investigated for liquid embolic compositions. 2-Iodoethyl 2-cyanoacrylate (IECA) had a calculated iodine concentration of 1100 mg I/mL. Among the fluorinated cyanoacrylates evaluated, 2,2,3,3,3-pentafluoropropyl 2-cyanoacrylate (PFPCA) showed the highest polymerization rate (15.77 ± 1.96 μL/s). The IECA/PFPCA blend containing 67% IECA (IF67) had an iodine concentration of 730 mg I/mL. The optimized formulation, IFO50, containing IF67 and 50% ethyl oleate, showed a polymerization rate of 0.80 ± 0.07 μL/s, an iodine concentration of 370 mg I/mL, and a microcatheter adhesion force of 2.24 ± 0.36 N. In rabbit renal artery embolization, IFO50 was visible under fluoroscopy, and post-embolization digital subtraction angiography showed no contrast-medium opacification of the treated artery. Computed tomography at 7 days showed the embolic cast in the treated kidney without apparent migration to distant organs.

title: Rapid Endovascular Hemorrhage Control in Trauma: Joint Position Statement from the American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma and the Society of Interventional Radiology.
abstract: Timely hemorrhage control is a critical determinant of survival after traumatic injury, and advances in transarterial embolization have made rapid access to endovascular intervention an increasingly important component of contemporary trauma care. This joint position statement from the American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma and the Society of Interventional Radiology clarifies expectations for interventional radiology under ACS Verification, Review, and Consultation Program Standard 4.15 and provides practical guidance for integrating endovascular hemorrhage control into trauma centers. Standard 4.15 reflects a requirement for system readiness rather than a universal mandate that every vascular intervention begin within 60 minutes. Rapid intervention is expected when clinically indicated, particularly for patients with an endovascular target who are hemodynamically labile, and the relevant performance interval is the time from a shared decision by trauma surgery and interventional radiology to proceed with intervention to arterial puncture. Trauma centers should establish multidisciplinary activation pathways that enable rapid mobilization of personnel and resources while preserving clinical judgment regarding patient selection and competing priorities. Recommended strategies include standardized activation protocols, process mapping, parallel rather than sequential workflows, early patient transport when appropriate, documentation of key time points, structured debriefing, and continuous performance monitoring. Interventional radiologists should be integrated as essential members of multidisciplinary trauma teams rather than engaged late as procedural consultants. Applying the 60-minute expectation according to clinical urgency and monitoring decision-to-puncture time focuses Standard 4.15 on its intended objectives: institutional readiness, timely definitive hemorrhage control in appropriately selected high-risk patients, and continuous performance improvement.

title: Sirtuins in Cellular Senescence and Cardiovascular Diseases: From Mechanistic Basis to Activator Development and Translational Perspectives.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and cellular senescence serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of cardiovascular degeneration and related diseases. Sirtuins act as a crucial molecular hub linking cellular senescence to CVDs, and their upregulated activity is closely associated with delayed cellular senescence and preserved normal cardiovascular function; therefore, the research and development of small-molecule Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) hold important research value and promising translational potential for CVD intervention. This review systematically elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which various Sirtuin subtypes influence senescence-related processes in CVDs through the regulation of biological events such as DNA damage repair, mitochondrial homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Furthermore, it comprehensively outlines their roles in major cardiovascular conditions, including hypertension, angiogenesis, atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysm and dissection, and heart failure. Finally, this paper summarizes recent advances in the development of Sirtuin activators and, in light of current challenges such as insufficient specificity and hurdles in clinical translation, provides perspectives on the future development of Sirtuin-targeted therapies for the prevention and treatment of CVDs.

title: Chest Pain in Vain: Spontaneous Portal Vein Thrombosis.
abstract: A 53-year-old man with a patient-reported history of ultrasound-diagnosed fatty liver disease presented with sudden-onset severe chest pain and a brief loss of consciousness, followed by progressive abdominal pain and a single episode of bloody diarrhoea. Admission investigations approximately 24 hours after the chest pain episode showed a D-dimer of 14,502 µg/L and high-sensitivity troponin I below 3 ng/L. An arterial-phase computed tomography (CT) aortogram showed no aortic dissection but did not establish portal venous patency. Following specialist thoracic radiology review, the aortogram was considered satisfactory to exclude pulmonary embolism down to the segmental level, and dedicated pulmonary angiography was not performed. Portal venous-phase CT performed 72 hours after the aortogram demonstrated extensive portal, superior mesenteric, and splenic vein thrombosis, with equivocal caecal and ascending colonic changes. Symptoms improved during anticoagulation. Repeat CT three months later showed resolution of thrombosis, with all three affected veins patent. This case illustrates the importance of selecting an imaging protocol appropriate to the evolving clinical presentation. An unrevealing arterial-phase examination did not exclude portal venous thrombosis. The relationship between the thrombosis and the initial chest pain and collapse remains uncertain, as does the contribution of the patient's reported fatty liver disease.

title: Association of Advanced Age With Functional Recovery After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Large-core Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Evidence supporting endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large-core ischemic stroke has expanded, but outcomes in patients aged ≥80 years remain insufficiently characterized. We evaluated outcomes after EVT in this population, with particular attention to prestroke disability-adjusted functional recovery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with anterior-circulation large vessel occlusion and large-core stroke (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score 0 to 5 or CT perfusion core volume ≥50 mL) treated with EVT between October 2019 and September 2025. The primary outcome was prestroke disability-adjusted functional recovery, defined as 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≤ prestroke mRS + 1. RESULTS: Among 377 patients, 75 were aged ≥80 years, and 302 were <80 years. Functional recovery occurred in 14.7% and 18.9%, respectively. Age ≥80 years was not significantly associated with functional recovery (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.45-2.22; p = 0.992). Patients aged ≥80 years had lower odds of mRS 0 to 3 (aOR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.21-0.79) and higher odds of mortality (aOR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.01-3.16). Successful reperfusion and hemorrhagic outcomes did not differ significantly between groups. Each 10-year increase in age was associated with lower odds of functional recovery (aOR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.46-0.77). CONCLUSION: Among selected patients aged ≥80 years with large-core ischemic stroke, successful reperfusion and functional recovery remained achievable after EVT, despite poorer conventional functional outcomes and higher mortality. Advancing age was associated with progressively worse outcomes when modeled continuously. These findings support individualized prognostic assessment after EVT rather than reliance on chronological age alone.

title: Enterococci as Emerging Pathogens in Infective Endocarditis and Cardiac Device Infections: Future Implications.
abstract: Enterococci are emerging as important pathogens in an era of an aging population with high healthcare and antibiotic exposure, along with an increasing utilization of prosthetic valves, transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), and cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs). Contemporary cohorts place enterococci among the three leading causes of infective endocarditis, with highest risk after TAVR, where enterococci account for 15% to 30% of cases in several registries. Enterococci cause a smaller proportion of CIED infections, but present late with lead or valve involvement. Enterococcus faecalis currently causes majority of enterococcal endocarditis. Its endovascular tropism, adhesion to damaged tissue and prosthetic surfaces, biofilm tolerance, and association with occult infective endocarditis during bacteremia make it the principal cardiac species of concern. Enterococcus faecium represents a distinct future threat. Hospital-adapted lineages combine prolonged intestinal colonization, environmental persistence, mobile resistance elements, ampicillin resistance, frequent vancomycin resistance, and biofilm capacity. Absolute burden may rise because the population-at risk-living with cardiac foreign devices is expanding. Future monitoring therefore requires linked, species-level surveillance that connects bacteremia, imaging, recurrence, resistance, and genomic data.

title: Predicting prosthetic use and survival following transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To examine associations between BLARt, CFS, prosthetic use and 24-month survival after unilateral transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 168 adults aged ≥65 years who underwent unilateral transfemoral amputation between 2019 and 2023. BLARt was analysed as a continuous score and CFS as an ordinal measure grouped as ≤4, 5 and ≥6. Prosthetic-use analyses excluded participants who had died by the relevant time point. Logistic regression, exact tests, ROC analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analysis were used. RESULTS: At discharge, 23 of 132 survivors (17.4%) were using a prosthesis; at 24 months, 17 of 80 survivors (21.3%) were using one. Higher BLARt scores were associated with lower odds of prosthetic use at discharge (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.33-0.60) and 24 months (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.37-0.69; both p<.001). Prosthetic use differed across CFS groups at both time points (p<.001), with no prosthetic users among participants with CFS ≥6. By 24 months, 88 participants (52.4%) had died. Compared with CFS ≤4, adjusted odds of death were higher for CFS 5 (OR 4.12, 95% CI 1.12-15.20) and CFS ≥6 (OR 8.40, 95% CI 1.97-35.80). CFS and the combined mortality model each had an AUC of approximately 0.71. CONCLUSIONS: BLARt was associated with prosthetic use among survivors, while increasing frailty was strongly associated with both lower prosthetic use and higher 24-month mortality. These measures may support multidisciplinary prognostic discussion but should not be used as rigid thresholds for prosthetic rehabilitation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 168 adults aged ≥65 years who underwent unilateral transfemoral amputation between 2019 and 2023. BLARt was analysed as a continuous score and CFS as an ordinal measure grouped as ≤4, 5 and ≥6.

title: Medical Complications of Catatonia and Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Catatonia and neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) are related neuropsychiatric conditions linked to diverse and potentially life-threatening medical complications; however, no large-scale review of existing literature has described the types and rates of such complications. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to systematically examine documented medical complications associated with catatonia/NMS, delineate their clinical implications, and inform strategies for monitoring and improving patient outcomes. METHODS: Systematic searches of PubMed and Web of Science were conducted up to February 8, 2025 for articles including patients with catatonia or NMS who experienced medical complications. Reviewers independently performed screening and data extraction. Quality assessment was completed via the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Case data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. RESULTS: 281 articles (11 observational studies and 270 case reports/series) met inclusion criteria. Eleven observational studies examined medical complications in 2,008 patients with catatonia/NMS; study quality was low in 1, moderate in 6, and high in 4. Across studies, pneumonia occurred in 0-64% of patients, rhabdomyolysis in 0-30%, and deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolus (DVT/PE) in 0-25%, with these complications reported in both malignant and non-malignant presentations. Comparative studies identified catatonia as a significant risk factor for specific complications including DVT and rhabdomyolysis. Case reports/series (364 patients; mean age 45.7 years) demonstrated widespread complications including rhabdomyolysis (n=178), renal dysfunction (n=105), respiratory dysfunction (n=78), respiratory infections (n=47), aspiration (n=36), pulmonary emboli and infarcts (n=43), cardiac dysfunction (n=37), and malnutrition (n=63). Overall 23.9% (n=87) of case-reported patients experiencing medical complications from catatonia/NMS died. Within this case-report sample, mortality rates appeared lower among those receiving benzodiazepines (n=26, 16.9% vs n=61, 29.1%) and electroconvulsive therapy (n=6, 7.3% vs. n=81, 28.7) compared to those not receiving such interventions. CONCLUSIONS: Catatonia/NMS carries high risks for multisystem complications and mortality, including in non-malignant cases and younger patients. Rhabdomyolysis, renal injury, respiratory compromise, and thromboembolism were particularly common. Among case reported patients, numerically lower mortality rates were seen in those who received benzodiazepines or electroconvulsive therapy. Clinicians should recognize strategies that may reduce risk for certain medical complications.

title: Amrecibart and cenvacibart for the prevention of catheter-related thrombosis (ROXI-CATH): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are often complicated by venous thromboembolism, yet no thromboprophylaxis is approved. Factor XI (FXI) inhibition might prevent catheter-associated venous thromboembolism without increasing bleeding. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of amrecibart and cenvacibart for preventing venous thromboembolism after PICC placement. METHODS: ROXI-CATH is a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial conducted across 12 hospital centres in Bulgaria, Canada, Israel, Romania, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants aged 18 years or older undergoing PICC insertion, with the PICC expected to remain for at least 14 days, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 or less were randomly assigned (1:1:1) using a permuted block design and stratified by site and diagnosis of active cancer to receive a single intravenous infusion of amrecibart (300 mg; anti-FXI A2 domain monoclonal antibody), cenvacibart (250 mg; anti-FXI catalytic domain monoclonal antibody), or placebo. Participants, principal investigators, and study site staff were masked to treatment assignment. The primary efficacy outcome was adjudicated venous thromboembolism (symptomatic or asymptomatic PICC-associated deep vein thrombosis or superficial vein thrombosis, or pulmonary embolism, including pulmonary embolism-related death) up to day 14. Ultrasounds were performed on days 7 and 14. The key secondary efficacy outcome was adjudicated thrombosis detected by ultrasound in the upper extremity with the PICC up to day 14. The primary safety outcome was site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to the end of the study. The key secondary safety outcomes were adjudicated major and clinically relevant non-major (CRNM) bleeding up to day 14. Efficacy analyses were performed in the full analysis set, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug and with any evaluable post-baseline ultrasound or a confirmed episode of venous thromboembolism. Safety analyses were performed in the safety analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug (as treated). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299111 (completed; these analyses were performed after database lock on May 6, 2026). FINDINGS: Between Sept 20, 2024, and Dec 19, 2025, 240 participants were screened, and 195 were randomly assigned to amrecibart (n=65), cenvacibart (n=66), or placebo (n=64). One participant in the placebo group who did not receive study treatment and had no evaluable ultrasound was excluded from the full analysis set. The median follow-up time was 100 days (IQR 100-103). The median age was 60 years (49-69), and 89 (46%) of 194 participants were female, 105 (54%) were male, and 192 (99%) were White. Adjudicated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occured in 13 (20%) of 65 participants in the amrecibart group (odds ratio [OR] 0·37 [90% credible interval 0·18-0·65]), 13 (20%) of 66 participants in the cenvacibart group (0·36 [0·17-0·64]) compared with 27 (43%) of 63 participants in the placebo group. Adjudicated PICC-associated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occurred in 12 (18%) participants in the amrecibart group (OR 0·30 [95% CI 0·14-0·67]), 13 (20%) participants in the cenvacibart group (0·32 [0·14-0·69]), compared with 27 (43%) participants in the placebo group. Site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to day 100 occurred in 45 (69%) participants in the amrecibart group, 42 (64%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and 48 (76%) participants in the placebo group. No participants had major bleeding up to day 14. CRNM bleeding up to day 14 occurred in two (3%) participants in the amrecibart group, two (3%) in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred in nine (14%) participants in the ambrecibart group, six (9%) in the cenvacibart group, and ten (16%) in the placebo group. One (2%) participant in the amrecibart group, four (6%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) participants in the placebo group died; these deaths were assessed as not related to treatment by the respective investigators. INTERPRETATION: A single infusion of amrecibart or cenvacibart reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism following PICC insertion, suggesting FXI inhibition at the A2 or catalytic domain as a promising prophylactic strategy for contact-mediated thrombosis. title: Global trends and intellectual structure in war surgery and combat casualty care: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis (2000-2026).
abstract: BACKGROUND: War surgery and combat casualty care (CCC) research has expanded rapidly, yet its growth dynamics, collaboration structure, thematic evolution and citation-based intellectual architecture remain incompletely characterised. This study mapped war surgery and CCC literature to identify dominant, emerging and declining themes and influential actors. METHODS: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis used Web of Science Core Collection records retrieved on 15 February 2026. Articles published between 2000 and 2026 were identified through a topic search combining war/CCC terms with conflict-setting anchors and refined to English-language journal publications in relevant clinical categories. Performance indicators and network analyses were implemented in bibliometrix/Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and CiteSpace. The corpus was partitioned into three time slices to assess thematic evolution and temporal keyword dynamics. RESULTS: The final corpus comprised 413 WoSCC records indexed as Article. Production rose markedly after 2009 and remained sustained, while mean citations per article declined in recent cohorts, consistent with shorter citation windows. Thematic mapping showed a stable core around trauma/CCC and haemorrhage, alongside diversification towards capability-oriented themes. Burst detection and frequency-ratio analyses identified prolonged field care, readiness, and endovascular and transfusion-related innovations as accelerating topics, while earlier intervention-specific terms declined. The collaboration network was hub-dominated, indicating a concentrated knowledge-production structure organised around limited high-intensity bilateral links. CONCLUSIONS: War surgery and CCC research is organised around a durable clinical core but is increasingly oriented towards system resilience under evacuation delays and resource constraints. Strengthening multi-country collaboration and sustaining inter-conflict research capacity are key levers for preparedness and civilian-military knowledge transfer.

METHODS: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis used Web of Science Core Collection records retrieved on 15 February 2026.

title: The pathological role of chemokines and chemokine receptors in diabetic vascular disease.
abstract: Diabetic vascular diseases, which include microvascular and macrovascular diseases, are a common complication of diabetes mellitus. Both chemokines and their receptors are involved in the pathophysiological process of diabetic vascular diseases, given their diverse functions. Crucially, when evaluating these chemokine networks, it is essential to distinguish descriptive clinical and bioinformatic biomarker observations from functional causal mechanisms established through in vitro and in vivo interventional studies, as observational concentration changes alone do not inherently demonstrate a direct pathogenic role or identify a therapeutic target. In this review, we examine recent studies and provide an overview of the mechanisms underlying chemokine-mediated signaling in diabetic microvascular and macrovascular diseases. We conclude that while circulating chemokines primarily serve as diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers, specific functional chemokine axes represent viable therapeutic targets for diabetic vascular complications.

title: Pediatric spontaneous vertebro-venous fistula coil occlusion with vertebral artery preservation and distal vertebral artery flow restoration.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vertebro-venous fistula (VVF) is a rare high-flow arteriovenous shunt between the vertebral artery and the surrounding venous plexus. Spontaneous VVF in the pediatric population is exceptionally uncommon. Prior pediatric reports have demonstrated successful endovascular fistula occlusion with preservation of vertebral artery patency, although the reported experience remains limited. OBSERVATIONS: A 9-year-old boy presented with an 8-month history of progressive cervical and upper thoracic pain without neurological deficit. MRI demonstrated a left suboccipital vascular lesion with bilateral vertebral artery enlargement and diminution of the distal left vertebral artery. Digital subtraction angiography confirmed a high-flow direct arteriovenous fistula at the V3 segment with a large venous pouch and absence of V4 visualization. Endovascular coil embolization achieved marked reduction in fistula flow with immediate restoration of V4 segment visualization. Follow-up angiography confirmed complete obliteration without residual shunting. LESSONS: Spontaneous pediatric VVF can be successfully treated by precise fistula-point coil occlusion with vertebral artery preservation. Timely and complete endovascular fistula obliteration can restore distal vertebral artery visualization while preserving the parent artery. This illustrates the potential reversibility of flow-related angiographic abnormalities in high-flow VVF.

title: Endovascular treatment of hepatic artery bleeding and pseudoaneurysms using stent-grafts: a retrospective single-centre analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate technical and clinical success rates and complications of stent-grafting for hepatic artery bleeding or pseudoaneurysms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study consecutively included 58 patients who underwent attempted stent-grafting for hepatic artery bleeding (n = 40) or pseudoaneurysm (n = 18) between January 2010 and June 2021. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 97% (56/58) of cases. Insufficient haemostasis after technical success was present in five cases (88% primary clinical success), decreasing to three cases after reintervention. In 3/5 cases, it was due to undersizing of the stent-graft, which occurred frequently, especially in vessel sizes ≥ 6 mm (n = 19, compared to the non-acute vessel diameter; n = 11, compared to the acute one). Median occlusion-free survival was 763 days. Patency rates were 81 ± 6% at 30 days and 56 ± 10% at two years. Early occlusion (≤ 30 days) was associated with significantly smaller stent-graft diameters (4.7 ± 0.7 mm vs 5.4 ± 0.7 mm; p = 0.014). In multivariate Cox regression analysis, a small diameter (4 mm) was confirmed as a risk factor for stent-graft occlusion (HR = 8.59, p = 0.006). Liver necrosis or liver failure due to insufficient collateralization occurred only in early occlusions. Median overall survival was 714 days. In 6/29 documented deaths, mortality was procedure-related (four because of insufficient haemostasis, with two after technical failure and two after technical success, and two because of fatal liver failure after stent-graft occlusion). CONCLUSION: Stent-grafting is effective for managing hepatic artery bleeding, but precise sizing is crucial, as undersizing and small diameters increase the risk of inadequate haemostasis and occlusion. KEY POINTS: Question What are the technical and clinical outcomes of stent-graft treatment for hepatic artery bleeding or pseudoaneurysm, and which factors influence these outcomes? Findings Stent-graft treatment achieved high technical and clinical success rates. Stent-graft undersizing and smaller stent-graft diameters were associated with inadequate haemostasis and occlusion. Clinical relevance Stent-graft treatment is an effective option for managing hepatic artery bleeding or pseudoaneurysm in critically ill patients. Accurate stent-graft sizing is a key determinant of clinical success.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study consecutively included 58 patients who underwent attempted stent-grafting for hepatic artery bleeding (n = 40) or pseudoaneurysm (n = 18) between January 2010 and June 2021. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 97% (56/58) of cases.

title: [Image-guided procedures for treatment of erectile dysfunction].
abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is defined as the chronic inability to achieve and maintain erection sufficient for sexual intercourse. It is a common condition, affecting an estimated 30-50 % of men above the age of 40, and can significantly impair quality of life and interpersonal relationships. The most common vascular etiology includes arterial obstruction of the pelvic arteries and venous leakage. The goal of image-guided endovascular treatments is to restore adequate erectile function. Arterial blood flow to the penis can be achieved through endovascular revascularization and venous leakage can be treated by embolization. The studies published to date show that these minimally invasive procedures are effective and safe in carefully selected patients and treatment outcomes remain stable over the long term in most patients.

title: Saphenofemoral junction reconstruction and recurrence after the treatment of superficial venous reflux disease with endovenous ablation methods.
abstract: 2 p BackgroundRecurrence of varicosities and reflux-related symptoms after endovenous ablation of the great saphenous vein (GSV) remains common. Standard ablation is delivered 1.5-2 cm distal to the saphenofemoral junction (SFJ), leaving the junctional tributaries and dilated proximal junction untreated, unlike conventional high ligation and stripping. We compared standard endovenous ablation with a technique combining open SFJ reconstruction and endovenous ablation.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed patients treated for symptomatic primary GSV reflux. Group 1 underwent standard endovenous ablation (at our institution or referred from elsewhere). Group 2 underwent open SFJ reconstruction - ligation of the junctional tributaries, division of the saphenous vein, and reduction of the dilated common femoral vein - plus endovenous ablation of the GSV trunk. The protocol was introduced during the study period and applied selectively and non-randomly; patients with a body mass index ≥30 kg/m, those aged ≥70 years and those with groin skin infection received standard ablation. Beyond a 3-month review, duplex follow-up was not standardised and was performed mainly when symptoms recurred. Symptomatic recurrence, recurrent visible varicosities, duplex recurrence patterns, reintervention and complications were reported separately.ResultsGroup 1 included 115 patients (70 treated at our institution and 45 referred after treatment elsewhere) and Group 2 included 203. Mean age was 54.3 ± 10.9 and 48.7 ± 14.8 years, and 62.6% and 71.9% were female, respectively. Group 1 had a higher body mass index and more diabetes, hypertension and smoking (all P ≤ .003). During follow-up, 18 patients in Group 1 (15.7%) returned with symptomatic recurrence, compared with 7 (3.4%) in Group 2 (< .001; adjusted OR 0.14, 95% CI 0.05-0.40). No Group 2 patient showed a patent refluxing GSV trunk. In Group 2, six patients (3.0%) had groin wound complications, four managed with wound care and two requiring surgical revision, and one had a minor groin hematoma; one Group 1 patient developed deep vein thrombosis. There was no pulmonary embolism and no mortality.ConclusionsIn this selected, non-randomised cohort, adding open SFJ reconstruction to endovenous GSV ablation was associated with an acceptable complication rate, at the cost of reintroducing groin wound morbidity, and with lower symptomatic recurrence than standard ablation. Given the baseline imbalance, potential referral bias and non-standardised follow-up, these findings show an association rather than a preventive effect. Whether patients at particularly high risk of SFJ/anterior accessory saphenous vein-related recurrence benefit from this approach should be tested prospectively.

title: MEX3B leads to aberrant expression of VCAN, aggravating the thoracic aortic dissection by contributing to the phenotype transformation of VSMCs.
abstract: In vitro Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a lethal condition due to the risk of aortic rupture and malperfusion of arterial branches. Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis. A murine model of TAD was established with β‑aminopropionitrile monofumarate and angiotensin II. Hematoxylin and eosin and elastic Van Gieson staining were performed to assess the TAD formation and fragmentation of elastic fibers. Echocardiography was applied to measure the diameter of thoracic aorta. RT‑qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry were employed to detect the expression of phenotypic transformation markers of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). mRNA sequencing was performed to further explore the downstream factors of MEX3B. MEX3B was upregulated following TAD induction. Knockdown of MEX3B alleviated TAD formation, as evidenced by decreased diameter and hematomas of thoracic aorta, as well as the enhanced integrity of the aortic structure and decreased thrombi in the false lumens. Loss of MEX3B mitigated the TAD‑induced depletion and fragmentation of elastic fibers., small interfering RNA pool‑mediated MEX3B downregulation triggered VSMC switching from a synthetic towards a contractile phenotype. High‑throughput transcriptomics demonstrated that the MEX3B knockdown reduced the expression of versican (VCAN). MEX3B potentiated VCAN mRNA stability by binding to its 3'untranslated region. VCAN downregulation induced a contractile phenotype of VSMCs. In conclusion, the loss of MEX3B protected against TAD, potentially via its contribution to VSMC phenotype switching, which may be associated with the downregulation of VCAN. The present study preliminarily demonstrated the function and mechanism of MEX3B in TAD. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding TAD pathogenesis.

Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis.

title: Perioperative venous thromboembolism prophylaxis during penile prosthesis surgery without routine drain placement: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients undergoing penile prosthesis surgery are at elevated risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet perioperative thromboprophylaxis is not addressed in current urologic guidelines and the safety of subcutaneous heparin (SqH) without drain placement remains unclear. We aim to evaluate the safety and efficacy of perioperative SqH for VTE prevention in penile prosthesis surgery performed without surgical drains. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all penile prosthesis surgeries performed at a single institution from January 2019 to January 2025 in which no drain was placed. Demographics, comorbidities, Caprini risk scores, VTE risk factors, hematoma incidence, and 90-day postoperative complications were compared between patients who did and did not receive perioperative SqH. RESULTS: The primary outcome of our study was postoperative VTE, with secondary outcomes including hematoma formation and 90-day complications. Of 524 patients, 85% were classified as high risk for VTE (Caprini ≥ 5). A total of 246 (47%) received perioperative SqH. VTE occurred in 0.7% (2/278) of patients who did not receive SqH, while no VTE was observed in the SqH group. Hematoma rates were similar between groups (SqH 2.0% vs non-SqH 2.2%; P = .920). Caprini scores and most comorbidities were comparable, though smoking (P = .043) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (P = .025) were more common in the non-SqH cohort. DISCUSSION: Implementation of VTE prophylaxis with SqH in penile prosthesis patients may reduce the risk of VTE in a high-risk population and is relatively cost effective and simple to implement. The main strength of this study is that it is the largest cohort of penile prosthesis patients receiving SqH to be analyzed. In addition, our patient population is unique in the lack of drain placement postoperatively. The study is limited by its retrospective nature and potential bias in reporting complications. The cohort of patients receiving SqH prophylaxis did not develop a VTE and adverse event rates were similar between groups suggesting a possible protective benefit without increasing postoperative complications.

We aim to evaluate the safety and efficacy of perioperative SqH for VTE prevention in penile prosthesis surgery performed without surgical drains. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all penile prosthesis surgeries performed at a single institution from January 2019 to January 2025 in which no drain was placed.

title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial.
abstract: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion eligible for EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset were randomly assigned (1:1) to the tenecteplase group receiving intra‑arterial tenecteplase during EVT or the control group receiving EVT alone. The primary endpoint was favorable functional outcome. Of 380 randomised patients (192 in the tenecteplase group and 188 in the control group), primary outcome data were available for 190 and 186 patients, respectively. Favorable 90-day functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) occurred in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 46.8% of the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 0.76, [95% CI 0.50-1.14], P = 0.19). This work suggests intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy did not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population. (Funded by National Science and Technology Major Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657444).

title: [Right aortic arch with a true bicarotid trunk and aberrant left subclavian artery in an adult: Value of CT angiography].
abstract: We report a rare right aortic arch variant detected during neurovascular assessment in a 48-year-old woman. Arch-to-vertex computed tomography angiography showed three consecutive branches: a true bicarotid trunk dividing into both common carotid arteries, a separate right subclavian artery, and an aberrant left subclavian artery with a retroesophageal course. Neither a Kommerell diverticulum nor aortic dissection was identified. Focused questioning disclosed chronic dysphagia, without definitive evidence of vascular esophageal compression. No causal relationship with the presenting stroke could be established. This case underscores the value of multiplanar and three-dimensional imaging in distinguishing a true bicarotid trunk from a common brachiocephalic-carotid origin, identifying aberrant subclavian anatomy, and informing cardiovascular and neuroendovascular procedural planning.

title: Concurrent Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor and Factor Xa Inhibitor Use Is Associated With Increased Transfusion and Periprosthetic Joint Infection After Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty Despite Tranexamic Acid.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) impair platelet function, and concurrent SSRI and oral anticoagulant use has been associated with major bleeding in medical populations. We evaluated whether preoperative concurrent SSRI and factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor use was associated with higher transfusion and complication rates compared with use of either medication alone after primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) when tranexamic acid (TXA) use was standard. METHODS: Adult patients who underwent primary THA and received TXA on the day of surgery were identified in a large electronic health records database. The SSRI-only, FXa-only, and concurrent-use cohorts were independently 1:1 propensity-score matched to controls who did not have either exposure. The concurrent-use cohort was also matched directly to the SSRI-only and FXa-only cohorts. The primary outcome was allogeneic red blood cell transfusion. The secondary outcomes were surgical site infection (SSI), venous thromboembolism (VTE), periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), and revision THA at 30, 90, and 365 days. RESULTS: Compared with matched controls, SSRI-only patients had significantly higher transfusion, PJI, and revision THA rates at all timepoints (30-day transfusion risk ratio [RR] 1.44; 1-year PJI, RR 1.48; 1-year revision, RR 1.84; all P < 0.001). The FXa-only patients did not have higher transfusion or complication rates. Compared with SSRI-only patients, concurrent use was not associated with significantly different rates of any outcome at any timepoint. Compared with FXa-only use, concurrent use was associated with higher transfusion rates at all timepoints and higher PJI and revision rates at 90 days and one year (RR 1.54 to 2.12; all P ≤ 0.026). CONCLUSION: Preoperative SSRI use was associated with higher transfusion, PJI, and revision THA rates. Concurrent use exceeded FXa-only rates, but not SSRI-only rates, suggesting that SSRI use may be the more important perioperative risk marker. The use of SSRIs should be recognized during preoperative bleeding-risk assessment.

METHODS: Adult patients who underwent primary THA and received TXA on the day of surgery were identified in a large electronic health records database.

title: VOLUME ADJUSTED CALCIUM ANALYSIS OF AORTOILIAC ATHEROSCLEROSIS AS A PREDICTOR OF AMPUTATION FREE SURVIVAL.
abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Pre-operative cross-sectional imaging guides surgical planning in vascular surgery. Despite the relationship between atherosclerotic burden and surgical success, no studies have adjusted atherosclerotic burden according to lumen volume. Given variability in vessel diameter and significance of aortoiliac disease, we developed a volume-adjusted calcium score (VACS) and evaluated its association with patient outcomes. METHODS: This single-institution retrospective study included 187 patients over nine years who underwent peripheral vascular intervention. Using TeraRecon, calcium and patent lumen volumes were quantified along a contiguous aorto-iliac segment totaling 10 cm generating a VACS. An intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) assessed inter-rater reliability. Patients were stratified into two groups. Primary outcomes were death at one year and amputation-free survival. Secondary outcomes were re-interventions and number of arteries treated. RESULTS: Intervention type did not differ between the two groups. Patients with higher VACS were more likely older, have CHF, COPD, or hypertension. Patient in the higher VACS group had greater number of arteries treated, subsequent vascular interventions, and one-year all-cause mortality. A Cox-regression model demonstrated a VACSgreater than 0.33 was independently associated with decreased amputation-free survival at one year (HR 2.24, p=0.019). CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing intervention for aortoiliac occlusive disease, higher VACS was independently associated with worse one-year amputation free survival. Incorporating patent lumen volume into VACS appears to capture a systemic atherosclerotic burden not fully reflected by traditional lesion-specific assessments.

Despite the relationship between atherosclerotic burden and surgical success, no studies have adjusted atherosclerotic burden according to lumen volume. Given variability in vessel diameter and significance of aortoiliac disease, we developed a volume-adjusted calcium score (VACS) and evaluated its association with patient outcomes.

title: Prevalence of concomitant aneurysms in patients with thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms who underwent Fenestrated/Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair (F-BEVAR).
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of synchronous ascending aortic and peripheral arterial aneurysms in patients with Crawford extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA) undergoing fenestrated/branched endovascular aneurysm repair (F/BEVAR). METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective review of prospectively collected data from patients with Crawford extent I-IV TAAA treated with F/BEVAR under a physician-sponsored investigational device exemption. The preoperative CTA obtained for device planning was used to measure the ascending aorta and bilateral common iliac (CIA), hypogastric (HA), and common femoral (CFA) arteries using centerline reconstruction. Bilateral popliteal artery (PA) diameters were obtained from preoperative arterial duplex imaging. An aneurysm was defined as a vessel diameter >50% greater than the expected normal diameter for that arterial bed, using references available from literature. Multivariable logistic regression included sex, obesity, race/ethnicity, TAAA diameter ≥7 cm, and prior aortic dissection. A sensitivity analysis was performed after excluding patients with prior aortic dissection. RESULTS: Among 249 patients (mean age, 70.8±8.6 years; 40.2% women), 177 (71.1%) had at least one concomitant aneurysm. Race/ethnicity was 75.1% NH-White, 21.7% NH-Black, 0.8% Hispanic, and 2.4% Other. Among evaluable patients, aneurysm prevalence was 12.0% in the ascending aorta (29/242), 62.8% in the CIA (140/223), 42.1% in the HA (98/233), 22.2% in the PA (51/230), and 9.6% in the CFA (22/228). On multivariable analysis, CIA aneurysm was associated with obesity, non-White race/ethnicity, and TAAA diameter ≥7 cm; HA aneurysm with male sex, obesity, and prior dissection; CFA aneurysm with male sex; PA aneurysm with male sex and prior dissection; and ascending aortic aneurysm with TAAA diameter ≥7 cm and prior dissection. After exclusion of 46 patients with prior dissection, concomitant aneurysms remained a common occurrence. CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant aneurysms are common in patients undergoing F/BEVAR for Crawford extent I-IV TAAA. Several associations remained significant after multivariable adjustment. These findings should be interpreted in the context of a single-center referral population, variable arterial-bed denominators, possible diffuse arteriomegaly, and residual confounding. The prevalence of PA aneurysm supports further evaluation of selective popliteal assessment; however, this study does not support a universal screening recommendation or establish an effect on management, outcomes, or cost.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of synchronous ascending aortic and peripheral arterial aneurysms in patients with Crawford extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA) undergoing fenestrated/branched endovascular aneurysm repair (F/BEVAR). METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective review of prospectively collected data from patients with Crawford extent I-IV TAAA treated with F/BEVAR under a physician-sponsored investigational device exemption. The preoperative CTA obtained for device planning was used to measure the ascending aorta and bilateral common iliac (CIA), hypogastric (HA), and common femoral (CFA) arteries using centerline reconstruction.

title: Repair durability following fenestrated versus chimney endovascular repair for elective juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare repair durability following elective fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) and chimney endovascular aneurysm repair (ChEVAR) for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms using complementary procedural, imaging, and clinical outcome measures. METHODS: 2 A retrospective multicenter cohort study was performed across five high-volume aortic referral centers. Consecutive patients undergoing elective FEVAR or ChEVAR for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms were included. Baseline characteristics, technical success, endoleaks, secondary aortic intervention, aneurysm sac remodeling, and target vessel patency were compared. Repair durability was assessed by integrating proximal seal integrity, longitudinal aneurysm sac remodeling, and freedom from secondary aortic intervention. Continuous variables were compared using Student's t test or the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using χor Fisher's exact tests. Statistical significance was defined as P < .05. RESULTS: A total of 130 patients underwent elective repair, including 77 treated with FEVAR and 53 with ChEVAR. Baseline demographic characteristics, aneurysm diameter, and duration of follow-up were similar between groups. Technical success was comparable (98.7% vs 98.1%; P = .76), and target vessel patency exceeded 95% in both cohorts (P = .38). Type Ia endoleak occurred less frequently following FEVAR than ChEVAR (1.3% vs 22.6%; P < .001), with a lower incidence of all Type I endoleaks (Types Ia, Ib, and Ic) (7.8% vs 26.4%; P = .006). Secondary aortic intervention was also less common following FEVAR (10.4% vs 30.2%; P = .006). Progressive aneurysm sac regression was observed following FEVAR, with a mean reduction of 11 mm at 24 months, whereas ChEVAR demonstrated limited early regression followed by late sac re-expansion, resulting in an overall 2-mm reduction. Mean aneurysm sac diameter was significantly smaller following FEVAR compared with ChEVAR at both 12 months (55 vs 59 mm; P = .01) and 24 months (51 vs 63 mm; P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Elective FEVAR and ChEVAR achieved similarly high technical success and target vessel patency for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms. During mid-term follow-up, FEVAR was associated with lower rates of proximal attachment-site failure, greater aneurysm sac regression, and fewer secondary aortic interventions. These concordant procedural, imaging, and clinical outcomes suggest that integrated longitudinal assessment provides a more comprehensive evaluation of repair durability following complex endovascular aneurysm repair than technical success alone.

METHODS: 2 A retrospective multicenter cohort study was performed across five high-volume aortic referral centers. Consecutive patients undergoing elective FEVAR or ChEVAR for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms were included.

title: Risk Prediction With a Type Ia-Oriented Proximal Neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score After EVAR.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We developed an exploratory Type Ia-oriented proximal neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score (Type Ia-ASGS) and assessed its association with postoperative type Ia endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). METHODS: We analyzed 304 elective standard EVAR patients treated during 2016-April 2024 with an Ankura endograft (Lifetech). Neck measurements were proximal diameter (A), distal diameter (B), and centerline length (C). The score assigned 1 point each for C ≤15 mm, max(A, B) >28 mm, and B - A ≥3 mm, and 2 points each for angulation >60° and calcification. The theoretical range was 0-7; weights reflected observed univariable associations. RESULTS: Mean clinical and imaging follow-up was 27.6 ± 3.2 months, with final follow-up in June 2026. Type Ia endoleak occurred in 14/304 patients (4.6%). Observed event proportions were 1.2%, 2.8%, and 28.1% in exploratory low (0-1), intermediate (2-3), and high (≥4) score categories (p < 0.001). Each point was associated with greater odds of type Ia endoleak (odds ratio, 2.78; 95% confidence interval, 1.80-4.29). Apparent area under the curve was 0.859 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.750-0.943). Individual event and censoring dates were unavailable for time-to-event analysis. CONCLUSIONS: The Type Ia-ASGS was associated with postoperative type Ia endoleak in this derivation cohort. Its heuristic weights and exploratory categories require independent validation before clinical use.

METHODS: We analyzed 304 elective standard EVAR patients treated during 2016-April 2024 with an Ankura endograft (Lifetech). Neck measurements were proximal diameter (A), distal diameter (B), and centerline length (C).

title: Managing Abnormal Uterine Bleeding During Anticoagulant Therapy in Clinical Practice.
abstract: Anticoagulant therapies, including heparins, vitamin K antagonists, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) such as rivaroxaban, apixaban and dabigatran, are crucial for the treatment and the prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE). While DOACs offer improved safety profiles, their use, espe-cially in women of reproductive age, increases the risk of abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), partic-ularly heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB). HMB, defined as blood loss exceeding 80 mL per cycle or causing significant life disruption, is associated with reduced quality of life and substantial economic costs. Women on anticoagulants report higher incidences of HMB, often requiring adjustments in therapy or additional interventions. Management strategies include the referral for a gynecological consultation, the adjustment of hormonal therapy and anticoagulant treatment, the administration of tranexamic acid, and the treatment of iron deficiency. The review underscores the importance of a comprehensive, personalized approach to managing AUB in women on anticoagulants to optimize both anticoagulation effectiveness and patient quality of life.

title: Temporal trend and geographic variation in anticoagulation of patients hospitalized with acute pulmonary embolism: the RIETE registry 2013-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: A recent U.S. study of initial anticoagulation in adults with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring hospitalization found intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) use exceeded 50%. Guidelines, however, recommend low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) over UFH for most patients requiring parenteral anticoagulation. Use patterns in other geographic regions are unclear. METHODS: We analyzed data from RIETE, a prospective multinational registry of consecutive patients with venous thromboembolism. We included adults hospitalized for acute PE from 2013 through 2024 in 273 hospitals across 31 countries. We assessed temporal trend and regional variation in initial anticoagulation. Using multivariable regression, we identified variables independently associated with UFH. RESULTS: Among 36,210 adults, 83.2% received subcutaneous LMWH, 7.1% UFH, and 6.8% direct oral anticoagulants. LMWH use decreased slightly from 2013 to 2024 (85.8% to 79.2%; unadjusted), while UFH increased (8.9% to 10.4%). Wide geographic variation was observed in overall use of LMWH (37%--95%) and UFH (2%--39%). When adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates, increased weight, recent surgery, recent major bleeding, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, severe renal dysfunction, abnormal vital signs, and early reperfusion therapy were positively associated, whereas age >80 years, active cancer, chronic lung disease, prior ischemic stroke, and year were negatively associated with UFH. Compared with Spanish hospitals, hospitals in other European countries, the United States, and Asia were independently associated with UFH use. CONCLUSIONS: Results highlight opportunities for some geographic regions to align anticoagulation practices more closely with evidence-based guidelines recommending LMWH as the preferred parenteral agent in most patients with PE requiring hospitalization.
