title: Descending aortic replacement after frozen elephant trunk: graft clamping and true-lumen anastomosis.
abstract: Second-stage descending aortic replacement after arch replacement with a frozen elephant trunk requires proximal control at a site that is often hostile to cross-clamping. The conventional elephant trunk technique was introduced to avoid cross-clamping the vulnerable proximal aorta; the previously implanted graft, left hanging in the descending aorta, is grasped and clamped directly, and the new graft is sutured to it. This video tutorial demonstrates the manoeuvre in the current era of the frozen, stented elephant trunk. In a patient with a frozen elephant trunk, computed tomography confirmed complete circumferential thrombosis of the false lumen around the stented graft. Through a left thoracotomy the distal aorta was clamped, and the completely thrombosed false lumen was opened without a proximal cross-clamp. The previously implanted stented graft was exposed and clamped directly, providing proximal control without dissecting or cross-clamping the densely adherent native aorta and without damaging the stent. The new graft was anastomosed proximally to the unstented distal cuff, and distally to the true lumen only, avoiding leak into the false lumen and limiting late aortic enlargement. The imaging that makes the approach safe, the step-by-step conduct, and the pitfall of identifying the graft within the walled-off true lumen are described.

title: Carotid artery bypass and supraclavicular subclavian artery cannulation for cerebral malperfusion in aortic dissection.
abstract: Cerebral malperfusion complicating acute aortic dissection type A is a serious complication associated with markedly increased morbidity, permanent neurological deficit, and mortality. Early cannulation and extended replacement of occluded or dissected carotid arteries is an effective yet underused strategy for improving outcomes in such patients. We present a case of acute aortic dissection type A extending from the aortic root to the right common femoral artery, complicated by an occluded right common carotid artery and a dissected left common carotid artery. The patient was successfully treated with an extensive repair comprising David's procedure, arch repair, frozen elephant trunk implantation, bilateral extended carotid artery bypass and extended left subclavian artery bypass.

title: Design and Navigation of Magnetic Micro/Nanorobotic Swarms in Complex Endovascular Networks: From Swarm Dynamics to Targeted Therapeutics.
abstract: The human vascular network, with its intricate geometries and diverse flow regimes, represents a formidable frontier for microrobotic navigation. While isolated microrobots frequently reach their functional ceiling due to weak signal contrast, low payload capacity, and susceptibility to hydrodynamic drag, the emergence of programmable micro/nanorobotic swarms offers a strategy to overcome these limitations in vascular intervention. By harnessing collective intelligence and programmable behavior, these swarms enhance positional stability, detectability in hard-to-reach circulatory environments, and versatility across endovascular tasks. This review provides a critical synthesis of magnetic actuation as an effective strategy for governing these collectives, owing to its deep-tissue penetration and precise spatiotemporal control. An integrated design framework bridges fundamental physical principles and practical swarm-engineering strategies with their translational potential in endovascular medicine, emphasizing relationships among collective structure, swarm dynamics, and navigation. These collective structures facilitate amplified imaging signals, high local therapeutic payloads, and task-specific interventions, enabling robust navigation through tortuous vascular networks. By evaluating the transition from laboratory prototypes toward clinical applications, this work highlights the integrated advances required to overcome biosafety and scalability hurdles. Ultimately, programmable magnetic swarms emerge as a versatile platform with considerable potential for high-precision, minimally invasive endovascular medicine.

title: Comparative cardiovascular outcomes of IL-6 inhibitors versus rituximab in rheumatoid arthritis: a claims-based observational study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Interleukin-6 receptor inhibitors (IL-6i), tocilizumab and sarilumab, are FDA-approved therapies for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Beyond their efficacy in controlling systemic inflammation, growing evidence suggests that IL-6 inhibition may confer cardioprotective effects. This study investigates the long-term cardiovascular outcomes associated with IL-6i in RA patients, comparing IL-6 inhibitors with rituximab and evaluating differences between individual IL-6 inhibitor agents. METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study using the TriNetX Linked Network (2010-2025) including adults with RA initiating an IL-6 inhibitor or rituximab and ≥ 2 prescriptions for a drug of interest ≥ 6 months apart. Comparisons were as follows: (1) IL-6 inhibitors (sarilumab, tocilizumab) versus rituximab, and (2) tocilizumab versus sarilumab. Patients receiving both IL-6 inhibitors simultaneously or a non-FDA-approved IL-6 blocker (e.g., siltuximab) were excluded. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, heart failure (HF), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) over 5 years. We calculated propensity scores using demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, inflammatory markers, prior TNFi exposure, systemic glucocorticoid use, and conventional DMARDs, and used scores to match exposed individuals 1:1 with comparators. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality and cardiovascular outcomes individually. All analyses were conducted using the TriNetX platform. RESULTS: After matching, 4288 RA patients per group were included for IL-6i versus rituximab and 605 per group for sarilumab versus tocilizumab. Compared to rituximab, IL-6i was associated with lower hazards of mortality (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.55-0.82), MACE (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.64-0.85), and HF risk (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.69-0.94), with no significant difference in MI, stroke, or VTE. Amongst IL-6 inhibitors, sarilumab was associated with lower hazards of all-cause mortality compared to tocilizumab (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.29-0.94), but no significant differences were identified for other cardiovascular outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with RA, IL-6i use was associated with lower rates of all-cause mortality, MACE, and heart failure compared to rituximab, while risks of stroke, MI, and VTE were similar. A lower risk of all-cause mortality was observed with sarilumab compared to tocilizumab. These findings support a potential survival and cardiovascular benefit of IL-6i and highlight the need for larger studies to further distinguish the cardiovascular outcomes with IL-6i agents. Such evidence could inform personalized treatment decisions based on cardiovascular risk factors. Key Points • This study provides long-term real-world evidence that IL-6 inhibitors may offer superior cardiovascular outcomes compared with rituximab in RA patients previously managed with TNFi, an important evidence gap in biologic choice after TNFi failure. • This study directly compares cardiovascular outcomes between sarilumab and tocilizumab, identifying a potential lower myocardial infarction risk with sarilumab.

title: Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke - New Directions.
abstract: In the past 5 years, substantial changes have been made in the use of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Integrating IVT with endovascular thrombectomy, which improves outcomes in patients with stroke due to large cerebral vessel occlusion, has been a particular challenge. This review discusses the underlying vascular targets for IVT and thrombectomy, the increasing use of tenecteplase instead of alteplase, broadening indications for the use of IVT, and ancillary drugs and dosing methods that may augment the success of IVT.

title: Age Adjustment of the Combined Early Ischemic Change and Collateral Extent Score for Outcomes after Endovascular Therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Both age and ischemic core volume are strong predictors of outcomes after endovascular therapy. We previously developed and reported the ASPECTS and the multiphase CTA collateral extent (mCTA-ACE) score, which combines early ischemic changes on NCCT and the extent of leptomeningeal filling on multiphase CTA, and showed that it was associated with outcomes after endovascular therapy (EVT). The aim of this study was to refine the mCTA-ACE score through age adjustment and external validation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a post hoc analysis of EVT-treated patients from the Alteplase Compared with Tenecteplase (AcT) trial. The mCTA-ACE score was calculated as the baseline ASPECTS plus a 10-point multiphase CTA (mCTA) collateral score, corresponding to ASPECTS regions M2-M6 graded as poor (0), moderate (1), or normal (2). From the mixed-effect logistic regression for mRS ≤2 at 90-120 days, the relative regression coefficient of age to mCTA-ACE score was used to derive the age-adjusted mCTA-ACE score. The prediction ability of age-adjusted mCTA-ACE score was validated in a reduced model from the Precise and Rapid Assessment of Collaterals Using Multi-Phase CTA in the Triage of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke for IA Therapy (PRove-IT) trial. RESULTS: P P n Of 1577 patients in the intention-to-treat population in the AcT trial, 368 who underwent EVT therapy and had assessable imaging were included (179 men, median age 73 years). In multivariable analysis, mCTA-ACE score and age were independently associated with mRS ≤2 (coefficients: 0.15 and -0.05, respectively); then the age-adjusted mCTA-ACE score was derived as mCTA-ACE score - age/3. The age-adjusted score showed superior predictive performance compared with the original mCTA-ACE score for mRS ≤2 (C-statistic 0.72 vs 0.65;< .01). The C-statistics of age-adjusted and original mCTA-ACE scores for mRS ≤2 were 0.79 and 0.68, respectively (< .01; DeLong test) in the PRove-IT population who underwent endovascular therapy (=261; 124 men, median age 73 years). CONCLUSIONS: An age-adjustment of the mCTA-ACE score may provide a more individualized prediction of functional outcomes after endovascular therapy, which helps patient selection, particularly in settings with limited access to endovascular therapy.

title: Multifocal Cutaneous Angiosarcoma of the Lower Limbs Presenting With Severe Tumour-Related Haemorrhage: A Case Report.
abstract: Cutaneous angiosarcoma (CAS) is a rare and highly aggressive vascular tumour of endothelial origin with a poor prognosis. It can present with atypical skin lesions, making early diagnosis challenging. We present a case of a man in his late 80s who presented with a two-year history of weight loss, fatigue, iron-deficiency anaemia, and persistently elevated inflammatory markers. He subsequently developed rapidly progressive, multifocal violaceous nodules affecting both lower limbs. Initial differential diagnoses included melanocytic and nodular vasculitis. Skin biopsy confirmed high-grade CAS. The lesions progressed to fungation with recurrent bleeding, resulting in severe symptomatic anaemia requiring repeated blood transfusions. Management was complicated by his background of a persistent endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) of a large abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). This case highlights the importance of considering CAS in rapidly evolving, atypically located skin lesions. Early diagnosis and patient-centred multidisciplinary management are essential, particularly when advanced disease and significant comorbidities limit therapeutic options.

title: Aspirin is safe and effective for prevention of deep vein thrombosis following acetabular fracture surgery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with acetabular fractures are at significant risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet the optimal chemoprophylactic agent remains undefined. Emerging evidence from elective arthroplasty and general orthopaedic trauma populations suggests that aspirin (ASA) may be a safe and effective alternative to traditional anticoagulants. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ASA compared to other anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention following acetabular fracture surgery. METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using a global, web-based health research network that provides on-demand access to de-identified, real-world data from electronic health records and claims. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent surgical treatment for acetabular fractures between January 2014 and December 2025 and received VTE prophylaxis within 14 days of surgery were identified. Patients were stratified into ASA (n = 1189) and other anticoagulant (n = 5478) cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to balance baseline characteristics, yielding 1174 patients per cohort. Rates and odds of DVT, emergency department (ED) visits, deep infection, stroke, and readmission were assessed at 14-, 30-, and 90-day postoperative intervals. Temporal trends in VTE prophylaxis utilization were also analyzed. RESULTS: Compared to other anticoagulants, ASA was associated with significantly lower odds of DVT at 14 days (1.11% vs. 2.22%; odds ratio [OR]: 0.494; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.253-0.967; P = 0.036), 30 days (1.45% vs. 2.73%; OR: 0.524; 95% CI: 0.290-0.950; P = 0.030), and 90 days (2.56% vs. 4.34%; OR: 0.577; 95% CI: 0.365-0.913; P = 0.018). ASA was also associated with significantly lower odds of ED visits at 90 days (OR: 0.741; 95% CI: 0.570-0.963; P = 0.024). There were no significant differences in deep infection, stroke, or readmission rates. ASA utilization increased from 7.2% in 2014-39.5% in 2025. CONCLUSIONS: ASA is safe and effective for DVT prevention following acetabular fracture surgery and is associated with fewer ED visits compared to other anticoagulants. These findings support the growing adoption of ASA as a VTE prophylactic agent in the acetabular fracture population.

The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ASA compared to other anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention following acetabular fracture surgery.

title: Development and Usability Evaluation of a Virtual Learning Environment for Training Nursing Technicians in Arteriovenous Fistula Cannulation.
abstract: In Brazil, where approximately 140,000 patients depend on hemodialysis, virtual learning environments (VLEs) represent a promising educational technology for training nursing technicians. Although VLEs are innovative, research on the development and usability of platforms specifically for arteriovenous fistula (AVF) cannulation training remains scarce. This study aimed to develop and evaluate the usability of a VLE, "Venocurso," for AVF cannulation training. This technological development study followed the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation model and the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning. Content was validated by 14 nursing experts, and navigability was validated by 12 information technology specialists. Usability was then evaluated by 53 nursing technicians using the System Usability Scale. The mean content and navigability validation indices were 0.94 and 0.85, respectively. The mean usability score was 85.6. The VLE's content validity, navigability, and usability were validated. It is a promising tool for AVF cannulation training, and future studies are recommended.

title: Idiopathic Middle Aortic Syndrome Causing Pediatric Resistant Hypertension: Beyond Coarctation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Middle aortic syndrome (MAS) is a rare cause of severe hypertension in children, characterized by segmental narrowing of the distal thoracic and abdominal aorta. Early recognition is essential to prevent irreversible end-organ damage. CASE SUMMARY: A 12-year-old girl presented with resistant hypertension, headache, facial edema, blurred vision, and postprandial abdominal pain. Marked upper-to-lower limb blood pressure discrepancy, with absent femoral pulses. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated long-segment thoracoabdominal aortic narrowing extending to the iliac arteries, consistent with MAS. Because of unfavorable anatomy for endovascular treatment. Thoracoabdominal extra-anatomic aorto-aortic bypass with polytetrafluoroethylene graft was successfully performed. DISCUSSION: This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of idiopathic MAS and demonstrates that individualized management based on vascular anatomy can achieve excellent outcomes. TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Cross-sectional vascular imaging should be considered in children with resistant hypertension and diminished femoral pulses. Open aorto-aortic bypass remains effective when endovascular treatment is unsuitable.

title: Risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism after simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty: A Japanese nationwide medical claims database study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty may offer clinical and economic advantages but raises concerns regarding thromboembolic complications. We compared postoperative outcomes between simultaneous bilateral and unilateral knee arthroplasty. METHODS: Using Japan's nationwide Diagnosis Procedure Combination database, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of hospitalizations for knee arthroplasty between April 2016 and March 2023. Hospitalizations involving simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty were compared with those involving unilateral procedures. Propensity score matching was performed based on age, sex, body mass index, surgical procedure (total or unicompartmental knee arthroplasty), comorbidities, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index. Postoperative complications and perioperative outcomes were evaluated. RESULTS: Among 259,319 eligible hospitalizations, 16,601 matched pairs were identified. In the propensity score-matched cohort, simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty was associated with higher odds of deep vein thrombosis (odds ratio [OR], 1.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.42-1.63) and pulmonary embolism (OR, 2.49; 95% CI, 1.75-3.56) compared with unilateral surgery. In absolute terms, the risk difference was 4.0% (95% CI, 3.3-4.6) for deep vein thrombosis and 0.38% (95% CI, 0.24-0.53) for pulmonary embolism. Simultaneous bilateral procedures were also associated with a modestly longer length of hospital stay and higher perioperative blood transfusion requirements. In contrast, no statistically significant differences were observed for pneumonia, cerebrovascular events, postoperative cognitive dysfunction, surgical site infection, periprosthetic fracture, or in-hospital mortality. CONCLUSION: Simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty is associated with an increased risk of postoperative deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, despite routine postoperative antithrombotic medications. Careful perioperative management is therefore essential when considering simultaneous bilateral procedures, particularly with regard to thromboembolic risk.

We compared postoperative outcomes between simultaneous bilateral and unilateral knee arthroplasty. title: Perioperative Outcomes After Open Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Tissue-Loss Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia in Patients Aged 80 Years or Older: An NSQIP Analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: We compared 30-day outcomes of open bypass versus endovascular intervention in patients aged ≥80 years with tissue-loss chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), in whom trial evidence from younger populations may not apply. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing infrainguinal revascularization for tissue-loss CLTI in the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program vascular-targeted modules (2014-2024) were classified as open bypass with single-segment saphenous vein (OPEN-GSV) or alternative conduit (OPEN-Other), or endovascular intervention (ENDO). Doubly-robust inverse-probability weighting with regression adjustment estimated 30-day risks of the co-primary outcomes, major adverse limb events (MALE) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: The cohort comprised 4,415 patients (2,573 ENDO; 1,124 OPEN-GSV; 718 OPEN-Other). Adjusted MACE risk was 2.9% after ENDO versus 6.5% after OPEN-GSV (risk ratio [RR] 0.44, 95% CI 0.29-0.61) and 6.0% after OPEN-Other (RR 0.48, 0.33-0.79). MALE did not differ significantly (RR 0.85 and 0.86), with CIs spanning clinically important differences in both directions. Serious complication, any complication, and non-home discharge were lower after ENDO (RR 0.41-0.56); major amputation did not differ. Mortality was lower after ENDO than OPEN-GSV (4.7% vs 6.9%; RR 0.68) but not OPEN-Other (RR 0.87). CONCLUSIONS: In this population, endovascular intervention was associated with substantially lower 30-day cardiovascular events and systemic morbidity than open bypass, with no significant difference - though not established equivalence - in early limb outcomes. These findings support weighing perioperative physiologic risk in individualized treatment selection; data beyond 30 days are needed to address durability and limb salvage.

title: A National Consultant Information Programme Data Analysis of Deep Venous Interventions in England.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to characterise contemporary deep venous interventions (DVIs) performed within the English National Health Service (NHS), describing procedural mix, patient heterogeneity, anatomic distribution, and short and midterm outcomes. METHODS: National data on DVIs performed between 1 June 2020 and 31 May 2023 were extracted from the National Consultant Information Programme. Percutaneous transluminal venous procedures (PTVs) and venous thrombolysis were identified using pre-defined procedural and diagnostic code hierarchies. All cases underwent structured patient level validation to ensure concordance between indication, treated venous anatomy, and procedural intent. The primary outcomes were ninety day and one year mortality. Secondary outcomes included procedural volume variation. Re-interventions were recorded descriptively. RESULTS: In total, 2 339 DVIs were performed, of which 1 617 PTVs and 604 venous thrombolysis procedures were validated. Patient cohorts were heterogeneous, most commonly chronic kidney disease (CKD) (41.8%), chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) (16.0%), and venous compression syndromes (14.0%). Anatomic distribution differed markedly by indication: CKD procedures predominantly involved upper limb and central veins, whereas CVI and venous compression were overwhelmingly confined to the lower limbs and iliocaval system. Among 650 patients with primary lower limb venous disease (CVI, venous thrombosis, or venous compression), 76.3% underwent iliac or inferior vena cava interventions. Overall mortality varied substantially by indication, being highest in patients with malignant neoplasms and lowest in primary lower limb venous disease. Thrombolysis was most frequently performed for lower extremity venous thrombosis and was associated with low short and midterm mortality in this group. CONCLUSION: This service level analysis of DVIs in England demonstrates distinct clinical populations with marked differences in anatomy, indication, and outcomes that vary substantially by indication and comorbidity. Mortality was lowest in elective primary lower limb venous disease and highest in patients with advanced systemic illness such as malignancy and renal disease. Future work should focus on indication specific venous registries and risk adjusted outcomes to aid benchmarking, service level organisation, and patient care.

title: Propensity Score Matched Analysis of Outcomes of Conservative and Invasive Management of Patients with Chronic Limb Threatening Ischaemia: The PROCLION Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Current guidelines recommend revascularisation for patients with chronic limb threatening ischaemia (CLTI). However, revascularisation may be burdensome in these frail patients. The objective of this study was to compare the clinical and patient reported outcomes in patients with CLTI treated with conservative best supportive care versus primary invasive endovascular and/or surgical revascularisation. METHODS: This was a multicentre prospective cohort study in the Netherlands. Propensity score matching was used to create similar groups based on known factors influencing the odds of undergoing revascularisation. Twelve month amputation free survival (AFS), major amputation rates, mortality, and patient reported outcomes after primary conservative treatment were compared with primary invasive treatment (intention to treat; ITT). Outcomes after invasive treatment at any time were compared with definitive conservative treatment (per protocol; PP). RESULTS: A total of 365 patients with CLTI were included in 18 centres. In the ITT analysis, patients were matched 1 : 1, resulting in two groups of 121 patients. Twelve month AFS was 73.0% for patients after conservative treatment and 72.1% after invasive treatment (risk difference [RD] -0.9%, 95% confidence interval [CI] -10.2 - 8.4%). There were no significant differences in amputation and mortality rates. In the PP analysis, patients were matched 1 : 2, with 51 in the conservative group and 102 in the invasive group. Again, no significant differences were found for AFS, amputation rate, and mortality. Patient reported outcomes improved after 1 year in both groups (VascuQoL: ITT conservative group from 14 to 16.2, and invasive group from 13.8 to 16.5), but no significant differences were found in ITT or PP comparisons. CONCLUSION: The current study suggests that the 12 month clinical outcomes of primary conservative and invasive treatment for CLTI are similar. Conservative management may therefore be a viable first choice treatment option in selected patients with CLTI.

title: Prediction models for venous thromboembolism in pediatric patients: A protocol for systematic review and critical appraisal.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) in children is a severe disease with high mortality rates. It is also gradually recognized as a major source of morbidity in hospitalized children, leading to increased length of hospital stay, higher mortality, and increased costs. The majority of pediatric subjects with VTE present inherited or acquired risk factors,such as the use of a central venous catheter (CVC), which accounts for more than more than 90% of neonatal VTE and 50% of pediatric VTE. Clinical studies on predictive models for VTE in children have shown inconsistent results. This systematic review aims to evaluate published prediction models for pediatric VTE, analyzing their characteristics, predictors, efficacy, and the methodological quality and applicability. The protocol has been prepared using the Preferred Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) guidelines. The systematic review protocol for VTE prediction in pediatric patients has been registered on PROSPERO (PROSPERO 2025CRD420251231316. Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/vi-ew/CRD420251231316.) A comprehensive search across five major databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang) will be conducted for studies on prediction models of VTE among pediatric patients. Two researchers will independently screen literature, extract data, and evaluate the bias risk and applicability of included studies using prediction modelling study tools. This systematic review will provide critical insights into the efficacy and quality of reporting of the VTE model in pediatric patients. This will guide clinical physicians in selecting the most appropriate VTE prediction model and inform future research endeavors in pediatric VTE prediction.

title: SEQuential tUnneled Catheters and Infective Events in haemodiaLysis: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study (SEQUEL Study).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tunnelled-cuffed catheters (TCCs) are widely used for haemodialysis access when permanent vascular access is unavailable. Internal jugular vein (IJV) placement is guideline-preferred, but femoral vein (FV) catheters are frequently used when upper venous access is limited. Whether femoral access confers a higher infection risk than catheter sequence number remains unclear. This study evaluated these two competing determinants of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI). METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included all TCC insertions at a tertiary nephrology unit between January 2016 and December 2021. The primary analysis examined CRBSI incidence per 1000 catheter-days stratified by catheter sequence number (first, second, third+ insertion per patient). Secondary analyses compared femoral versus internal jugular TCCs overall and within sequence strata. A registry-index cohort (patients with no documented prior TCC before January 2016, n = 135) was used to reduce, though not eliminate, sequence-related confounding in the site comparison; given only 24 CRBSI events, this analysis is exploratory and a clinically meaningful site difference cannot be excluded. Kaplan-Meier methods with log-rank testing were used for time-to-event outcomes. A cluster-robust marginal Cox model was used to account for repeated catheter insertions within patients, adjusting for sequence number, insertion site, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter. RESULTS: Among 626 TCC insertions in 339 patients (389 FV, 237 IJV), contributing 98,727 catheter-days, CRBSI incidence escalated with catheter sequence: 1.17 per 1000 catheter-days for first insertions, rising to 1.98 for second and 2.49 for third-or-more insertions. Notably, by the second insertion, CRBSI rates were similar between FV and IJV access (31.7% each). In the index cohort (n = 135; FV = 95, IJV = 40), CRBSI-free survival did not differ significantly between sites (log-rank p = 0.340), nor did catheter survival (p = 0.950) or patient survival (p = 0.487). In the all-TCC cohort, after adjustment for catheter sequence number, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter using a cluster-robust marginal Cox model, femoral access remained associated with a higher, though attenuated, CRBSI hazard after adjustment for the measured covariates (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.02-2.01; p = 0.039), indicating a modest residual site hazard beyond the sequence effect. CONCLUSIONS: Repeated catheterization was independently associated with increasing CRBSI risk, and catheter sequence number was the strongest predictor in the fully adjusted model. The femoral site effect was substantially attenuated after adjustment for sequence and was not statistically significant in the registry-index cohort analysis, though the wide confidence intervals preclude an equivalence interpretation. IJV access remains preferred; when IJV is unavailable, femoral TCC placement may be an acceptable alternative from an infection-risk perspective, but this must be weighed against thrombotic and limb complications, including deep vein thrombosis, which were not systematically ascertained in this study. Residual confounding cannot be excluded in this single-center retrospective study.

Internal jugular vein (IJV) placement is guideline-preferred, but femoral vein (FV) catheters are frequently used when upper venous access is limited. Whether femoral access confers a higher infection risk than catheter sequence number remains unclear.

title: Middle meningeal artery embolization in chronic subdural hematoma: A real-world multicenter italian experience.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate technical feasibility, short-term radiological outcomes, subsequent surgical intervention, and complications of middle meningeal artery (MMA) embolization for chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH), distinguishing primary embolization from embolization after surgery. METHODS: This retrospective study included 228 consecutive patients undergoing attempted MMA embolization at three Italian referral centers between January 2019 and November 2024. Technical success was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included radiological success, defined as residual hematoma thickness ≤ 6 mm on CT at 60-90 days, subsequent surgical evacuation, and procedure-related complications. Subgroup comparisons were exploratory and used available-case data. RESULTS: Primary embolization was performed in 115 patients and embolization after surgery in 113. Technical success was achieved in 223/228 patients (97.8%). Follow-up CT was available in 188/228 patients (82.5%). Median residual hematoma thickness was 4 mm (interquartile range, 0-8), without a significant difference between groups (p = 0.372). Radiological success occurred in 132/188 patients (70.2%): 57/88 (64.8%) after primary embolization and 75/100 (75.0%) after surgery (p = 0.151). Complications occurred in 7/228 patients (3.1%), including one major ischemic stroke, without a significant between-group difference (p = 0.720). Subsequent surgical evacuation was required in 7/188 patients (3.7%): 5/88 (5.7%) versus 2/100 (2.0%), respectively (p = 0.255). CONCLUSION: MMA embolization demonstrated high technical success, favorable short-term radiological outcomes, and a low rate of subsequent surgical intervention. These findings support its feasibility and potential clinical value in selected patients with CSDH, both as primary treatment and after surgical evacuation. Prospective comparative studies are needed to confirm these observations.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 228 consecutive patients undergoing attempted MMA embolization at three Italian referral centers between January 2019 and November 2024. title: The Coagulation-Immune Axis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Mechanisms, Prognostic Significance, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) develops in a microbe-rich, injury-prone mucosa in which coagulation, inflammation, and tissue repair are closely coupled. Tumor and host cells can activate tissue factor-thrombin signaling, platelets, fibrin turnover, extracellular vesicles, and neutrophil extracellular traps, thereby reshaping myeloid-cell recruitment, cytotoxic immunity, angiogenesis, and invasion. However, local procoagulant biology does not necessarily predict systemic venous thromboembolism. We therefore organize the evidence using a compartmentalized immunothrombosis model that distinguishes intratumoral coagulation-immune remodeling, systemic thrombosis, and treatment-dependent perioperative events. Direct OSCC studies support several components of this network, but much of the evidence linking coagulation to immune escape and treatment response remains preclinical or extrapolated from other tumors. Circulating D-dimer, fibrinogen, platelet indices, and inflammatory ratios show prognostic associations, yet their incremental value beyond established clinicopathologic factors has not been established. Anticoagulant, antiplatelet, protease-activated receptor, podoplanin-CLEC-2, fibrinolytic, and NET-directed strategies are biologically plausible but should not be used as OSCC treatment without a standard indication or clinical trial. Future studies should pair longitudinal blood measurements with spatial tumor profiling and match interventions to a verified mechanism, anatomical compartment, and safe treatment window.

title: Case report: Severe consequence of unnecessary retention of a TIVAD, phlegmasia cerulea dolens-A case for better stewardship.
abstract: Totally implanted venous access devices (TIVADs) have been used for decades in cancer management. Traditionally placed in the chest wall, they can also be inserted in the upper arm using peripherally inserted central catheter methodologies (PICC-Ports), which are recognized as a safe and comfortable alternative. However, as with all vascular access devices, their safety profile depends on appropriate management, including timely removal. We report a case of Phlegmasia Cerulea Dolens (PCD)-critical venous ischemia-occurring a year after treatment completion due to a retained device. A 59-year-old breast cancer patient presented with arm edema ipsilateral to a PICC-Port, 1 year after chemotherapy had ended. Despite an initial "normal" duplex ultrasound (DUS), her condition worsened into full-blown PCD with cyanosis and loss of pulses. CT angiography revealed massive thrombosis, and standard anticoagulation failed, necessitating interventional radiology for subclavian stenting. While TIVADs are established as a safe method of chemotherapy administration, their safety remains contingent upon adherence to insertion protocols, timely removal, and knowledge of international guidelines. Leaving an inactive device for 12 months post-treatment represents a significant risk. Furthermore, a false-negative initial ultrasound led to a critical diagnostic delay, underscoring that strong clinical suspicion should sometimes override early negative imaging to prevent progression from deep vein thrombosis to PCD. Ultimately, "lost to follow-up" patients with retained TIVADs and non-compliance with international guidelines represent a major iatrogenic risk in cancer management.

title: Hemodialysis access dysfunction caused by heavily calcified subclavian artery chronic total occlusion: Two cases treated with balloon-expandable covered stents.
abstract: Proximal arterial inflow lesions are an underrecognized cause of hemodialysis access dysfunction, particularly in patients with advanced arterial calcification. We report two hemodialysis patients with access dysfunction associated with heavily calcified left subclavian artery chronic total occlusion. Both patients lacked upper-limb claudication or neurological symptoms. Endovascular recanalization was achieved using balloon-expandable covered stents (Viabahn VBX) while preserving the vertebral artery origin. In the first patient, brachial artery flow increased from 55 to 731 mL/min. In the second, flow increased from 275 to 339 mL/min after subclavian revascularization and to 1090 mL/min after subsequent angioplasty of residual fistula stenosis. No procedure-related adverse events occurred, and both accesses remained functional during follow-up. Subclavian artery occlusion should be considered in otherwise unexplained access dysfunction. Balloon-expandable covered stents may provide a useful reconstruction option for heavily calcified proximal inflow lesions.
englishSummary: Proximal arterial inflow lesions are an underrecognized cause of hemodialysis access dysfunction, particularly in patients with advanced arterial calcification. We report two hemodialysis patients with access dysfunction associated with heavily calcified left subclavian artery chronic total occlusion. Both patients lacked upper-limb claudication or neurological symptoms.

title: Two chromosome-scale genomes of wild Aedes aegypti aegypti mosquitoes from North America and South-East Asia.
abstract: The yellow fever mosquito (Aedes aegypti) is the primary vector for diseases such as chikungunya, dengue fever, yellow fever, and Zika fever. These mosquitoes have been designated as two subspecies: Ae. aegypti formosus (Aaf) and Ae. aegypti aegypti (Aaa)-the former being a darker form limited to sub-Saharan Africa and the latter referring to lighter colored individuals found circumglobally in the tropics and sub-tropics. In addition to morphology and distribution, these two sub-species differ in their behavior and ecology-Aaf females generally feed on nonhuman mammals and live in rural and sylvatic areas, whereas Aaa females preferentially feed on humans and are found in human dwellings in urban areas. These characteristics and differences make them species of great medical importance, and the development of resources for understanding their biology has high priority. We recently published a chromosome-scale wild Aaf genome assembly and here we add to this body of resources by presenting two de novo chromosome-scale genome assemblies of wild-caught Aaa from North America and Southeast Asia. Using the Pacific Biosciences HiFi sequencing platform combined with HiC sequencing, we achieved high continuity (N50: >400 Mb; L50: 2) and completeness (BUSCO single-copy: ~97%; diptera set). These assemblies will contribute to further elucidate the global genetic diversity of this major disease vector and uncover the genetic basis of phenotypic differences between the sub-species.

title: Perioperative Management of the Orthopedic Patient Taking Antipsychotics: A Narrative Review.
abstract: PURPOSE: Antipsychotic prescribing continues to rise among older adults, the group most likely to present for orthopedic surgery, and orthopedic surgeons now operate regularly on patients taking these agents. Guidance for managing them around an operation sits largely in the psychiatric, anesthesiology and pharmacologic literature rather than the surgical one. This narrative review gathers the orthopedic-specific evidence and organizes it by whether a finding reflects the medication or the psychiatric illness for which it was prescribed. FINDINGS: Antipsychotic exposure is associated with higher all-cause revision and periprosthetic fracture after total knee arthroplasty, and second-generation exposure raises all-cause and aseptic revision after shoulder arthroplasty independent of psychiatric diagnosis. Venous thromboembolism roughly doubles after primary total knee arthroplasty. Among geriatric hip fracture patients antipsychotics are the only medication class independently linked to in-hospital falls, and preoperative use independently predicts postoperative delirium that prophylaxis does not prevent. Spine, sports medicine and trauma surgery all show worse outcomes in patients carrying a psychiatric diagnosis, yet none of those literatures disentangles the drug from the disorder. Thromboembolism and the shoulder revision signal are the clearest drug-attributable exceptions. Hyperprolactinemia-mediated hypogonadism, metabolic derangement and impaired fracture healing remain plausible but unproven. Nearly all available evidence is retrospective. CONCLUSION: Antipsychotic therapy should continue through the perioperative period unless a specific reason exists to stop it. Abrupt discontinuation risks psychiatric relapse, which is harder to manage than the perioperative risks the drugs themselves carry. Low bone mineral density, poor glycemic control and thromboembolic risk are all worth addressing before surgery, drawing on psychiatry and internal medicine. Antipsychotics are not recommended for delirium prophylaxis. Whether altering therapy improves orthopedic outcomes has not been studied prospectively.

Guidance for managing them around an operation sits largely in the psychiatric, anesthesiology and pharmacologic literature rather than the surgical one. This narrative review gathers the orthopedic-specific evidence and organizes it by whether a finding reflects the medication or the psychiatric illness for which it was prescribed.

title: Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes in patients with severe pelvic ring injury requiring REBOA: A two-center matched cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) is used for life-threatening hemorrhage, but evidence has largely focused on acute outcomes. Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes among survivors treated with REBOA remain poorly characterized. METHODS: This retrospective two-center matched cohort included 98 adults with severe, hemodynamically unstable pelvic ring injuries who survived at least 24 h; hospital survivors required at least 12 months of follow-up. Forty-nine REBOA-treated patients were matched 1:1 to 49 non-REBOA patients by major Young-Burgess category, Injury Severity Score, and age. The primary outcome was functional status among hospital survivors, categorized as good/fair/poor. Deep surgical site infection (SSI) after definitive pelvic fixation was the key secondary outcome, and nonunion was exploratory. Main models used a propensity-score linear predictor based on age, Injury Severity Score, initial systolic blood pressure, and lactate. RESULTS: Seventy-five patients survived hospitalization (30 REBOA; 45 non-REBOA); median follow-up was 19 months. Good/fair/poor outcomes were 16.7%/46.7%/36.7% in REBOA survivors and 51.1%/37.8%/11.1% in non-REBOA survivors. REBOA exposure was associated with worse functional status after adjustment (common odds ratio [cOR], 3.14; 95% CI, 1.11-8.92; P = 0.032). Among 68 definitive-fixation survivors, deep SSI occurred in 44.0% versus 9.3% (adjusted OR, 7.01; 95% CI, 1.88-31.07; P = 0.003); all observed events occurred within 60 days. Nonunion occurred in 26.7% versus 6.7% (adjusted OR, 9.09; 95% CI, 2.00-53.71; P = 0.004). Sensitivity analyses for deep SSI were directionally consistent. CONCLUSIONS: Among hospital survivors, REBOA exposure was associated with poorer long-term functional recovery and a higher burden of deep SSI. Nonunion was more frequent but remained exploratory. These findings characterize a high-risk orthopaedic survivor phenotype but do not establish a direct causal effect of REBOA.

Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes among survivors treated with REBOA remain poorly characterized. METHODS: This retrospective two-center matched cohort included 98 adults with severe, hemodynamically unstable pelvic ring injuries who survived at least 24 h; hospital survivors required at least 12 months of follow-up.

title: Dysphagia as the Initial Manifestation of Anti-HMGCR Antibody-Positive Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibody-positive immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy characterized by progressive proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase levels. Although commonly associated with prior statin exposure, statin-naïve cases and atypical presentations are well described. Patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are also at increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), though data specific to IMNM remain limited. CASE PRESENTATION: An 83-year-old man with brief, remote statin exposure presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness and a three-year history of oropharyngeal dysphagia preceding limb involvement. Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated creatine kinase and transaminases. Anti-HMGCR antibodies were positive, and muscle biopsy confirmed necrotizing myopathy. During evaluation for occult malignancy, bilateral pulmonary emboli were incidentally identified. The patient required high-dose corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil, and intravenous immunoglobulin for refractory disease. With aggressive immunosuppressive therapy and rehabilitation, he demonstrated substantial clinical recovery at 6 months. CONCLUSION: This case highlights oropharyngeal dysphagia as an early and, for a prolonged period, isolated manifestation of anti-HMGCR antibody-positive IMNM; here, it preceded the onset of limb weakness by approximately 3 years. It underscores the importance of comprehensive diagnostic evaluation in patients with unexplained oropharyngeal dysfunction, in whom an inflammatory myopathy may otherwise be overlooked for years. Clinicians should maintain awareness of thrombotic risk in inflammatory myopathies, particularly during active disease. Early recognition and prompt immunosuppressive therapy remain critical to optimize outcomes and prevent irreversible muscle damage.

Although commonly associated with prior statin exposure, statin-naïve cases and atypical presentations are well described. Patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are also at increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), though data specific to IMNM remain limited.

title: Bare-Metal vs Covered Balloon-Expandable Stents for Transplant Renal Artery Stenosis: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
abstract: PURPOSE: To compare short- and long-term outcomes of bare-metal (BMS) vs covered (CS) balloon-expandable stents in transplant renal artery stenosis (TRAS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated patients who underwent elective stent placement for TRAS between 2016 and 2023. Short-term efficacy was assessed by clinical improvement (resolution of resistant hypertension/hypervolemia) and reduction in serum creatinine (sCr) within 14 days post-procedure. Long-term outcomes included Doppler ultrasound parameters - peak systolic velocity (PSV), acceleration time (AT) and resistive index (RI) - and restenosis/occlusion rates requiring or not intervention. Graft survival at the latest follow-up was recorded. RESULTS: P P P P P A total of 40 patients (mean age 58 ± 13 years, 68% male) were treated with BMS (n = 31) or CS (n = 9). Clinical improvement was observed in 71% of BMS and 83% of CS patients ( = 1.00). Median sCr decreased by 26% and 33% in BMS and CS patients, respectively ( = .30). At a median follow-up of 29 months, there were no statistically significant differences between groups in median PSV reduction (47% BMS vs 47% CS; = .44), AT improvement (36% BMS vs 25% CS; = .38) or RI increase (15% BMS vs 33% CS; = .12). In the BMS group, 2 cases of in-stent restenosis occurred (6.5%). In the CS group, 1 stent occlusion occurred (11%), resulting in graft loss. At final follow-up, overall graft survival was 85%. CONCLUSION: In this pilot study, BMS and CS showed no significant differences in TRAS outcomes. Further studies are warranted to better guide stent selection.Clinical ImpactIn transplant renal artery stenosis, balloon-expandable covered stents achieved clinical, biochemical and Doppler outcomes comparable to bare-metal stents, despite being used in more complex, atherosclerotic and longer lesions. This first direct comparison suggests that covered stents may be a reasonable option when heavy calcification, a friable wall or mural thrombus raise concern for embolisation or rupture, while bare-metal stents remain appropriate for most lesions. The single late covered-stent occlusion with graft loss highlights the need for careful platform selection and antiplatelet management. These pilot data should inform adequately powered multicentre registries rather than directly change practice.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated patients who underwent elective stent placement for TRAS between 2016 and 2023. Short-term efficacy was assessed by clinical improvement (resolution of resistant hypertension/hypervolemia) and reduction in serum creatinine (sCr) within 14 days post-procedure.

title: The Lost Kidney: Ultrasound Diagnosis of Adult Bochdalek Hernia With Renal Herniation and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: Adult Bochdalek hernia (BH) with left renal herniation is clinically rare and has an insidious onset, rendering it prone to misdiagnosis. We report a case of a 77-year-old male patient who presented with an abdominal pulsatile mass in the absence of respiratory symptoms. Ultrasonography revealed a giant abdominal aortic aneurysm and additionally identified renal echogenicity on the left side of the heart, with a normally positioned spleen. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated herniation of the left kidney and a portion of the bowel into the thoracic cavity, along with a giant abdominal aortic aneurysm and multiple atherosclerotic ulcers of the iliac arteries. Ultrasonography is valuable for initial screening, while contrast-enhanced CT defines diaphragmatic defect, ectopic-kidney rotational malformation, and elongated renal pedicle, providing critical evidence for definitive diagnosis.

title: A multi-guideline clinical agent for vascular surgery: architecture, implementation, and benchmark evaluation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) published by the European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) span approximately 1100 pages whose simultaneous cross-referencing is impractical at the point of care. Unguarded large language models (LLMs) carry hallucination risk, motivating a guideline-locked design. METHODS: We describe the architecture and development of a context-aware clinical agent encompassing the full ESVS corpus of 14 CPGs. The system extends a validated single-guideline GraphRAG prototype with an LLM-driven Guideline Router, an embedded Context Gate that withholds retrieval when decision-critical parameters are absent, dual-channel retrieval, and GPT-5 synthesis under a mandatory citation template. An automated benchmark assessed the final system on 55 vignettes, scored by 2 blinded LLM judges over 3 runs (330 judgments), with clinician adjudication of every flagged claim. RESULTS: The system stayed within its locked corpus, declined all out-of-scope queries, and achieved 98.4% guideline-routing recall. The Context Gate showed 91.9% specificity and 78.6% sensitivity for underspecified queries, and all 259 cited recommendations were verifiable within the locked corpus. Automated judges flagged an unsupported claim in 18.2% of items under a sensitive screening definition; on adjudication by 2 vascular surgeons, 7.3% of items contained a clinically consequential error, none graded capable of causing harm. Clinical acceptability of complete answers was not scored and is reserved for prospective expert evaluation. CONCLUSION: These results support the feasibility of a multi-guideline context-aware clinical agent for vascular surgery; citation traceability and locked-corpus provenance facilitate future auditability.

METHODS: We describe the architecture and development of a context-aware clinical agent encompassing the full ESVS corpus of 14 CPGs.

title: Ruptured INfrarenal abdominal AneurySm: aortiC repair using the ENduranT Endograft. The R.IN.AS.C.ENT.E. Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) represents a vascular surgical emergency with high mortality. Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the bifurcated Endurant stent graft system is widely employed; however, data specifically addressing its performance in infrarenal rAAA remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study including 121 patients with confirmed infrarenal rAAA treated exclusively with bifurcated Endurant II or IIs (Medtronic Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota) devices across 5 Italian tertiary vascular centers from January 2014 to October 2024. Primary endpoints were technical success and 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included long-term survival, incidence of endoleaks, and reintervention rates. Patients receiving alternative stent grafts or hybrid procedures were excluded to ensure cohort homogeneity. RESULTS: P P A total of 121 patients were enrolled during the study period. The cohort had a mean age of 75.3 ± 8.2 years, with 91.7% male predominance. Technical success was achieved in 96.7%. The 30-day mortality rate was 15.7%. Multivariate logistic regression identified abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) (odds ratio [OR], 29.8; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.8-317.7; = .005) and use of an aortic occlusion balloon (AOB) (OR, 16.4; 95% CI, 2.5-106.2; = .003) as independent predictors of early mortality. At a median follow-up of 33.6 months (interquartile range, 4.9-72.3), 5-year survival was 65.4%, freedom from any endoleak was 92.6%, and freedom from reintervention was 91.6%. Late type Ia endoleaks occurred in 2.5% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: In this large, strictly defined infrarenal rAAA cohort, bifurcated Endurant stent grafts demonstrated high technical success and favorable early and mid-term clinical outcomes, including in patients with hostile neck anatomy. Early identification and management of ACS and judicious use of AOBs may improve survival. These findings reinforce current EVAR-first guidelines and emphasize the importance of device-specific outcome assessment in emergent rAAA repair.Clinical ImpactThis multicenter study provides one of the largest device-specific evaluations of bifurcated Endurant stent grafts for infrarenal ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms in a rigorously defined Italian cohort, demonstrating high technical success (96.7%) and low 30-day mortality (15.7%) despite a high prevalence of hostile neck anatomy (54.5%). Abdominal compartment syndrome and the use of an aortic occlusion balloon emerged as independent predictors of early mortality, highlighting the critical role of perioperative management. Mid-term outcomes were favorable, with a 5-year survival rate of 65.4%, a low incidence of type Ia endoleak (2.5%), and high freedom from reintervention (91.6%). Overall, these findings support the use of Endurant devices in emergent settings for anatomically suitable patients and reinforce EVAR-first strategies in the management of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms.

title: Outcomes of AngioJet™ Rheolytic Thrombectomy for Occluded Lower-Extremity Bypass Grafts: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower-extremity bypass graft occlusion is associated with recurrent ischemia and potential limb loss. This study evaluated the technical and clinical outcomes of AngioJet™ rheolytic thrombectomy for occluded bypass grafts in a single-center retrospective cohort. METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing AngioJet™ thrombectomy as the primary strategy for occluded bypass grafts (2014-2024) were reviewed. Technical success was defined as <30% residual stenosis. Outcomes included Rutherford category improvement, complications, 30-day mortality, major amputation, target lesion revascularization, and primary patency. Follow-up was available for 38/40 (95.0%) 30-day survivors. RESULTS: Forty-one procedures were analyzed. Technical success was achieved in 38/41 (92.7%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 80.1%-98.5%). Periprocedural complications occurred in 4 patients (9.8%; 95% CI: 2.7%-23.1%). Thirty-day mortality was 2.4% (1/41; 95% CI: 0.1%-12.9%) and major amputation was 4.9% (2/41; 95% CI: 0.6%-16.5%). Rutherford category improvement at 30 days was 43.9% (18/41; 95% CI: 28.5%-60.3%). Primary patency at final follow-up was 63.4% (26/41; 95% CI: 46.9%-77.9%) in the overall cohort (intent-to-treat) and 68.4% (26/38; 95% CI: 51.3%-82.5%) among technically successful cases. CONCLUSION: AngioJet™ thrombectomy is a technically feasible endovascular option for occluded bypass grafts with low 30-day mortality (2.4%) and amputation rates (4.9%). Prospective comparative studies are needed to define its role relative to surgical and alternative endovascular approaches.Clinical ImpactOccluded lower-extremity bypass grafts often cause limb-threatening ischemia in patients at high surgical risk. In this single-center cohort, AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy achieved technical success in 92.7% of procedures, with 30-day mortality of 2.4% and major amputation of 4.9%. These findings support AngioJet-assisted thrombectomy as a minimally invasive option for carefully selected patients with crossable grafts and treatable inflow or outflow disease. Clinicians should anticipate adjunctive interventions, monitor for compartment syndrome, and provide structured surveillance because reintervention remains common. Prospective comparative studies are needed before routine first-line use.

This study evaluated the technical and clinical outcomes of AngioJet™ rheolytic thrombectomy for occluded bypass grafts in a single-center retrospective cohort. METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing AngioJet™ thrombectomy as the primary strategy for occluded bypass grafts (2014-2024) were reviewed.

title: Examining Racial Disparities in Lower Extremity Amputation Outcomes Among Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers in North America: A Multicohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Racial and ethnic disparities in diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) outcomes are well described. We examined whether differences in major and minor lower extremity amputation (LEA) persist after matching for comorbidities, and whether the level of amputation identifies opportunities for earlier limb-preservation intervention. APPROACH: In this retrospective, propensity-matched cohort study using the TriNetX network (2002-2019), reported in accordance with Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology, adults with DFU were identified by diagnostic codes and stratified by race/ethnicity. Minor and major LEA risks were compared with a matched White (non-Hispanic) reference, reporting both relative and absolute risks. We also calculated the high-to-low (Hi-Lo) ratio (major:minor). RESULTS: Among 388,371 adults with DFU and after matching, Hispanic and African American patients had higher minor, major, and overall LEA risk than White patients (major-LEA absolute risk 3.0-4.7% vs. ∼2.7%; relative risks up to 1.89). Asian patients had the lowest risk. Native American patients had the highest Hi-Lo (major-to-minor amputation) ratio despite no significant increase in major-LEA risk, suggesting potential differences in disease presentation or access to limb-preservation care that warrant further study. Disparities persisted after adjustment for diabetes-related comorbidities and peripheral arterial disease. INNOVATION: Applied to a multiethnic DFU cohort, the Hi-Lo ratio gave a descriptive view of major- versus minor-amputation burden, most notably in Native American patients. CONCLUSION: The Hi-Lo amputation ratio may identify populations experiencing disproportionate major limb loss and help prioritize earlier vascular assessment, multidisciplinary limb-preservation referral, and posthealing surveillance. Persistent racial and ethnic differences after matching warrant further study of disease severity, access, and care delivery.[Figure: see text].

APPROACH: In this retrospective, propensity-matched cohort study using the TriNetX network (2002-2019), reported in accordance with Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology, adults with DFU were identified by diagnostic codes and stratified by race/ethnicity.

title: Clinical Criteria for Imaging in Children at Risk for Pulmonary Embolism.
abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a rare but serious condition in children. Clinical guidelines for imaging a suspected pediatric PE in Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) are lacking. The computerized tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) is the preferred diagnostic modality for suspected PE in an emergency department. Our study aims to introduce a simplified clinical assessment tool for ordering CTPA in children in the emergency room. This is a retrospective review of patients managed in our Emergency Department from 2000 to 2020. Patients were identified using International Classification of Diseases codes for PE, deep vein thrombosis, or similar diagnoses. The control group consisted of patients with PE symptoms, seen within the same time frame as the study group, who had negative CTPA. Twenty-five CTPA-positive patients were identified. Twenty-three of 25 CTPA-positive patients were aged 13 to 18 years. Common risk factors include protein-losing state (ie, nephrotic syndrome), oral contraceptive pill use, and obesity. Chest pain and tachypnea were the most common complaint and clinical sign, respectively. The hypercoagulability screen was negative in 65% of the patients. The mean D-dimer was 5.27 g/mL, and 6 patients, of whom 4 had saddle PE, had D-dimer > 10. Recurrence of PE and neurologic deficits were noted in 2 patients each. We present clinical criteria for ordering CTPA in children with suspected PE based on data from our center and a literature review of pediatric studies. Further multicenter studies with larger samples are needed to validate our proposed criteria.

The computerized tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) is the preferred diagnostic modality for suspected PE in an emergency department.

title: The law of surprise: temporal variation and seasonality of acute aortic syndromes: a single-centre epidemiologic cohort analysis spanning 20 years.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) represent life-threatening cardiovascular emergencies characterized by high mortality rates despite rapid intervention. Global epidemiological data indicate substantial variance in incidence. Longitudinal single-centre data over extended periods are limited but crucial for understanding diagnostic, demographic, and systemic factors influencing admission trends.(1). This study aimed to analyze annual and seasonal variation trends of AAS over a 20-year period in a single maximal care centre and explore potential chronological and environmental contributors to this variation. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated 403 patients admitted with a confirmed diagnosis of AAS between 2005 and 2025 at the University Hospital Erlangen, Germany. All diagnoses were established via computed tomography angiography (CTA) and confirmed intraoperatively. Annual, quarterly, and monthly surgical volumes were calculated, and temporal trends were analyzed using Poisson and negative binomial regression models. Admission rates during public holidays and school vacations were also evaluated. RESULTS: Over the 20-year observation period, a steady increasing trend in the annual number of AAS cases was observed, peaking in 2017. Analysis of quarterly distributions revealed a statistically significant dominance of cases in the fourth quarter (Q4: October-December; p < 0.05) compared to the second (Q2) and third (Q3) quarters. Monthly analysis demonstrated a prominent peak in October (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.85 vs. June, p < 0.05). Conversely, fixed public holidays and school vacations were associated with statistically significant reductions in daily admission counts (p < 0.05), with the lowest relative case counts observed during the Christmas vacation period (IRR: 0.40-0.50). CONCLUSION: The case counts of acute aortic syndromes exhibits significant temporal and seasonal variation, characterized by a distinct late-autumn and early-winter peak, alongside significant declines during institutional vacation periods. These findings suggest that acute cardiovascular events are heavily modulated by cyclical environmental and socio-systemic factors.

title: In Silico Insights into Device-Artery Interactions in Endovascular Pulmonary Flow Restrictors for Neonates with Congenital Heart Defects.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter pulmonary flow restriction using a modified Medtronic Vascular Plug (MVP™) has recently emerged as a promising alternative to surgical pulmonary arterial banding in neonates with complex congenital heart defects. However, clinical outcomes remain variable, and the underlying biomechanical mechanisms are poorly understood. This study aims to exploit in silico modeling to improve the understanding of device-artery interactions following the deployment of modified MVP™ in neonatal pulmonary arteries. To this end, we (i) developed and validated a high-fidelity digital twin of an MVP™ device, and (ii) used clinical imaging data from a retrospective cohort of seven neonates treated at Boston Children's Hospital to reproduce in silico the in vivo device-artery interaction in both the right and left pulmonary arteries. METHODS: The digital twin was reconstructed from high-resolution optical measurements and mechanically characterized under both local and global compression. Idealized artery geometries were generated based on pre-procedural angiographic measurements. For each patient, wall thickness was varied within a size-adjusted range derived from the literature, while Young's modulus was calibrated to reproduce the post-implantation arterial diameters, thereby quantifying the vessel's stiffness in response to device expansion. RESULTS: Case-specific simulations revealed marked variability in pulmonary artery effective stiffness across patients and between arterial branches. While identical post-implantation diameters could be reproduced through different thickness-stiffness combinations, these generated substantially different local contact pressure distributions. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the feasibility of a patient-specific computational framework for simulating the deployment of endovascular pulmonary flow restrictors using a validated MVP™ digital twin.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter pulmonary flow restriction using a modified Medtronic Vascular Plug (MVP™) has recently emerged as a promising alternative to surgical pulmonary arterial banding in neonates with complex congenital heart defects. However, clinical outcomes remain variable, and the underlying biomechanical mechanisms are poorly understood. This study aims to exploit in silico modeling to improve the understanding of device-artery interactions following the deployment of modified MVP™ in neonatal pulmonary arteries.

title: Hospital-wide massive transfusion over time: Indications, treatment strategies, and clinical outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Massive transfusion (MT) is a lifesaving intervention for severe hemorrhage. Contemporary data on indications, transfusion practices, and outcomes across a broad in-hospital population remain limited. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult patients receiving MT at Karolinska University Hospital between 2016 and 2021. MT was defined as transfusion of ≥10 red blood cell (RBC) units within 24 h. Data were obtained from the hospital transfusion registry and medical records. RESULTS: A total of 486 MT events were identified. Median age was 60 years (interquartile range [IQR] 46-70), and 65.6% of patients were male. The most common indications were trauma (15.6%), abdominal cancer surgery (15.0%), cardiothoracic surgery (14.0%), and vascular surgery (12.3%). The overall median RBC:plasma:platelet ratio was 5:5:1, consistent with balanced transfusion strategies. MT was more frequently associated with acute than elective procedures (67.2% vs. 32.8%, p < 0.001). Fibrinogen, tranexamic acid, and prothrombin complex concentrate were administered in 69.5%, 52.1%, and 13.6% of cases, respectively. Mortality was 10.3% at 24 h and 31.7% at 30 days. The annual number of MT events decreased significantly during the study period (p < 0.001), corresponding to an approximately 40% reduction between 2016 and 2021. CONCLUSION: MT was required across a wide range of surgical and medical specialties and remained associated with substantial mortality. Balanced transfusion strategies were well implemented, whereas the use of adjunct hemostatic therapies varied considerably. The marked reduction in MT events over time suggests improvements in hemorrhage management and bleeding control.

Contemporary data on indications, transfusion practices, and outcomes across a broad in-hospital population remain limited. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult patients receiving MT at Karolinska University Hospital between 2016 and 2021.

title: Treatment Strategies and Outcomes of Aneurysms Affecting Small and Medium Arteries in Neurofibromatosis Type 1. A systematic review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated arterial aneurysms are rare and characterized by vessel fragility and heterogeneous presentation. Evidence guiding optimal management remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate treatment strategies and outcomes in NF1-related arterial aneurysms. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251169825). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting management and outcomes of NF1-associated arterial aneurysms. Case reports, case series, and observational studies were included. Data were independently extracted by two reviewers. Primary outcomes included treatment strategies, technical success, complications, and mortality. Isolated aortic aneurysms or aortic dissections were not considered the primary target of the review. However, studies reporting concomitant aortic disease and aneurysmal involvement of non-aortic arteries were retained when relevant data on NF1-associated vasculopathy and its management were available. RESULTS: Eighty-six studies including 99 patients (mean age 42 years; 44.4% male) were analyzed. Aneurysms were most frequently located in cervico-vertebral (45.2%) and visceral arteries (24.0%). Multifocal disease was present in 12.1% of patients. Overall, 65.7% of patients presented with aneurysm rupture or acute hemorrhage. This high proportion should be interpreted cautiously because of the substantial publication bias inherent to a literature predominantly based on case reports and small case series. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently used approach (68.7%), followed by open surgery (19.2%), hybrid repair (5.0%), and conservative management (9.1%). Endovascular treatment showed a reported technical success rate exceeding 90%. Recanalization (6.3%), delayed thrombosis (4.2%), and new aneurysm formation (5.3%) were observed. Open repair was mainly used for anatomically complex or endovascularly inaccessible lesions. Overall mortality was 8.1%, primarily in patients presenting with rupture. CONCLUSIONS: NF1-associated aneurysms require an individualized, anatomy-driven management strategy. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently reported treatment and appears to be a viable option in anatomically suitable patients, while open and hybrid techniques remain important for selected complex lesions. However, the available evidence is derived predominantly from case reports and small case series and does not permit comparative assessment of treatment strategies. Lifelong imaging surveillance is mandatory due to the risk of recurrence and new aneurysm formation.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated arterial aneurysms are rare and characterized by vessel fragility and heterogeneous presentation. Evidence guiding optimal management remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate treatment strategies and outcomes in NF1-related arterial aneurysms.

title: Transcarotid Artery Stenting Using Flow Reversal for Non-Atherosclerotic Carotid Artery Disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the use of transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) in non-atherosclerotic carotid disease and compared outcomes with transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for all TCAR and TFCAS procedures performed from 2017-2024. Patients with lesion types categorized as atherosclerosis or restenosis were excluded. The study cohort included dissection, trauma, fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), and other non-atherosclerotic etiologies. Primary outcomes included major adverse events, including stroke, death, and composite endpoints. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences. RESULTS: A total of 541 TCAR and 2,348 TFCAS patients met inclusion criteria. TCAR was associated with lower contrast usage and fluoroscopy time across all lesion types. In unadjusted analyses, stroke or death rates were higher with TFCAS than TCAR for dissection (7.1% vs 1.9%, p=0.006), other lesions (8.7% vs 2.1%, p<0.001), and symptomatic (8.1% vs 2.2%, p=0.001) and asymptomatic patients (6.4% vs 1.6%, p<0.001). After propensity matching (527 pairs), TCAR was associated with significantly lower rates of stroke (4.4% vs 1.7%, p=0.0118), death (4.4% vs 0.4%, p<0.001), stroke or death (7.6% vs 1.9%, p<0.001), and stroke, death, or MI (8.0% vs 2.7%, p<0.001) compared with TFCAS (TFCAS vs TCAR, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: This study supports consideration of TCAR for non-atherosclerotic carotid pathology when carotid stenting is indicated and suggests that TCAR may offer important advantages over TFCAS, particularly in reducing the risk of perioperative stroke or death.

title: Beyond Risk Scores: Concordance of a Multidisciplinary Decision Support Instrument with Real Life Treatment Decisions for Patients with Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Treatment decisions for patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) are ethically complex and must be made under time pressure. This prospective observational study assessed how a previously developed decision support instrument (DSI) for rAAA aligns with real life treatment decisions and determined a reference threshold for interpreting its output. The DSI estimates the proportion of experts from the original multidisciplinary expert panel who would be expected to favour operative treatment (OT) for a given patient profile. METHODS: Consecutive rAAA patients were included between March 2024 and January 2026 from two Dutch hospitals. Treating vascular surgeons completed the DSI after the actual treatment decision (OT or palliative care). DSI outputs were analysed in relation to observed treatment decisions. A threshold sweep analysis was performed to identify a contextual reference threshold reflecting the level of DSI estimated expert support at which OT was generally pursued. Post-operative outcomes were assessed in OT patients for clinical context. RESULTS: Fifty patients were included; OT was chosen in 43 patients (86%). DSI estimated expert support was higher for patients receiving OT compared with palliative care (median 98% [interquartile range 97, 99%] vs. 83% [59, 89%]; p < .001). The contextual reference threshold was 93%, with concordance of 94% (95% confidence interval 83.8 - 97.9%). Case analysis highlighted challenges in capturing unresponsiveness due to profound hypovolaemic shock and assessing cardiac burden acutely Among patients surviving OT, relatively high health related quality of life was observed. CONCLUSIONS: The DSI shows concordance with real life treatment decisions for rAAA. A contextual reference threshold above which operative treatment was generally pursued could be empirically derived. Although refinement is needed to better identify certain high risk patients, these findings represent an important first step in the validation pathway and provide proof of concept for behavioural artificial intelligence technology methodology.

This prospective observational study assessed how a previously developed decision support instrument (DSI) for rAAA aligns with real life treatment decisions and determined a reference threshold for interpreting its output. The DSI estimates the proportion of experts from the original multidisciplinary expert panel who would be expected to favour operative treatment (OT) for a given patient profile.
