title: Clinical and economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to peripheral artery disease in Italy: A nationwide analysis.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) represents a major cause of non-traumatic lower-limb amputation and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite advances in medical and revascularization therapies, major amputations remain frequent, and comprehensive nationwide estimates of their clinical and hospital-related economic burden within the Italian National Health Service (SSN) are limited. The objectives of this study were to estimate the hospital-related economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to PAD in Italy and to assess revascularization patterns and in-hospital mortality within the SSN. We conducted a nationwide observational study using the Italian National Hospital Discharge Database. Acute hospital discharges between 2015 and 2021 with a major lower-limb amputation and Diagnosis Related Group 113 were identified. Inpatient volumes, length of stay, and costs were estimated by amputation level. A longitudinal cohort of patients amputated between 2015 and 2017 was followed for two years before and after the index hospitalization to assess prior revascularization and in-hospital mortality using age- and sex-adjusted Cox models. A total of 26,417 PAD-attributable major amputations were identified, 75.6% of which were above-knee procedures. Cumulative inpatient expenditure reached €294 million, corresponding to over 511,000 hospital days. Only 46.0% of patients underwent revascularization before amputation. In-hospital mortality increased steeply within the first six months post-amputation and remained higher after above-knee procedures and among patients with diabetes, reaching 16-25% at 180 days and 23-34% at two years. Major lower-limb amputation remains a severe and costly outcome of PAD in Italy. Improved implementation of guideline-recommended PAD management is needed to reduce avoidable amputations and their economic burden on the SSN.

Despite advances in medical and revascularization therapies, major amputations remain frequent, and comprehensive nationwide estimates of their clinical and hospital-related economic burden within the Italian National Health Service (SSN) are limited. The objectives of this study were to estimate the hospital-related economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to PAD in Italy and to assess revascularization patterns and in-hospital mortality within the SSN.

title: Orthoplastic Limb Salvage Using Transtibial Transport and Free-Flap Reconstruction in Patients With Diabetes-Related Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: Early revascularization-through endovascular or open surgery-is the cornerstone of treatment for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, some patients are deemed "no-option" because of diffuse infrapopliteal disease, poor distal runoff, or failed previous interventions, leaving limited limb-salvage strategies. We report an orthoplastic limb-salvage case in a 56-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes, severe peripheral arterial disease, and a chronic foot ulcer complicated by toe gangrene after unsuccessful revascularization. After urgent radical débridement, ray amputation, culture-directed antibiotics, and negative-pressure wound therapy, transtibial transport (TTT) was done to improve microcirculation. After infection control and wound stabilization, definitive reconstruction was achieved using a large anterolateral thigh perforator free flap with a flow-through microsurgical technique to provide durable coverage while preserving distal perfusion. At 12-month follow-up, the flap remained viable with complete epithelialization, no ulcer recurrence, preserved foot architecture, and independent ambulation with protective footwear, indicating meaningful functional recovery. This case highlights the potential role of combining TTT with microsurgical reconstruction in orthoplastic management of "no-option" CLTI. Enhancing microcirculation alongside robust soft-tissue coverage may expand limb-salvage possibilities when traditional revascularization is not feasible.

We report an orthoplastic limb-salvage case in a 56-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes, severe peripheral arterial disease, and a chronic foot ulcer complicated by toe gangrene after unsuccessful revascularization.

title: Venous thromboembolism after breast cancer surgery: incidence, predictive factors and outcomes in 270,564 patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast cancer surgery is generally considered to be low risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, when VTE occurs, it may lead to severe complications and increased mortality. This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database. METHODS: The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2008-2023) was queried to identify female patients undergoing surgery for breast cancer without concurrent reconstruction. Patients were stratified according to postoperative VTE occurrence. Demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, operative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of VTE and to construct a predictive model, which was internally validated using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: Among 270,564 patients included, 465 (0.2%) developed postoperative VTE. Of these, 247 (53.1%) had deep vein thrombosis, 177 (38.1%) pulmonary embolism, and 41 (8.8%) both. Patients who developed VTE were older, had higher body mass index (BMI), greater comorbidity burden, and longer operative times (all p < 0.001). They also demonstrated lower preoperative serum albumin, hematocrit, prothrombin time, and albumin-to-creatinine ratio. VTE was associated with significantly longer hospital stays, increased rates of reoperation and readmission, and a more than 20-fold higher crude 30-day mortality (1.9% vs. 0.1%) (all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.26 per 10 years), BMI (OR 1.17 per 5 kg/m²), congestive heart failure (OR 2.43), metastatic cancer (OR 2.05), lower serum albumin (OR 0.63 per 1 g/dL), and longer operative duration (OR 1.09 per 30 min) were independently associated with postoperative VTE. Compared with partial mastectomy, total mastectomy (OR 2.58), modified radical mastectomy (OR 2.22), and radical mastectomy (OR 2.80) were associated with significantly higher odds of postoperative VTE. The predictive model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.717; optimism-corrected 0.700) and good calibration. Age, BMI, congestive heart failure, metastatic cancer, mastectomy and operative time remained associated with VTE in all sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSION: Postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery is uncommon but associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Advanced age, obesity, cardiac comorbidity, metastatic disease, hypoalbuminemia, longer operative duration, and greater surgical extent were independently associated with increased thromboembolic risk. Awareness of these risk factors may support individualized perioperative risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis decisions, as recommended by current consensus guidance, and facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative VTE. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

However, when VTE occurs, it may lead to severe complications and increased mortality. This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database.

title: Functional outcomes and quality of life after endovascular thrombectomy in large and extensive infarcts (ASPECTS 0-5): a multicentre registry study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is established for large infarcts, but remains cautiously applied in extensive infarcts with an Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) of 0-2. Real-life outcome data remain limited. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment comparing extensive (ASPECTS 0-2) and large infarcts (ASPECTS 3-5) in patients with anterior-circulation occlusion and EVT. The primary outcome was the ordinal 90-day mRS distribution; secondary outcomes were mRS 0-3, survival, quality of life (3-level European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions) and living condition. RESULTS: Of 18,069 screened patients, 889 were analysed (ASPECTS 1-2, n = 89; ASPECTS 3-5, n = 800); none had ASPECTS 0. With ASPECTS 1-2, 20.2% achieved mRS 0-3 and 55.1% died within 90 days. In the model including successful reperfusion, no statistically significant association was detected between infarct group and the 90-day mRS distribution (common odds ratio [cOR] 0.80; 95% CI, 0.53-1.23) or mRS 0-3 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.64-1.25), whereas successful reperfusion was associated with both (cOR 3.68; 95% CI, 2.31-5.85 and aOR 4.10; 95% CI, 2.45-6.86). Among survivors, median European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions utility index was 0.445 vs 0.541 (n = 27/324), and 51.5% vs 50.9% lived at home (n = 33/411). DISCUSSION: An extensive infarct carried a challenging prognosis, yet acceptable outcome and non-institutional living remained achievable in a relevant minority. An independent association of infarct group with outcome was not detected. CONCLUSION: An acceptable outcome remained attainable in selected patients with extensive infarction, particularly after successful reperfusion. Lacking a medically managed comparator, these data describe prognosis rather than treatment effect.

Real-life outcome data remain limited. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment comparing extensive (ASPECTS 0-2) and large infarcts (ASPECTS 3-5) in patients with anterior-circulation occlusion and EVT.

title: Hypoxia Paradox in Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization for Chronic Subdural Hematoma: A Mechanistic Framework for Treatment Resistance.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The clinical efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) in chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) is increasingly established; yet, recent landmark randomized controlled trials consistently report only a 30% to 50% reduction in recurrence, implying that middle meningeal artery occlusion alone does not fully resolve the pathological microenvironment of the outer hematoma membrane. The mechanistic basis of this incomplete treatment response remains undefined. METHODS: To develop a mechanistic framework for this clinical paradox, we performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review. Of 876 records identified across PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov, 47 underwent full-text review and 18 studies (16 clinical studies and 2 registry records) published through October 2025 were included, integrating clinical outcomes with pathological and molecular insights. A secondary analysis of a publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data set of normal human dural tissue was performed to map the cellular infrastructure underlying key molecular drivers. RESULTS: CSDH progression is driven by an interconnected triad of inflammatory infiltration, pathological angiogenesis, and vascular hyperpermeability within the outer hematoma membrane. While MMAE suppresses these pathogenic programs by reducing middle meningeal artery-derived arterial supply, we propose that occlusion-induced ischemic stress may paradoxically stabilize hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, triggering compensatory angiogenesis in cases of incomplete devascularization, a mechanism we formally term the "hypoxia paradox". Secondary single-cell RNA sequencing analysis identified fibroblast-like and endothelial dural populations as the primary cellular platforms for this response, providing a translational cellular basis for the proposed framework. CONCLUSION: The hypoxia paradox represents a testable mechanistic hypothesis, offering a coherent explanation for heterogeneous MMAE outcomes and generates specific, testable predictions regarding post-MMAE molecular signatures in the outer hematoma membrane. Prospective paired tissue sampling integrated with multimodal molecular analyses is essential to validate this model and advance CSDH management toward individualized, mechanism-guided therapy.

The mechanistic basis of this incomplete treatment response remains undefined. METHODS: To develop a mechanistic framework for this clinical paradox, we performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review.

title: Transcatheter coil embolization for proximal thoracic aortic pseudoaneurysms: a case series with mid-term clinical and imaging follow-up.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms represent a life-threatening complication of cardiac surgery. Traditional redo surgery is associated with substantial operative risk, while conventional endovascular stenting is often precluded by complex anatomy. We evaluated the clinical feasibility, safety, and durability of transcatheter coil embolization for proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms in a high-risk cohort. METHODS: Between September 2020 and February 2024, nine consecutive high-risk patients with proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms underwent transcatheter coil embolization at our institution. Preoperative risk profiles, procedural characteristics, intra-hospital outcomes, and serial computed tomography angiography follow-up datasets were retrospectively analyzed. RESULTS: The cohort was predominantly male (88.9%), with a mean age of 69.1±13 years and a mean Logistic EuroSCORE of 22.82%±18.76%. Patients had undergone a mean of 2.56 previous aortic procedures. Access routes included transfemoral (n = 6), transapical (n = 3), axillary (n = 1), and transbrachial (n = 1) approaches. Stent-assisted embolization was deployed in two cases. Technical success was achieved in all cases, with a median post-procedural stay of six days. Mean follow-up was 16±14.8 months. Serial imaging demonstrated stable sac dimensions in all patients, with no local recurrences. All-cause mortality was 33.3% (n = 3), and all deaths were attributed to sudden systemic events unrelated to target lesion failure or rupture. CONCLUSIONS: Transcatheter coil embolization appears to be a safe, technically feasible, and durable alternative for the exclusion of proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms. In this small high-risk cohort, the technique achieved excellent local control and mid-term structural stability in fragile, multi-operated patients who were not candidates for conventional open surgery.

Traditional redo surgery is associated with substantial operative risk, while conventional endovascular stenting is often precluded by complex anatomy. We evaluated the clinical feasibility, safety, and durability of transcatheter coil embolization for proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms in a high-risk cohort.

title: Utilizing evidence-based diagnosis and treatment for central venous thrombosis: closing the gaps where guidelines fail.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Catheter-related thrombosis (CRT) is a frequent complication of central venous catheters and accounts for most upper extremity deep vein thrombosis events. Despite its increasing clinical burden, management remains poorly standardized because recommendations are largely extrapolated from general venous thromboembolism studies rather than CRT-specific evidence. AREAS COVERED: We performed a structured comparative review of major international, European, and North American guidelines, consensus documents, and position statements identified through PubMed, Ovid, and Scopus searches covering January 2016 to March 2026. Nineteen documents from vascular medicine, oncology, and vascular access societies were included. Recommendations on diagnostic strategies, imaging modalities, catheter management, anticoagulant selection, treatment duration, and invasive interventions were systematically compared. EXPERT OPINION: Considerable heterogeneity persists across recommendations. Ultrasound is consistently endorsed as the first-line imaging modality, whereas the role of clinical prediction scores and D-dimer remains uncertain because neither has been validated in CRT populations. Catheters should be preserved when functional, correctly positioned, and free from infection. Anticoagulation for at least 3 months is universally recommended, while invasive procedures should be reserved for selected patients with extensive thrombosis or life- or limb-threatening complications. Prospective studies are urgently needed to validate diagnostic algorithms, optimize anticoagulant strategies, and develop CRT-specific evidence-based pathways.

title: Electrosurgical Septotomy Across the Full Spectrum of Aortic Dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion. METHODS: A retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure. RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair, and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < .001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia, or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital, and overall mortality were 10%, 14%, and 19%, respectively, with 1 fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months. CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small, heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

title: Development and Validation of a Nomogram for Predicting Preoperative Venous Thromboembolism in Patients With Lower Extremity Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: p = BackgroundPatients with lower extremity fractures (LEF) are at high risk of preoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, existing risk assessment models are not specifically developed and validated for this population.ObjectiveTo develop and validate a prediction model for preoperative VTE in emergency LEF patients, and to compare the performance of traditional logistic regression (LR) with that of machine learning (ML) algorithms.DesignRetrospective cohort study.SettingPeking University Shenzhen Hospital, China.Participants486 patients with LEF admitted between January 2022 and July 2025.MethodsTwo modeling strategies were compared: 1) a traditional LR nomogram using backward stepwise selection, and 2) nine ML algorithms with Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)-based feature selection. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination (area under the curve, AUC), calibration, classification metrics (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) and decision curve analysis.ResultsOf 486 enrolled patients, 79 (16.3%) developed preoperative VTE. Among the ML models, LASSO-LR and multilayer perceptron (MLP) achieved the highest validation AUCs (0.709 each), the best calibration and highest net benefit. The traditional LR nomogram showed an identical AUC of 0.709 (95% CI: 0.691-0.718), with superior calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow0.738, calibration intercept = -0.109, slope = 0.921) and better stability. Therefore, this simple five-predictor traditional LR nomogram, incorporating age ≥ 65 years, hemoglobin, glucose, external immobilization, and pre-injury anticoagulant or antiplatelet use, was selected as the optimal model.ConclusionThe traditional LR nomogram appears promising for preoperative VTE risk prediction in LEF patients. External validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: SERPINE1 IntegratingGenotype With Clinical Indicators Improves Venous Thromboembolism Risk Prediction in Cancer Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study From Xinjiang.
abstract: SERPINE1 SERPINC1 PROC MTHFR F5 F2 SERPINE1 P SERPINE1 ObjectiveTo develop and validate a venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk prediction model integrating genetic polymorphisms and routine clinical indicators in a cohort of cancer patients from Xinjiang, China.MethodsA retrospective study was conducted on 1135 cancer patients (179 with VTE, 956 without) at Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University between March 2024 and May 2025. Six gene polymorphisms (,,,,,) and clinical predictors were assessed. Chi-square tests and logistic regression identified independent predictors for model construction. Model performance was evaluated using ROC analysis, and three clinically optimized cut-off values were defined.ResultsThe4G allele was identified as a strong genetic risk factor for VTE (4G/4G genotype: OR=2.330, 95%CI: 1.378-3.942; 4G/5G genotype: OR=2.399, 95%CI: 1.411-4.078). No significant associations were found for the other five genes. Age (OR=1.022, 95%CI: 1.008-1.037), D-dimer level (OR=1.288, 95%CI: 1.186-1.399), and hemoglobin level (OR=0.987, 95%CI: 0.979-0.995) were independent clinical predictors (<0.01). The combined model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.769 (95%CI: 0.731-0.807). Three optimized cut-off values were derived for different clinical contexts: high-sensitivity (90.5%), balanced (Youden index 0.434), and high-specificity (90.1%).ConclusionThe4G allele independently predicts VTE risk in this cohort of cancer patients from Xinjiang. A prediction model integrating this genetic marker with age, D-dimer, and hemoglobin demonstrates good discriminatory performance. The three derived cut-off values may facilitate risk-stratified thromboprophylaxis in clinical practice; however, these findings are based on a retrospective, single-center cohort and internally validated only by ROC analysis.

title: Trends and Disparities in Peripheral Artery Disease and Dementia-Related Mortality in the United States, 1999-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular risk factors are common among individuals with both peripheral artery disease (PAD) and dementia, and these co-existing conditions are a major public health problem. Our goal is to assess nationwide mortality trends and disparities associated with concomitant PAD and dementia in the United States between 1999 and 2024. METHODS: This is a population-based analysis using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database to assess adults aged 65 years and older. Death certificates that mentioned both PAD and dementia were included. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and annual percent changes (APCs) were calculated to study the national trends by demographic and geographic subgroups. RESULTS: There were 317,390 deaths among patients who had both PAD and dementia. The overall AAMR was fairly stable over the study period, rising marginally from 23.97 in 1999 to 24.22 in 2024. AAMRs were higher in non-Hispanic African Americans across racial and ethnic groups and peaked in non-metropolitan regions. The sensitivity analyses showed that mortality rates that were driven by PAD significantly declined (AAPC: -4.77) and rates driven by dementia (AAPC: 3.77) increased significantly over the 25-year period. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the age-standardized mortality for concomitant PAD and dementia was largely stable, but there are still important geographical and demographic differences. The mortality curves when divided by underlying cause of death show that deaths due to PAD have decreased, while deaths due to dementia have risen in the United States among older adults over the study period.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Self-Reported Practices of Emergency and Intensive Care Nurses in Managing Traumatic Brain Injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide, with a growing burden in low- and middle-income countries. Nurses in emergency and intensive care units (ICUs) play a critical role in TBI management, yet little is known about their competencies in Palestine. AIMS: This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes and self-reported practices of emergency and intensive care unit nurses regarding traumatic brain injury management and to identify factors associated with these outcomes. STUDY DESIGN: A descriptive cross-sectional survey using stratified random sampling was conducted in governmental and private hospitals in the northern West Bank, Palestine. Data were collected in January 2025 using a validated Arabic questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation coefficients and multiple linear regression analyses were performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: A total of 151 nurses participated, yielding a response rate of 61.4% (151/246). Nurses demonstrated generally good foundational knowledge, particularly in Glasgow Coma Scale interpretation and recognition of neurological responses, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring. Attitudes were predominantly positive, with strong support for specialised training. Self-reported practices included maintaining adequate blood pressure and initiating deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis. Knowledge correlated significantly with attitude and self-reported practice, and attitude correlated strongly with self-reported practice. Previous TBI training, higher educational level and longer clinical experience were associated with better outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Emergency and intensive care unit nurses demonstrated adequate foundational knowledge and positive attitudes towards traumatic brain injury management, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring and selected self-reported practices. Structured continuing professional development, standardised protocols and organisational support are needed to strengthen neurotrauma nursing care. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The findings support context-sensitive continuing education, simulation, standardised protocols and organisational measures that enable nurses to translate knowledge into consistent neurotrauma care in resource-constrained settings.

title: Mortality, Morbidity, and Treatment-Related Outcomes Following Pathological Hip Fractures: An 8-Year Single-Center Experience.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, type of treatment, and factors associated with mortality and morbidity, including the length of hospital stay, among patients with pathological hip fractures in a tertiary center in Saudi Arabia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted, which included all adult patients diagnosed with pathological hip fractures from 2016 to 2024. Demographics, fracture type, type of treatment, complications, and outcomes data were evaluated. A univariate analysis was performed to identify associations between clinical variables and patient outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 47 patients were included, with a mean age of 60.6 ± 17.12 years. Most patients were female (61.7%) and had femoral neck fractures (63.8%). Surgical treatment was performed in 78.7% of cases. The overall mortality rate was 6.4%, and 17.0% of patients experienced complications, including gait disturbances, bleeding, and deep vein thrombosis. Mortality was significantly associated with conservative treatment (P = 0.007). All deaths occurred in the conservatively treated group. Longer hospital stays were linked to pre-operative anticoagulant use (P = 0.011) and osteoporosis (P = 0.03). CONCLUSION: Surgical management of pathological hip fractures was associated with improved survival and should be prioritized when clinically feasible. Awareness of pre-operative anticoagulant use and osteoporosis is essential for perioperative planning and may help reduce prolonged hospitalization in this high-risk population.

title: Limb Salvage in Limb-Threatening Necrotizing Fasciitis of the Diabetic Foot: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Necrotizing fasciitis (NF) is a rapidly progressive soft tissue infection with high morbidity and mortality, especially in patients with diabetes mellitus. Early diagnosis is challenging because initial clinical signs may be subtle, yet timely intervention is critical to prevent limb loss and death. CASE REPORT: We report a 68-year-old male with long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus and multiple comorbidities who presented with a 1-week history of rapidly progressive left foot pain and swelling extending to the mid-calf. Laboratory investigations revealed marked inflammation, and imaging indicated fascial involvement. The patient underwent multiple surgical debridements, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, strict glycemic control, limb off-loading, tibial angioplasty to optimize perfusion, and advanced wound care including negative pressure wound therapy and reconstructive procedures. Progressive healing was achieved without major amputation. CONCLUSION: Limb salvage remains feasible in selected diabetic patients with limb-threatening NF when early recognition, aggressive surgical management, vascular optimization, metabolic control, and coordinated multidisciplinary care are implemented.

title: [Successful Hybrid Treatment of Crawford Type IV Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysm:Report of a Case].
abstract: Thoracolaparotomy remains the first-line surgical approach for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms. However, there is still room for improvement with regard to mortality and the incidence of postoperative complications, including paraplegia. In this context, hybrid treatment strategies that allow preservation of organ blood flow have gained increasing attention. We report a case of a Crawford type IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm that was successfully treated using a hybrid approach. The patient was an 87-year-old man. Computed tomography (CT) at admission revealed a thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm. Given the patient's advanced age and severe frailty, thoracolaparotomy was considered high risk. As the primary surgery, abdominal total debranching with thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed. Bypasses from the right external iliac artery to visceral arteries were made, and stent graft was deployed in the thoracic artery. Anastomosis to the left renal artery was technically impossible. On postoperative day two, endovascular abdominal aortic stent graft was implanted. The patient was extubated on postoperative day 4, and was transferred to a rehabilitation hospital on postoperative day 29.

title: [Non-anatomic Bypass for Severe Brachiocephalic Artery Stenosis due to Dissecting Aneurysm After Total Arch Aortic Replacement for Stanford Type A Acute Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
abstract: Dissecting brachiocephalic artery aneurysm after total arch aortic replacement poses a risk of postoperative cerebral infarction, yet no consensus exists regarding optimal management. Treatment decisions rely on the patient's condition, degree of true lumen stenosis, and lesion characteristics. We report a case of a dissecting brachiocephalic aneurysm with severe true lumen stenosis following surgery for Stanford type A acute aortic dissection. A 70-year-old man was transferred to our hospital with acute aortic dissection and multiple right-hemispheric cerebral infarctions and underwent emergency total arch replacement. On postoperative day nine, contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed progressive false lumen expansion with significant true lumen compression. To prevent further cerebral ischemia, a left axillary-right common carotid artery non-anatomic bypass was performed. The patient gradually recovered left upper limb function and was transferred for rehabilitation on postoperative day 27.

title: [Aortic Root Replacement for a Left Sinus of Valsalva Aneurysm Complicated by Ascending Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
abstract: We report a case of a left sinus of Valsalva aneurysm (SVA) complicated by ascending aortic dissection (AAD). A 37-year-old man presented to our hospital with worsening leg edema and was diagnosed with heart failure due to severe aortic regurgitation (AR). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and transesophageal echocardiography revealed the presence of an AAD and a left SVA. After medical treatment for heart failure, the patient underwent aortic root replacement. The postoperative course was favorable. The combination of SVA and AAD in a young patient is extremely rare and may lead to delayed diagnosis. Therefore, thorough investigation of the underlying cause is essential, particularly in young patients presenting with heart failure or AR.

title: Nomogram for Postoperative Permanent Neurologic Dysfunction Following Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery: A Multicentral Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Permanent neurologic dysfunction (PND) often complicates following surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and is strongly correlated with unfavorable outcomes. Consequently, developing an effective diagnostic method to identify high-risk patients is of considerable importance. METHODS: This retrospective study, covering 2022 to 2024 across two centers, ultimately included 117 ATAAD patients with Supra-Aortic Branch Vessel (SABV) dissection from our center (2022-2023) as the training set and 52 ATAAD patients with SABV dissection from a secondary center (2024) as the validation set. We used logistic regression to identify predictors and developed a nomogram, which was assessed using the area under the ROC curve, calibration and decision curve analysis. External validation was conducted using the validation set. RESULTS: In this study, 169 cases were finally collected (117 in the training set and 52 in the validation set), of whom 64 patients developed postoperative PND. Four risk factors were identified: brachiocephalic trunk dissection at the bifurcation plane, chronic kidney disease, age over 50, and cross-clamp duration over 168 min. The AUC was 0.809 for the training set and 0.736 for the validation set. The nomogram model demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, and decision curve analysis potential clinical utility for predicting postoperative PND risk for thresholds of 1%-90% in the training set and 3%-75% in the validation set. CONCLUSIONS: This study developed and validated a predictive model for assessing the risk of postoperative PND in patients undergoing ATAAD surgery, which may assist clinicians in individualized risk assessment.

title: Ethnic Differences in Clinical Manifestations of Behçet's Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Turkic and Non-Turkic Patients.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Behçet's disease (BD) is a multisystem inflammatory vasculitis with clinical heterogeneity that may vary across ethnic groups within the same country. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of ethnicity on the clinical manifestations, immunogenic laboratory findings and disease course of BD by comparing Turkic and non-Turkic patients in a large Iranian referral cohort. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 2697 patients with BD followed at the BD clinic of Shariati Hospital in Tehran, Iran, from 2007 to 2019 were included. RESULTS: Patients were stratified by ethnicity into Turkic (N = 1037; 38.5%) and non-Turkic (N = 1660; 61.5% [with Persian/Fars, N = 980 subgrouping]) groups, and demographic, clinical manifestations, and immunogenic laboratory findings were extracted from medical records. Mean age at BD onset was 25.72 ± 10.02 years in Turkic patients and 24.69 ± 10.23 years in non-Turkic patients, and males comprised 61.3% and 57.1% of the two groups, respectively. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-B5 positivity was 55.1% in Turkic versus 53.1% in non-Turkic patients, and HLA-B51 positivity was 48.7% versus 46.5%, respectively. Most clinical manifestations showed similar prevalence across groups, including oral aphthous ulcers (98.7% vs. 99.0%), genital aphthous ulcers (60.5% vs. 62.0%), uveitis (50.1% vs. 53.2%), and deep vein thrombosis (5.3% vs. 5.1%). Superficial phlebitis was more frequent in Turkic patients (p = 0.02), and oral aphthous ulcers occurred earlier in Turkic patients (p = 0.023). A three-class latent class model demonstrated the best fit (BIC = 14,986.58). In multinomial logistic regression analysis, Turkic patients had slightly higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 0.91-1.33; p = 0.320) and slightly lower odds ratio of the multisystem phenotype (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.68-1.30; p = 0.692); however, neither association was statistically significant. Female gender was associated with higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype than the mucocutaneous-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.14-1.67; p = 0.001). CONCLUSION: In this large Iranian BD cohort, Turkic and non-Turkic patients exhibited broadly similar disease phenotypes and comparable HLA-B51 frequencies, with small but potentially relevant ethnic differences in the timing of oral ulcers and the frequency of superficial phlebitis. These findings suggest that ethnicity may influence BD phenotype through mechanisms beyond HLA-B51, possibly involving other immune-related genetic variants such as tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, endoplasmic reticulum aminopeptidase 1(ERAP1), Interleukin (IL)-10. Of note, the significant differences observed in Turkic versus non-Turkic comparisons were not present in the Turkic versus Persian (Fars) comparison, indicating that the findings are not driven by a single ethnic subgroup.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Behçet's disease (BD) is a multisystem inflammatory vasculitis with clinical heterogeneity that may vary across ethnic groups within the same country. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of ethnicity on the clinical manifestations, immunogenic laboratory findings and disease course of BD by comparing Turkic and non-Turkic patients in a large Iranian referral cohort. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 2697 patients with BD followed at the BD clinic of Shariati Hospital in Tehran, Iran, from 2007 to 2019 were included.

title: Wound blush as a predictor for limb salvage among people with non-healing diabetic foot ulcers.
abstract: Background and objectives Wound blush represents angiographic visualisation of tissue-level perfusion around a diabetic foot ulcer. While wound blush after endovascular revascularisation (EVR) predicts improved outcomes, its' prognostic value on diagnostic digital subtraction angiography (DSA) has not been studied, particularly in India. This study compared the role of wound blush after DSA and after EVR in predicting wound healing and limb salvage in non-healing diabetic foot ulcers. Methods A total of 428 individuals with diabetic foot ulcers underwent diagnostic DSA. Wound blush was assessed on DSA and, where applicable, after EVR. Participants were followed for wound healing and amputation outcomes. The wound blush positive and wound blush negative groups on DSA, among participants managed without EVR, and according to wound blush status following EVR were compared. Results On diagnostic DSA, 137(31.6%) participants were wound blush positive and 291(68.4%) were wound blush negative. Wound blush positive participants demonstrated higher rates of complete wound healing (90.5% vs. 79%; P=0.002), and lower amputation rates (7.6 vs. 22.2%; P<0.001) compared to wound blush negative participants. Among participants managed without EVR, limb salvage was significantly higher in wound blush positive than wound blush negative participants (92.4% vs.77.8%; P=0.002). Following EVR, limb salvage was achieved in 89% of participants who demonstrated wound blush compared to 77% (P=0.062) of those who remained wound blush negative. Baseline wound blush positivity predicted favourable outcomes irrespective of EVR. Interpretation and conclusions Wound blush on diagnostic angiography and after EVR is a strong predictor of wound healing and limb salvage in non-healing diabetic foot ulcers. Wound blush on initial DSA helps identifying participants in whom revascularisation may be deferred, reducing endovascular interventions without adverse limb outcomes.

title: Development of Aortic Stents from Open Surgery to Endovascular Therapy: A Brazilian Contribution to the Treatment of Aortic Diseases.
abstract: The treatment of aortic diseases has undergone profound transformation over the last decades, with the progressive incorporation of endovascular techniques either replacing or complementing conventional open surgical repair. The development of aortic stents represents one of the most significant milestones in this transition. This article reviews the historical, experimental, and clinical evolution of aortic stents, with emphasis on pioneering Brazilian contributions, including the experimental phase in animal models, the first clinical applications in aortic dissection, and the role of the national industry in the development and dissemination of these technologies. The impact of these innovations on contemporary cardiovascular surgical practice and future perspectives are also discussed.

title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: An anatomy-aware spatio-temporal generative extrapolation network for distal ascending aorta restoration in standard echocardiographic views.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), the standard parasternal long-axis (PLAX) view enables reliable evaluation of the aortic valve and aortic root. Owing to the limited field of view of the ultrasound probe and rib-window occlusion, the distal ascending aorta (AA) is frequently truncated, compromising the diagnosis of aortic aneurysm and dilation. PURPOSE: We aim to address the incomplete visualization of the distal AA in standard PLAX views. By aggregating fragmented anatomical features intermittently visible in adjacent frames, we enhance the clarity of vessel wall edges and generate the distal AA structure, thereby completing the missing AA imagery in standard PLAX views. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ± Δ = 0.2 cm We retrospectively collected 1160 TTE videos from Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital (August 2022 - December 2024), all showing complete AA anatomy. After de-identification, 1059 cases were randomly split into training/validation/test sets (6:2:2), and 101 cases were reserved for observer agreement experiments. An additional 152 videos from three different device models (EPIQ CVX, GE Voluson E10, Resona A20T) formed an external validation set. Two training data types were constructed: (i) dual-view synchronous data - a standard PLAX sequence and an AO-PLAX sequence acquired after a cranial probe shift, phase-matched at end diastole (ED); and (ii) locally masked data - the distal AA region was masked, forcing the model to infer missing anatomy from left-side context. Input sequences of five frames (ED2) were extracted. The proposed Spatio-Temporal Ascending-Aorta generative adversarial network (STAA-GAN) first aligns adjacent frames using an Edge Boosted Feature Alignment (EBFA) module with multi-stage modulated deformable convolutions. A channel-wise fusion strategy then aggregates temporally aligned features. The fused representation is fed into a Swin-UNet generator enhanced with a Strip based Cross window Prediction (SCP) module to capture long-range structural dependencies. Training employs a composite loss including pixel reconstruction, feature reconstruction, texture consistency, relativistic average least-squares GAN (RaLSGAN), temporal coherence, and structure-aware terms, with data-dependent weighting. Statistical analyzes included Bland-Altman, Passing-Bablok regression, paired t-tests with Cohen's d, Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and two one-sided tests (TOST,). RESULTS: α 1 = 0.00417 ≤ 0.01 ± 0.13 Δ = 0.2 p < 0.001 0.913 0.045 ± p < 0.001 d < 0.2 STAA-GAN achieved the best image-quality values among the compared methods, with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) = 22.51 dB, structural similarity index (SSIM) = 0.7574, multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM) = 0.8598, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) = 0.1758. All 12 pairwise comparisons (SRN, IOH, and U-Transformer versus STAA-GAN, designated as the reference group) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (), with absolute effect sizes ranging from 0.255 to 3.439. The per-frame inference time was 203 ms. In clinical consistency validation, the mean difference between measurements on generated and original images was cm with 95% limits of agreement within cm; TOST with cm confirmed clinical equivalence for all comparisons (). The segmentation Dice coefficient on generated images averagedacross five cross-validation folds. External validation on three different ultrasound devices (Philips, GE, Mindray) maintained consistent equivalence (TOST, Cohen's). These results demonstrate that STAA-GAN produces clinically interchangeable distal ascending aorta images with high fidelity and real-time feasibility. CONCLUSIONS: STAA-GAN enables extrapolation of the missing distal ascending aorta in standard PLAX views, achieving improved image quality and clinically equivalent diameter measurements on both internal and external validation datasets. These findings support its potential for assisting distal ascending aorta assessment in routine echocardiography.

title: Angiographic Signatures of Brain Collateralization.
abstract: The severity of ischemic strokes, the likelihood of successful endovascular treatment, and subsequent clinical patient outcomes are all strongly influenced by the degree of collateralization of the brain arterial network. Although several scoring systems based on different imaging modalities have been developed to assess brain collateralization, they are subjective and quite coarse and do not capture many nuances of the underlying collateral vessel distribution. This article introduces a methodology for quantitatively and objectively assessing the degree of collateralization of the brain. The strategy is based on a regional analysis of time-density curves extracted from dynamic angiographic image sequences. To investigate the dependence of the extracted metrics on the underlying collateralization in a controlled manner, a computational study is carried out by generating virtual patients with prescribed collateralization characteristics and conducting blood flow and transport simulations to create virtual angiographic sequences. The virtual angiograms of patients with large vessel occlusions and different collateral vessel distributions are used to generate "angiographic signatures" reflective of the underlying collateralization. The results show that angiographic signatures created from virtual angiograms exhibit consistent characteristics with angiographic signatures of actual stroke patients with different levels of collateralization. These findings indicate that these angiographic signatures can be used to assess the underlying collateralization of the brain and identify patients and conditions associated with adverse treatment outcomes.

title: A Case of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Thumb-Sized Calcification Detected on Panoramic Radiograph.
abstract: A 73-year-old male with dyslipidemia and chronic kidney disease exhibited carotid calcification on a dental panoramic radiograph. Ultrasonography confirmed 30% asymptomatic carotid stenosis. This case highlights intimal calcification's link to kidney disease and atherosclerosis. Prompt medical-dental collaboration and diagnostic imaging remain crucial to prevent cerebrovascular events, extending healthy life expectancy.

title: Emergent Re-Do Open Aortic Valvular Repair and Foreign Body Retrieval During TAVR: A Case Report.
abstract: A 73-year-old man presented for a transcatheter aortic valve replacement after prosthetic aortic valve dysfunction. During the case, the transvenous pacer lost capture, causing the new prosthetic valve to embolize to the ascending aorta. This case details the intraoperative management throughout the valve deployment, attempted retrieval, and subsequent emergent redo open aortic valve repair with foreign body removal. Complications and considerations of a redo open chest, vasoplegia, cardiopulmonary bypass, aortic dissection, right ventricular failure, heart block, and prosthetic valve embolization are discussed.

title: [Aortic root replacement with a stentless xenograft (Freestyle®) in Iceland - indications and outcome].
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic root replacement (ARR) can be performed with a stentless porcine xenograft (Freestyle®) as an alternative to the conventional Bentall-procedure, where mechanical or stented bioprosthetic are sewn into a wov-en tube-graft. We examined early and late outcomes of Freestyle®-ARR in a whole-nation cohort, focusing on indications and surgical outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis that included 44 consecutive Freestyle®-ARR performed at Landspitali 2002-2018. Primary outcomes were 30-day and long-term survival (Kaplan-Meier), with a median follow-up of 111 months. Secondary outcomes included early postoperative complications and late reoperations. RESULTS: A median of three cases was performed per year (range 0-5). The most common indication was dilated aortic root (70%), followed by Type-A aortic dissection (9%) and small aortic annulus during aortic valve replacement (9%). Average age was 62 years and 65% were male. Median EuroSCORE-II was 11% (range 3-71%), cardiopulmonary bypass time 234 min. and cross-clamp time 157 min. The most common postoperative complications were new-onset atrial fibrillation (51%) and perioperative myocardial infarction (14%). Postoperative length of stay was 12 days median and 30-day mortality 14% (n=6). At follow-up, 1- and 5-year survival rates were 81% and 74%, respectively. For patients surviving the first 30 days, 5-year survival was 86%, and at long-term follow-up only three patients (7%) had undergone reoperation. CONCLUSIONS: Freestyle®-ARR is a technically challenging operation and is associated with high short-term mortality rates compared with regular AVR. However, long term survival was favourable, and reoperations were uncommon in those surviving to discharge.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis that included 44 consecutive Freestyle®-ARR performed at Landspitali 2002-2018.

title: Venous thromboembolism after joint arthroplasty: where do we stand with aspirin?
abstract: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty remains heterogeneous, particularly regarding the role of aspirin within modern fast-track pathways. Although aspirin is widely used in North American arthroplasty practice, European guidelines remain more conservative and often provide limited or non-operational recommendations for its use after total hip and knee arthroplasty. Contemporary evidence supports aspirin as a viable prophylactic option in selected patients, with potential advantages related to its safety profile, cost, ease of administration and reduced treatment burden. The clinical role of aspirin should be interpreted within a risk-stratified framework that accounts for thromboembolic risk, bleeding risk, surgical complexity, early mobilization and duration of prophylaxis. Available evidence, including recent randomized data, supports aspirin-based prophylaxis in appropriately selected patients, both as part of sequential strategies and, increasingly, as monotherapy within contemporary fast-track pathways. This scoping review synthesizes current guideline-level evidence and contemporary clinical data to clarify practical considerations for agent selection, dosing, duration and aspirin-based prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty.

title: Bilateral Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Deployment With IVUS-Guided Contrast-Sparing Technique: A Complex Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Preserving internal iliac artery (IIA) patency during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for aortobiiliac aneurysms typically requires substantial contrast volume, posing risk to patients with renal insufficiency. CASE DESCRIPTION: We present the case of an elderly female with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3b (baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 35 mL/min/1.73 m², serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and an aortobiiliac aneurysm who underwent complex bilateral iliac side-branch (iliac branch endoprosthesis [IBE]) deployment. The procedure used intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) as the primary guidance to minimize contrast exposure. A notable intraoperative challenge arose on the left side, where retrograde cannulation was unsuccessful due to anatomical tortuosity and sheath dislodgement. We therefore performed a left axillary cut-down, which facilitated successful IIA reconstruction and resolved a type 1b endoleak. The total contrast volume employed was approximately 38 mL. Incidental findings included hyperthyroidism and suspected lymphoproliferative disorder. CONCLUSION: Intravascular ultrasound-guided bilateral IBE is feasible and substantially reduces contrast exposure in patients with renal impairment, though technical flexibility is essential for complex anatomy.Clinical ImpactIVUS-guided bilateral iliac branch endoprosthesis deployment may offer a contrast-sparing option for patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing endovascular repair of complex aortobiiliac aneurysms. Using IVUS for vessel identification, sizing, landing-zone selection, and stent-apposition assessment can reduce reliance on iodinated contrast while preserving internal iliac artery perfusion. This case shows that bilateral reconstruction is feasible with only 38 mL of contrast, even when complex anatomy requires axillary access. Its innovation is using IVUS as the primary guidance modality, with angiography reserved for confirmation and troubleshooting.

title: Trends and determinants of peripartum blood transfusions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Blood transfusion is critical in mitigating blood loss during delivery, but the epidemiology of peripartum blood transfusion in the United States is not fully understood. The objective of this study was to estimate trends in peripartum blood transfusions, including severe hemorrhage, and identify transfusion risk factors. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort was assembled from the Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Study IV Pediatric (REDS-IV-P) database, which includes a network of hospitals and blood centers across four U.S. regional hubs. This included in-hospital deliveries ≥24 weeks gestation from 2019 to 2024, with the outcome being any peripartum (within ±7 days of delivery) blood product transfusion. Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) was used to examine associations. RESULTS: There were 158,322 deliveries, with transfusion occurring in 4246 (11% were severe hemorrhage). Overall incidence of transfusion increased from ~2% early in the study period to ~3% in later years (p < 0.001). The odds of peripartum transfusion were higher for deliveries where patients had an underlying hemoglobinopathy (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] [95% confidence interval; CI] aOR = 3.35 [2.65, 4.24]), venous thromboembolism (aOR = 3.25 [2.47, 4.26]), received hemostatic factor (aOR = 10.30 [9.58, 11.06]), mechanical ventilation (aOR = 13.91 [8.76, 22.11]), or hysterectomy (aOR = 13.68 [9.86, 18.96]). CONCLUSION: Peripartum transfusions are increasing across the REDS-IV-P hubs and are associated with underlying medical-obstetric risk factors such as bleeding disorders and hemoglobinopathies. Our findings support the importance of early prenatal healthcare and identification of conditions that may help prevent peripartum hemorrhage and associated transfusions.

title: Suspected Myelitis on MRI: Narrowing the Differential Diagnosis and Deciding What to Check Next.
abstract: Intramedullary T2 hyperintensity on spinal magnetic resonance imaging is not specific for myelitis; infarction, compression, venous congestion, tumor, and nutritional deficiency produce the same finding. Nearly half of the patients referred for transverse myelitis have a non-inflammatory cause, and compressive myelopathy and spinal arteriovenous fistula are often misdiagnosed as inflammatory or neoplastic disease, delaying treatment by months. Because the tests that establish a specific cause cannot be performed exhaustively and take time, the initial scan usually sets the direction of the work-up. This review shows radiologists reading a "suspected myelitis" scan what to consider first and what to ask the clinician to confirm or refute that suspicion. Two axes organize the assessment: the time from symptom onset to nadir, and the lesion distribution on sagittal, axial, and contrast-enhanced images. Eight imaging patterns defined by these axes are each linked to the first diagnosis to consider and to the single piece of information that changes the decision. A distinctive feature is the handling of numbers: published sensitivities and specificities in spinal cord disease mostly derive from small studies with restricted populations and comparators, and exceptions are common, so each number is presented with the population and comparator in which it was obtained and is used only within that range. The normal-appearing scan, discordance between antibody or rapid polymerase chain reaction results and imaging, and techniques that secure decision-changing images are also addressed. The report should state what the imaging supports, what cannot be excluded, and what to check next.

title: Early and Long-Term Outcomes of Carotid Endarterectomy in Patients With Carotid Near-Occlusion Versus Preocclusive Carotid Stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical role of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with carotid near-occlusion (CNO) remains a subject of ongoing debate, and comparative data regarding its long-term efficacy versus preocclusive carotid stenosis is limited. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the perioperative and long-term outcomes of CEA in these two distinct subsets of high-grade carotid disease. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a prospectively maintained database of 1775 consecutive CEAs performed at a single center between January 2014 and September 2025. The study cohort included 81 procedures for CNO (Group 1) and 144 for preocclusive carotid stenosis > 95% with distal lumen recovery (Group 2). CNO was defined by distal internal carotid artery caliber reduction and further stratified by the presence of full distal collapse. RESULTS: Results showed that patients in Group 2 were significantly older than those in Group 1 (76 ± 8 vs. 72 ± 8 years; p < 0.001). Symptomatic presentation was more frequent in Group 1 (35.8% vs. 24.3%; p = 0.06), and concordant ipsilateral ischemic brain lesions were significantly more common in CNO patients (24.5% vs. 9%; p = 0.001). Regarding perioperative safety, no 30-day deaths or major neurologic events occurred in Group 1, while Group 2 had a 30-day stroke/death rate of 3.4% (p = 0.08 vs. Group 1). During a median follow-up of 30 months (range 1-140), the estimated 6-year overall survival was 84% for Group 1% and 73% for Group 2 (p = 0.1). Notably, ipsilateral stroke at 6 years occurred in 0% of CNO patients compared with 8.5% in the preocclusive group (p = 0.03). Stroke-free survival at 6 years was 84% in Group 1% and 71% in Group 2 (p = 0.09). While freedom from restenosis was comparable (78.5% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.2), late carotid occlusion was significantly more frequent in the CNO group (6% vs. 0%; p = 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center series, patients undergoing CEA for carotid near-occlusion demonstrated favorable perioperative safety and a lower observed incidence of long-term ipsilateral stroke during follow-up compared with those treated for preocclusive stenosis, even in the presence of full distal collapse. The absence of a medically managed control group and the small number of events made these findings hypothesis-generating. However, the higher incidence of late restenosis and occlusion in near-occlusion highlights the importance of a personalized, intensified postoperative surveillance, particularly for patients with full distal collapse.

title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: AIMS: To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA). METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups. CONCLUSION: DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.

title: A Versatile, Patient-Centred Approach to Surgical Wound Closure: A Single-Centre Case Series on the Use of a Synthetic Electrospun Fibre Matrix in Vasculopathic Patients.
abstract: Patients with vascular disease often suffer from lower extremity ulcerations that may require surgical intervention to remove non-viable or infected tissues. Post-operatively, these patients still present with a high risk of non-healing due to poor blood flow and chronic inflammation. Advanced wound healing matrices may be considered to support tissue regenerative and reduce the risk of further wound complications. A synthetic electrospun fibre matrix (SEFM) (Restrata, Acera Surgical Inc.) is a fully synthetic, extracellular matrix that encourages cellular infiltration and neovascularization with minimal inflammatory response. In the present study, a single vascular surgeon retrospectively reviewed data of vasculopathic patients treated with SEFM during surgical management of various wound aetiologies. Ten patients were identified and data on time to closure, closure approach and post-operative complications were collected and analysed. SEFM was utilized to either support neo-vascularization for subsequent autografting or re-epithelialization through secondary intention healing. All patients in this series achieved either definitive closure or complete re-epithelialization in an average of 6.8 weeks. One instance of superficial infection was successfully managed with antibiotics. No instances of unplanned re-operation or other wound complications were observed. Early experience suggests practical application of SEFM for surgical wound management in vasculopathic patients.

title: Effectiveness of Tomazoni Measurement Method for Central Catheter Tip Positioning in Neonates: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) tip positioning in neonates remains challenging, with high rates of malposition reported using traditional measurement methods. AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method. STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025. RESULTS: Of 62 randomised procedures, 55 were evaluable (27 in the experimental group, 28 in the control group). Central positioning was achieved in 21 of 27 procedures (77.8%) in the experimental group versus 5 of 28 (17.9%) in the control group (p < 0.001). PICC insertion procedures assessed using the Tomazoni method were 4.36 times more likely to achieve central tip placement (RR = 4.36; 95% CI: 1.91-9.88). Catheter withdrawal was required in 3 of 27 procedures (11.1%) in the experimental group versus 16 of 28 (57.1%) in the control group (p = 0.001; RR = 0.19; 95% CI: 0.06-0.59). CONCLUSIONS: The Tomazoni measurement method was associated with substantially higher rates of central PICC tip positioning and reduced need for catheter withdrawal compared with the traditional method. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The Tomazoni method offers a reproducible, low-cost measurement strategy that can be implemented in neonatal intensive care units to improve catheter positioning accuracy and reduce procedure-related manipulations, with potential implications for patient safety. The trial, titled 'Comparison between measurements of peripherally inserted central catheters in children and newborns', was registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier RBR-55zwb45. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

title: [Efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt for acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: M t t CI CI HR CI P HR CI P HR CI P P vs. t P To evaluate the efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (PMT-TIPS) in patients with acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis (NCPVT).This is a retrospective case series study. The clinical data of 61 patients with acute NCPVT who underwent PMT combined with TIPS at Department of Endovascular Surgery, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University between June 2017 and June 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. There were 39 males and 22 females, with an age ((IQR)) of 49.0 (24.5)years (range:21 to 73 years). Paired sample-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test were used to compare liver volume and biochemical parameters before treatment and at 1 year after treatment. Independent sample-test was used to compare changes in liver volume between patients with different stent patency statuses. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate stent patency and symptom recurrence. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze the factors associated with stent occlusion.Among the 61 patients, 7 (11.5%) died during hospitalization and 5 (8.2%) died within 30 days after discharge, most commonly due to bowel necrosis. The remaining 49 patients were followed up for 43 (34) months (range:4 to 94 months). During follow-up, stent occlusion occurred in 35 patients (71.4%), with a median primary patency of 13.0 months (95%: 7.3 to 18.7 months). Among the 35 patients with primary stent occlusion, 21 developed symptom recurrence, whereas symptom recurrence occurred in 4 of the 14 patients with sustained patency. Ten patients with stent occlusion underwent stent recanalization, with a median secondary patency of 21.0 months (95%: 16.8 to 25.2 months). Univariate Cox regression analysis showed that myeloproliferative neoplasms (=3.08, 95%: 1.48 to 6.42,=0.003) and dual-stent implantation (=2.26, 95%: 1.09 to 4.70,=0.036) were associated with an increased risk of stent occlusion; multivariate Cox regression further revealed that only myeloproliferative neoplasms (=2.75, 95%: 1.31 to 5.78,=0.008) was an independent risk factor. At one year post-procedure, inflammatory and coagulation markers improved, total liver volume decreased compared with baseline (=0.005), and the reduction in liver volume was greater in patients with patent stents than in those with stent occlusion ((-215.6±205.5)cm³(-3.5±236.5) cm³,=-3.505,=0.001).In patients with acute NCPVT, the PMT-TIPS technique is feasible, but long-term stent patency is limited. This technique can be used as a rescue strategy rather than a definitive treatment.

The clinical data of 61 patients with acute NCPVT who underwent PMT combined with TIPS at Department of Endovascular Surgery, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University between June 2017 and June 2023 were retrospectively analyzed.

title: [Dominant false lumen flow and abnormally high shear stress: a hemodynamic analysis of multichanneled aortic dissection].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: To explore the hemodynamic characteristics of multichanneled aortic dissection (MCAD).This is a retrospective cohort study. Patients with acute uncomplicated Stanford-type B aortic dissection who presented at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University between January 2019 and December 2023 were enrolled. Patients were diagnosed as having either double-channeled aortic dissection (DCAD) or MCAD based on preoperative standardized computed-tomography angiography (CTA). Centered on 4 MCAD cases with preprocedural death, 4 non-preprocedural-death MCAD patients and 4 non-preprocedural-death DCAD patients with balanced baseline characteristics, complete preoperative CTA datasets and well-defined outcomes were matched, yielding a total of 12 male patients. The ages of patients in preprocedural-death MCAD group, non-preprocedural-death MCAD group and non-preprocedural- death DCAD group were (62.0±5.7) years (range:54 to 66 years), (61.5±5.8) years (range:54 to 67 years) and (61.3±8.1) years (range:52 to 71 years), respectively. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and patient-specific aortic models, preoperative hemodynamic indices were quantitatively analyzed, including blood flow velocity, pressure distribution, flow distribution, wall shear stress (WSS) and time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS).Hemodynamic analyses revealed a stepwise decreasing trend of false lumen (FL) flow rate across the three groups. The preoperative death MCAD group exhibited a significantly higher FL flow ((62.81±7.59)ml/s (range: 56.29 to 73.78 ml/s)) than the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((24.84±9.25)ml/s (range: 17.23 to 36.84 ml/s)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((11.86±5.62)ml/s (range: 6.72 to 19.84 ml/s)). The intergroup variation patterns of FL flow ratio and maximum FL TAWSS were highly consistent. The preoperative death MCAD group yielded values of 0.77±0.16 (range: 0.56 to 0.93) and (34.44±6.50)Pa (range: 27.54 to 41.38 Pa),which were elevated compared with the non-preoperative death MCAD group (0.44±0.17(range: 0.33 to 0.70), (15.46±7.75)Pa (range: 6.69 to 25.01 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group (0.22±0.11(range: 0.14 to 0.37), (20.80±7.34)Pa (range: 15.23 to 31.60 Pa)),whereas no obvious disparities were observed between the latter two groups. In addition,the maximum FL WSS in the preoperative death MCAD group reached (125.76±26.57)Pa (range: 87.55 to 147.91 Pa),markedly exceeding that of the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((64.89±30.45)Pa (range: 28.62 to 102.40 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((91.15±28.16)Pa (range: 61.51 to 126.41 Pa)).Elevated FL flow and abnormally high shear stress may correlate with poor outcomes in patients with MCAD,and these parameters could serve as potential biomechanical biomarkers. CFD simulation can act as an auxiliary tool to identify high-risk aortic dissection patients,which helps refine clinical management and facilitate individualized precision treatment for MCAD.

Patients with acute uncomplicated Stanford-type B aortic dissection who presented at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University between January 2019 and December 2023 were enrolled. Patients were diagnosed as having either double-channeled aortic dissection (DCAD) or MCAD based on preoperative standardized computed-tomography angiography (CTA).
