title: [Value of a CT angiography-based deep learning model for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ and grade Ⅲ blunt thoracic aortic injury: a retrospective multicenter staged study].
abstract: Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: CI To develop a segmentation-guided multitask deep learning model for Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ classification of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) and validate its clinical utility for differentiating SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ.This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026. The cohort included 258 male and 59 female patients, with an age of (54.8±15.3) years (range:16 to 92 years). The 253-patient development cohort was divided using a patient-level random split stratified by SVS injury grade and source center at an approximate ratio of 8∶2 into a training set of 202 patients and an internal validation set of 51 patients. The 64 BTAI cases from the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University were locked in advance as an independent external test set. The model consisted of a shared encoder, a lesion-segmentation branch, and a mask-guided classification branch. The primary outcomes were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and grade Ⅲ sensitivity for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) from grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) in the external test set. Secondary outcomes included segmentation, automated measurements, and offline reader-study results.The internal validation set covered SVS grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ, with an overall grading accuracy of 92.2% (47/51) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.919. The external test set included 31 SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) cases and 33 SVS grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) cases. The model had an AUC of 0.968 (95%:0.924 to 0.996), an accuracy of 92.2% (59/64), grade Ⅲ sensitivity of 93.9% (31/33), and grade Ⅱ specificity of 90.3% (28/31); two grade Ⅲ cases were misclassified as grade Ⅱ. The automated segmentation success rate was 96.9% (62/64), the overall lesion Dice similarity coefficient was 0.872±0.072 (range:0.46 to 0.99), and model inference time per case was (15.4±2.4) s (range:10.8 to 22.6 s). In the fixed-sequence reader study, six junior physicians had higher grade Ⅱ/Ⅲ accuracy and grade Ⅲ sensitivity and shorter interpretation times during the artificial intelligence-assisted phase than during the unaided phase.The segmentation-guided CTA deep learning model developed in this study performed BTAI lesion segmentation, SVS grading, and measurement of key morphologic parameters, and maintained good discrimination between SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ in the independent external test set. Model assistance may help reduce missed grade Ⅲ cases by junior physicians and shorten interpretation time, thereby supporting standardized imaging assessment of BTAI.

title: [Is there still a role for manual deployment techniques in the era of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair? Normative boundaries and practical value in the management of hostile aortic landing zones].
abstract: Standard endovascular aortic repair has been widely used for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysms and selected complex aortic diseases because of its minimally invasive nature, rapid recovery, and favorable perioperative safety profile. However, in hostile aortic landing zones characterized by a short neck, severe angulation, conical neck configuration, mural thrombus, or circumferential calcification, standard endovascular repair remains associated with inadequate proximal apposition, type Ⅰ endoleak, endograft migration, and secondary intervention. Manual deployment techniques, including the push-up technique, reverse slider technique, Kabedon technique, and stepwise controlled deployment, may improve endograft axial alignment, proximal edge positioning, and local wall apposition to some extent; however, their role is mainly limited to optimization of the deployment process and cannot replace the principle of a durable sealing zone. This review summarizes the anatomical characteristics of hostile aortic landing zones, the mechanisms and clinical evidence of manual deployment techniques, the standardized value of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair and physician-modified endografts, adjunctive fixation and intraoperative bailout techniques, and application scenarios in emergency repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms. The aim is to provide a practical reference for rational selection between optimized deployment of standard endografts and complex sealing-zone reconstruction in complex endovascular aortic repair.

title: [Technical considerations and advances in distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia of the lower extremities].
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the end stage of lower extremity arterial disease and is associated with high rates of disability and mortality. With the rapid advancement of endovascular techniques, an "endovascular-first" strategy has become widely adopted. However, for patients with complex, long-segment, heavily calcified, diffuse, inflammatory lesions, or those with repeated endovascular failure, distal bypass surgery remains an indispensable option for limb salvage. The success of distal bypass depends not only on advanced surgical expertise but also on appropriate patient selection, accurate assessment of inflow and outflow tracts, optimal conduit choice, and meticulous perioperative management. Based on recent international guidelines and clinical evidence, this review focuses on key technical aspects of distal bypass, including inflow selection, target artery assessment, conduit selection, graft tunneling, distal anastomosis, intraoperative flow assessment, postoperative antithrombotic therapy and wound management. It also discusses the appropriate role of these techniques in the comprehensive treatment of CLTI based on recent evidence-based medical findings. In addition, emerging developments such as alternative conduits, and gene/cell therapy are discussed, aiming to provide insights into optimizing revascularization strategies for patients with CLTI.

title: [From critical evaluation based on the gold standard to precision full-process management: advances in the diagnosis and treatment framework for aortic arch artery pathologies].
abstract: Supra-aortic arch artery diseases, including lesions of the carotid,subclavian,and vertebral arteries,represent major causes of cerebral and upper extremity ischemia. The diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for these conditions are undergoing a profound transformation-from conventional open surgery toward minimally invasive endovascular treatment,and further to individualized precision medicine. Recent advances in imaging assessment have substantially improved lesion characterization and risk stratification. The iterative evolution of endovascular devices has enhanced procedural safety. Meanwhile,several topics have become research hotspots,the evidence-based comparison between transcarotid artery revascularization and transfemoral carotid stenting;the renewed pathophysiological understanding of subclavian steal syndrome and vertebral artery diseases;and the construction of individualized treatment decision-making frameworks. Nevertheless,current clinical practice still faces challenges such as controversies over optimal surgical approaches,insufficient prevention and management of complications,and a lack of robust long-term outcome data. From the perspective of vascular surgery,this article systematically reviews recent advances in endovascular devices,surgical techniques,and treatment concepts,aiming to provide front-line clinicians with up-to-date,practical,and actionable insights into the management of supra-aortic arch artery diseases.

title: [A brief discussion on the progress and development directions of clinical research in vascular surgery].
abstract: Vascular surgery has experienced rapid development over the past three decades. With the application of minimally invasive and interventional techniques in the diagnosis and treatment of vascular diseases, clinical research and technological innovation in vascular surgery have expanded significantly. As populations aging accelerates globally-including in China-and the number of patients with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease within the existing healthcare system becomes increasingly evident. The future of vascular surgery will center on three core principles: minimization, precision, and intelligence. By integrating breakthroughs in basic science, engineering, and artificial intelligence, clinical translation will be accelerated. The discipline will shift from "disease treatment" to "health management", and from a "surgery-centered" single model to a "patient-centered" integrated approach model. Future developments will further incorporate artificial intelligence, big data models, precision medicine, more advanced and comprehensive minimally invasive technologies, enhancing multidisciplinary collaboration and preventive care. These advancements are expected to significantly improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment outcomes, and quality of life for patients with vascular diseases.

title: Learning Manipulation Features for Quantitative Assessment and Skill-Level Classification in Robot-Assisted Intervention: In Vivo Rabbit Studies.
abstract: Robot-assisted vascular interventions demand precise manipulation within tortuous millimeter-scale vessels, where surgical outcomes remain critically dependent on surgeon skill. Conventional metrics such as completion time or navigation success are too coarse to capture the subtle, yet decisive control differences between experts and novices, while sensor-heavy external approaches obscure the surgeon's intrinsic dynamics. This article introduces a task-aware spectral modeling (TASM) framework that directly extracts skill signatures from joystick control signals, revealing how surgical expertise manifests in the time-frequency domain. In vivo rabbit experiments demonstrate that expert manipulation emerges as smooth, deliberate low-frequency rhythmic control, whereas novice performance degenerates into fragmented, high-frequency corrections. Spectral analysis indicates that approximately 96% of control energy lies below 5 Hz, suggesting that low-frequency components may serve as an indicative spectral characteristic associated with expert-novice differentiation under similar experimental and task conditions. By deriving interpretable spectral descriptors, the framework achieves an average ROC-AUC of 0.992 across nine classifiers. Clinically, the proposed framework may support quantitative assessment of surgical skill and control stability in robot-assisted endovascular procedures, with potential value for identifying inconsistent control behaviors and informing future training and evaluation pipelines.

title: Biological sex differences in the United States CTEPH Registry.
abstract: RATIONALE: Biological sex underpins phenotypic differences in many cardiopulmonary conditions. In pulmonary hypertension, most studies have focused on the "sex paradox" in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), where females are more susceptible to PAH but have better right ventricular function, better response to PAH medications, and better survival than males. Sex differences have also been observed in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) but are less well characterized. OBJECTIVES: To investigate sex differences in males and females diagnosed with CTEPH in the United States. METHODS: Using the multicenter United States CTEPH Registry, we explored sex differences in a CTEPH population at baseline and follow-up. We collected data every 6 months for a total of 48 months. Sex was determined from self-reported "male," "female," or "transgender" categories recorded on case report forms. We report descriptive analyses comparing male and female characteristics. We examined prespecified variables of interest using regression modeling, including adjustment for age, body mass index (BMI), and interaction terms (sex vs age, sex vs BMI). Survival analysis was performed with Cox proportional hazards modeling. RESULTS: Females (n = 367, 49.1%) had greater BMI than males (median [IQR] F: 32 kg/m2 [26.6, 38.8] vs M: 28.7 kg/m2 [25.5, 33.8]). Males were more likely to have a recognized history of acute deep vein thrombosis (OR 2.6; CI 1.9-3.5). Males had better baseline PH-specific health-related quality of life (HRQoL) by EmPHasis10 (-3.3; CI -5.0- (-1.7), World Health Organization functional class (FC III/IV OR 0.52, CI 0.37-0.74) and longer 6-minute walk distance (+82.3 m, CI 56.4-108.2). Males were less likely to have distally located disease (OR 0.53, CI 0.35-0.78) and were less likely to have inoperable CTEPH (OR 0.62, CI 0.40-0.96). Post-PTE, females had persistently worse HRQoL and function, with increased need for adjunctive therapies. There was no difference in overall survival between males and females (HR 1.11; CI 0.71-1.75). CONCLUSIONS: Males and females may have distinct CTEPH phenotypes, which impact access to and feasibility of PTE. There are sex-associated disparities in the experience of CTEPH as a disease state, and differential impacts on HRQoL that warrant further investigation.

In pulmonary hypertension, most studies have focused on the "sex paradox" in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), where females are more susceptible to PAH but have better right ventricular function, better response to PAH medications, and better survival than males. Sex differences have also been observed in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) but are less well characterized.

title: The trajectories of comprehensive capacity of bedridden older people based on latent growth mixture models: a longitudinal study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bedridden older people generally have poor comprehensive capacity and are prone to multi-system complications including pressure injuries and lower limb venous thrombosis, imposing heavy caregiving and financial burdens and severely affecting their health. OBJECTIVE: To identify distinct trajectories of ability in bedridden older people and characteristics distinguishing the trajectories, while assessing the prognostic value of these trajectories for early risk identification of pressure injury and deep-vein thrombosis (DVT). PARTICIPANTS: Two hundred twenty six bedridden older people aged 65 years and above from two nursing homes in China. METHODS: Patients were required 5 assessments during 1-year follow-up period. Latent Growth Mixture Modelling identified distinct trajectories, multinomial logistic regression identified characteristics distinguishing the trajectories and generalised estimating equations evaluated associations between trajectories and pressure injury and DVT. RESULTS: There are three distinct trajectories of comprehensive capacity among bedridden older people, including severe impairment with stable type (63.5%); moderate impairment with slowly deteriorating type (16.3%); moderate-to-severe impairment with fluctuating type (20.2%). Characteristics distinguishing the trajectories were tooth loss, hypertension, indwelling gastric tube and dysphagia. Compared with the severe impairment stable type, the other two groups had higher pressure injury risk; the moderate impairment with slowly deteriorating type also had higher DVT risk. CONCLUSIONS: Capacity trajectories of bedridden older people are heterogeneous. Nurses may want to focus on those with tooth loss, hypertension, indwelling gastric tube and dysphagia to deliver targeted care. These trajectories are significantly associated with pressure injury and deep vein thrombosis risks. Their identification enables earlier risk stratification and more targeted prevention.

title: Outcomes post-thrombectomy in children: A multi-site assessment of a new non-lytic endovascular device combined with anticoagulation for management of adolescents with extensive acute lower limb deep vein thrombosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Adolescents who develop extensive lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (DVT) are at high-risk for adverse outcomes including post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) with anticoagulation alone. New mechanical thrombectomy devices, such as the ClotTriever® device, have been reported to reduce PTS in adults, however, there is limited data in adolescents with lower extremity DVT. AIM: To assess outcomes of adolescents post-mechanical thrombectomy with a ClotTriever® device for extensive lower extremity DVT in a multisite Canadian cohort. METHODS: Adolescents (age 10- < 18 years) who underwent mechanical thrombectomy with a ClotTriever® device for extensive lower extremity DVT between 01/2023-03/2026 at 5 Canadian centres were reviewed retrospectively. Data collected included demographics, DVT symptoms/risks, imaging, anticoagulation, procedure details and bleeding (major and clinically relevant non-major (CRNM)). Outcomes on imaging and PTS assessments (CAPTSure© score) were completed at 6 and/or ≥12 months post-thrombectomy. RESULTS: Twenty-one patients were identified with 20/21 undergoing thrombectomy <2 weeks from symptom onset. 20/21 had follow-up imaging after anticoagulation therapy with 12/20 showing full resolution of thrombus. No patients had major or CRNM bleeding post-thrombectomy even with intensive periprocedural anticoagulation. All patients completed PTS assessments with CAPTSure© scores at 6 and/or ≥12 months post-thrombectomy (median 12 months) with 19/21 having no PTS, 1/21 having mild PTS and 1/21 having moderate-severe PTS. CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest adolescents with extensive lower limb DVT who underwent thrombectomy with ClotTriever® in combination with anticoagulation had a high rate of thrombus resolution and a low rate of PTS. Lack of bleeding events may be an advantage over endovascular thrombolysis in this population.

title: Bilateral Lateral Tarsal Artery Bypass and Free Flap Reconstruction of an Infected Gangrenous Heel in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: A Case Report of Three-Year Functional Limb Salvage.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is technically demanding when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and revascularization alone seldom heals an extensive heel defect. CASE PRESENTATION: A man in his 60s receiving maintenance hemodialysis presented with bilateral CLTI and gangrene of the left heel after failed endovascular therapy, and bilateral major amputations had been considered before referral. Both limbs were classified as Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection clinical stage 4. Diffuse calcification of the infrapopliteal and pedal arteries left the lateral tarsal artery (LTA) as the only suitable distal target, and bilateral superficial femoral artery-to-LTA bypasses were performed with in situ great saphenous vein grafts under nerve block anesthesia. Because repeated debridement left the calcaneus exposed, a free latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous flap anastomosed to the left bypass graft was transferred and covered with a split-thickness skin graft. The wounds healed after minor amputations, and the patient regained independent ambulation. An ulcer subsequently developed on the weight-bearing surface of the transferred flap and never healed despite pressure-relieving insoles and additional inflow angioplasty; nevertheless, the flap remained viable, both grafts remained patent, and ambulatory function was preserved until the patient died of an unrelated cause 3 years after revascularization. CONCLUSIONS: The LTA can serve as a distal bypass target when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and, when combined with free flap reconstruction, it may achieve long-term functional limb salvage despite extensive heel gangrene. The reconstructed weight-bearing heel nevertheless remains prone to ulceration that may not heal, so preventive off-loading and long-term surveillance are essential.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy of a Combined Persistent Primitive Trigeminal Artery and Basilar Artery Occlusion: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Persistent primitive trigeminal artery (PPTA) is a rare anastomosis between the internal carotid artery and the posterior circulation, most commonly with the basilar artery (BA). It has been associated with neurovascular diseases such as cerebral hemorrhage and ischemic stroke. Its occlusion in the case of ischemic stroke presents multiple challenges, both diagnostic and therapeutic, as the modified vascular anatomy may complicate the initial imaging diagnosis and endovascular treatment with mechanical thrombectomy (MT). CASE PRESENTATION: We report here the case of a 64-year-old woman presenting with an altered conscious status and bilateral mydriasis due to an occlusion of a PPTA and the distal part of the BA, which was treated with MT. Complete recanalization was obtained using combined contact aspiration and stent retriever thrombectomy through the PPTA. CONCLUSION: PPTA is a rare vascular anatomical variant whose knowledge is important in the setting of stroke. In this setting, MT appears to be a feasible, safe, and effective technique compared to other proximal sites of occlusion.

title: An In Vitro Study Simulating Prophylactic Anticoagulation in Haemophilia A and B.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients with haemophilia A (HA) and haemophilia B (HB) are at increased bleeding risk. A recent guidance document suggests considering pharmacological thromboprophylaxis on a case-by-case basis in these patients undergoing surgery at high-risk of venous thromboembolism. This study aimed to assess the effect of prophylactic doses of three anticoagulants (enoxaparin, rivaroxaban and unfractionated heparin [UFH]) on in vitro models of HA and HB. METHODS: FVIII- and FIX-deficient plasma were spiked with FVIII and FIX concentrates to mimic severe, moderate and mild HA (FVIII concentrations < 1%, 1.2% and 17.0%, respectively) and HB (FIX concentrations < 1%, 3.9% and 22.9%, respectively). Each pool was spiked with enoxaparin (concentration range 0.3-0.4 IU/mL), rivaroxaban (50-100 ng/mL) and UFH (0.2-0.3 IU/mL). The following assays were performed: prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and thrombin generation (using the semi-automated fluorogenic calibrated automated thrombin generation assay [CAT]). RESULTS: The PT was not significantly affected by the anticoagulants. A significant prolongation of the APTT was observed; UFH showed the greatest increase, followed by rivaroxaban and enoxaparin. All anticoagulants impacted on the CAT curves. UFH showed the greatest reduction of the endogenous thrombin potential; rivaroxaban showed the greatest increase of lag time and time to peak. Peak thrombin and velocity index were similarly reduced by rivaroxaban and UFH, whereas enoxaparin was associated with smaller changes in all parameters. CONCLUSION: Trial Registration A significant effect of three prophylactic anticoagulants was observed in factor-deficient plasmas. This study provides further insight into this topic and supports the concept of an individualised approach to haemophilia patients.: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization. RESULTS: P P P During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall=0.71;for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]). CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

title: Beyond Anatomy in Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection: Hypoxia, Physiological Reserve, and the Next Generation of Intelligent Endovascular Devices.
abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) represents a heterogeneous disease process that cannot be fully understood through anatomy alone. Although the majority of patients initially meet current criteria for uncomplicated TBAD (uTBAD), a substantial proportion later progresses despite appearing stable during early assessment and surveillance. The mechanisms underlying this deterioration remain incompletely understood and extends beyond our current understanding of traditional anatomic high-risk criteria. This article examines impaired oxygenation and physiological reserve as potential dimensions of clinical vulnerability in uTBAD, while distinguishing their possible relevance to acute deterioration from their unproven value in predicting aortic progression or selecting patients for intervention. As such, TBAD is not simply a focal vascular event, but a disease with broader systemic and physiological implications. It also discusses how future intelligent endovascular technologies could support a more personalised approach to management by integrating embedded sensors, wireless physiological monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted haemodynamic analysis. Moreover, a conceptual framework is discussed in which the stent graft evolves from a purely mechanical device into an active therapeutic platform capable of physiological sensing and real-time feedback.

title: The chloroplast CLPD chaperone: consequences of under- and overexpression, interaction with the CLP protease core, and candidate substrates.
abstract: Expression of the chloroplast AAA + chaperone CLPD gene increases during senescence and drought, but its function in chloroplast proteostasis is poorly understood. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of Arabidopsis CLPD protein accumulation across development from early seedlings to senescence and compares results to its homologs CLPC1,2, as well as CLPB3 and cpHSP90. The developmental consequences of complete loss of CLPD expression (clpd-1), as well as overexpression of functional CLPD or CLPD impaired in ATP hydrolysis (CLPD-TRAP), were determined in Arabidopsis. clpd-1 has accelerated seedling development while functional CLPD overexpression lines, but not CLPD-TRAP, have delayed development. To determine whether CLPD is a bona fide CLP chaperone associating with the CLPPRT protease and to identify in vivo candidate substrates, we employed the CLPD-TRAP line during vegetative and flowering (senescent) growth stages. Affinity purification of CLPD-TRAP followed by mass spectrometry showed high enrichment of all 9 subunits of the CLP protease, suggesting that CLPD plays a role in substrate delivery to the CLP protease. CLPC1 and CLPC2 were also highly enriched in the CLPD-TRAP interactome, suggesting, together with prior information, heterooligomerization of the 3 chaperones. Nine chloroplast candidate substrates were identified in the CLPD-interactomes, including FHY2 involved in riboflavin synthesis, THI1 and THIC involved in thiamin metabolism, and 4 proteins of unknown function. Several of these were previously identified as potential CLP substrates based on CLPC1 trapping and comparative proteomics of clp mutants. Together, this suggests that CLPD acts in substrate selection within a heteromeric CLPC-CLPD hexamer, likely with unique contributions.

title: Haemodialysis in haemophilia B: a case report. Challenges and strategies from a nephrology perspective.
abstract: Haemophilia B, the result of factor IX deficiency, is a complex clinical condition that is particularly challenging when associated with kidney failure. This is primarily due to the high bleeding risk associated with kidney replacement therapies. The increase in life expectancy in haemophilia patients has resulted in a greater prevalence of age-related comorbidities, including chronic kidney disease. Nevertheless, a consensus has yet to be reached regarding the most suitable dialysis modality for this population. In this report, we present a case study of a 68-year-old male patient suffering from severe haemophilia B, who was administered prophylactic Idelvion® (albutrepenonacog alfa) and subsequently underwent arteriovenous fistula creation and haemodialysis initiation without encountering any bleeding complications. This narrative review, from the perspective of a nephrologist, addresses the epidemiology and main clinical considerations regarding dialysis in haemophilia B. These considerations include the choice between haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, vascular access planning, haemostasis management with factor IX replacement, and anticoagulation strategies aimed at minimising bleeding risk. A review of the extant literature and clinical reports published between 2020 and 2025 was conducted, integrating documented experiences and available guideline recommendations. In addition, we put forward a series of pragmatic recommendations that are -underpinned by a systematic decision-making framework. Through meticulous multidisciplinary planning incorporating the utilisation of factor IX concentrates, meticulous surgical techniques, and tailored anticoagulation protocols, patients with haemophilia B can be deemed eligible for chronic haemodialysis with a reasonable degree of safety.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound for proximal lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in emergency settings: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of emergency clinician-performed ultrasound for proximal lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and explore variation by scan protocol and operator group.MethodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis included studies of adults with suspected DVT in emergency settings. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 8 April 2026, and a targeted literature update was conducted through 20 September 2026 during revision. A bivariate binomial random-effects model jointly estimated sensitivity and specificity. The primary analysis included one dataset per study to avoid duplicate weighting of paired cohorts. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with QUADAS-2. Protocol and operator subgroup analyses were exploratory. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261361599).ResultsSixteen studies contributed quantitative data, providing 17 protocol datasets because one paired cohort was evaluated with both two-point and three-point protocols. Selecting the three-point result from that paired cohort for the primary overall model yielded 16 independent study datasets comprising 2,781 patient or limb/examination units. Pooled sensitivity was 0.91 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.85-0.95), and specificity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.91-0.97). Sensitivity estimates for two-point and three-point/extended protocols were 0.87 and 0.92, respectively. Source-data uncertainties, including a reconstructed diagnostic-analysis table in Jahanian 2019 and a provisional Crowhurst input, were examined in sensitivity analyses. Koylu 2026 was added during the revision-stage targeted literature update.ConclusionsEmergency clinician-performed ultrasound may support proximal DVT assessment within a defined diagnostic pathway. Negative limited examinations require interpretation alongside clinical probability and examination adequacy. Heterogeneity and unresolved source data limit confidence in the pooled estimates. Exploratory subgroup findings do not establish the superiority of any protocol or operator group.

A bivariate binomial random-effects model jointly estimated sensitivity and specificity.

title: Sex-based differences in fibrosis markers in human abdominal aortic aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are a complex degenerative vascular disease. The role of fibrosis in AAA progression is unclear. Our study evaluated the impact of fibroblast activation protein (FAP), collagen, and vimentin on AAA fibrosis and progression. We hypothesized that FAP may influence fibrosis and disease severity in AAA, with potential sex-specific differences. STUDY DESIGN: Multi-centered transcriptomic analysis of aortic samples from 15 human AAA and 5 non-AAA was performed to evaluate cell-specific fibrosis gene expression profiles. Histopathological and molecular analysis of 26 male and female AAA samples (mAAA and fAAA) and 29 male and female normal abdominal aortas (mNAA and fNAA) was performed to assess whole-tissue fibrosis markers and signaling. RESULTS: FAP COL1A1 Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified eight major cell clusters with distinct sex-based distributions. Although vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and fibroblast clusters had reduced counts in both male and female AAAs, they more highly expressedandgenes, particularly in females. Whole-tissue analysis demonstrated elevated extracellular matrix deposits with markedly increased collagen type 1 in both mAAA and fAAA. Alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA)-positive VSMCs were also reduced in mAAA and fAAA, but FAP was notably elevated, and robustly in fAAA. FAP-positive fibroblasts in fAAA exhibited increased expression of fibrosis markers, suggesting a unique pro-fibrotic phenotype. CONCLUSION: Our study reveals a sex-based difference in AAA tissue, with elevated fibrosis markers and increased FAP levels in females, suggesting its significant role in disease progression. These findings underscore the potential of FAP as a unique tissue biomarker for AAAs and warrants further investigation into novel targeted therapies that aim to stabilize AAAs, particularly in female patients.

title: Prognostic Value of the Frailty Index in Patients with Severe Aortic Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the prospective China DVD2 multicenter cohort, 298 patients with isolated severe AR who underwent TAVR were included. Frailty was assessed preprocedurally using an abbreviated 8-9-item cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) encompassing functional, cognitive, nutritional, and clinical domains. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. The cohort-derived FI threshold for mortality was derived using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP were applied. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed. RESULTS: The cohort-derived FI threshold was 0.407, classifying 32 patients as high frailty. High-FI patients exhibited greater symptom burden, higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, larger left atrial diameter, and elevated NT-proBNP. One-year mortality was significantly higher in the high-FI group compared with low-FI patients (15.6% vs 3.4%, P = 0.010). High FI was associated with higher one-year mortality in Model 3 (HR 4.00, 95% CI 1.18-13.50; P = 0.026). No significant multiplicative or additive interaction with NT-proBNP was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing TAVR for severe native aortic regurgitation, a high FI was associated with higher one-year mortality. These findings extend prior evidence on the prognostic implications of frailty to this understudied population.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population.

title: Imaging in tarsal tunnel syndrome: A case series.
abstract: Tarsal tunnel syndrome is an under-recognized yet potentially debilitating entrapment neuropathy that is often misdiagnosed due to its non-specific clinical presentation. This case series presents four representative cases of space-occupying lesions within the tarsal tunnel - ganglion cysts, varicose veins, lipomas, and peripheral nerve sheath tumors - with emphasis on high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging and complementary radiographic and ultrasound findings. We demonstrate the characteristic imaging hallmarks of these lesions, including their mass effect on the tibial neurovascular bundle, signal intensities, and enhancement patterns, to aid clinicians and radiologists in timely recognition of this condition.

title: Dissecting cell-type-specific genetic associations between colorectal cancer liability and thrombotic risk in peripheral blood immune cells.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether CRC-associated thrombotic susceptibility includes cell-specific inherited regulatory components in peripheral blood remains unclear. To investigate associations between CRC genetic liability and VTE-related outcomes within peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) regulatory contexts. We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR). Prioritized signals were further examined in single-cell RNA-seq datasets and bulk transcriptomes. Conventional MR showed no clear evidence that CRC liability increased VTE, DVT, or PE risk, and LD Score regression detected no significant genome-wide genetic correlation. In contrast, csMR identified nominal, cell-context-dependent associations. B intermediate cells were prioritized across VTE (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32), DVT (OR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.08-1.57), and PE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49), while CD14 + monocytes and CD4 + central memory T cells received additional support from downstream single-cell analyses. Gene-level analyses prioritized LAMA5, LIMA1, and TRIM28 in these respective cell contexts. In bulk blood, RPS21 showed consistent disease-associated expression patterns and discriminated VTE patients from healthy controls in an external dataset (AUC, 0.865; 95% CI, 0.800-0.923). These findings suggest that genetic overlap between CRC liability and thrombotic phenotypes may be localized to selected PBMC regulatory contexts rather than broadly detectable genome-wide. Among the prioritized signals, B intermediate cells showed the most consistent csMR associations across VTE, DVT, and PE. The cell-gene pairs, together with RPS21, warrant independent genetic, functional, and prospective validation as candidates for studying peripheral immune regulation and blood-based markers of CRC-associated thrombosis.

We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR).

title: L5 Corpectomy in a 12-Year-Old Owing to Rosai-Dorfman Disease: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis typically presenting with massive, painless lymphadenopathy or subcutaneous masses. Extranodal involvement, particularly in the spine, is exceedingly rare and poses significant diagnostic and management challenges. Lumbar spinal RDD with vertebral collapse and neurological compromise is almost unheard of in the pediatric population, with no prior reports of surgical intervention requiring L5 corpectomy and circumferential fusion in an adolescent. CASE DESCRIPTION: We present a case of a 12-year-old girl with a 6-month history of worsening lower back pain unresponsive to conservative treatment. Imaging revealed collapse of the L5 vertebral body and a destructive, enhancing lesion encasing the neural elements, leading to severe canal and foraminal stenosis. Computed tomography-guided biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of RDD. A multidisciplinary surgical team implemented a 2-stage circumferential surgical plan. Stage 1 involved posterior decompression and posterior instrumentation from L3 to the pelvis using S2AI screws. A silastic barrier was placed to protect neural elements. Stage 2, performed via an anterior approach with vascular surgery assistance, involved complete corpectomy of L5 and reconstruction with an expandable cage spanning L4 to S1. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and the patient remained neurologically intact. At 1-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated solid anterior and posterior fusion, maintained spinal alignment, and had returned to full activity. CONCLUSION: This is the first reported case of pediatric RDD requiring an L5 corpectomy with circumferential spinal fusion. The case underscores the importance of early tissue diagnosis, individualized surgical planning, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Recognition of RDD as a potential etiology for pediatric spinal lesions is critical, particularly when imaging mimics malignancy. Our successful outcome supports the use of staged, tailored surgical approaches in managing rare spinal pathologies in children.

title: Routine Chest CTA Reliably Quantifies Left Ventricular Myocardial Mass.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Routine chest computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the primary imaging modality for thoracic aortic disease, yet cardiac information within these examinations remains underutilized. We evaluated whether left ventricular myocardial mass (LVMM) can be reliably quantified from routine non-electrocardiographically (ECG)-gated chest CTA and its application in thoracic aortic pathology. METHODS: CTA scans were obtained from 257 patients without aortic disease and 181 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection. LVMM was quantified using automated three-dimensional segmentation. In a separate 10-patient validation cohort, LVMM was compared across end-systolic, end-diastolic, and non-ECG-gated source reconstructions. CTA-derived LVMM was compared with published echocardiographic and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) reference values using Cohen's d. RESULTS: d d d d p p LVMM remained stable across cardiac phases and non-ECG-gated images (mean coefficient of variation, 2.4%), whereas left ventricular volume varied substantially (36.9%). CTA-derived LVMM demonstrated small effect sizes with the Penn method (= 0.22) and moderate effect sizes with ASE linear (= 0.67), area-length (= 0.68), and CMR (= 0.63). LVMM increased through young adulthood, with minimal association with age beyond 30 years. LVMM was comparable between patients with thoracic aneurysms and normal adults (140 ± 43 g vs. 141 ± 40 g; adjusted= 1.0) but significantly greater in acute (199 ± 61 g) and chronic (191 ± 57 g) aortic dissection (both adjusted< 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Routine non-ECG-gated chest CTA enables reliable automated LVMM quantification without additional imaging or radiation and may facilitate large-scale investigations of ventricular remodeling in thoracic aortic disease.

We evaluated whether left ventricular myocardial mass (LVMM) can be reliably quantified from routine non-electrocardiographically (ECG)-gated chest CTA and its application in thoracic aortic pathology. METHODS: CTA scans were obtained from 257 patients without aortic disease and 181 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection.

title: Maternal Mortality Across a Multi-Hospital Health System in Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Study (2016-2024).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality remains a pressing global health challenge and is a vital indicator of healthcare quality. Despite improvements in Saudi Arabia, preventable maternal fatalities continue to occur, with insufficient research on regional disparities. OBJECTIVE: This study seeks to assess the maternal mortality ratio (MMR) and its causes across five hospitals within the Ministry of National Guard Health Affairs in Saudi Arabia and evaluate it is main causes,thereby addressing a gap in maternal mortality data in the Gulf region. METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, descriptive study included all maternal deaths occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days postpartum between 2016 and 2024 across five National Guard hospitals in Riyadh, Jeddah, Madinah, Al-Ahsa, and Dammam. Data were extracted from hospital records and analyzed descriptively using SPSS version 28. RESULTS: Eighteen maternal deaths were identified over the nine-year period, yielding an overall MMR of 6.2 per 100,000 live births (mean age at death 29.8 ± 6.3 years). MMR varied considerably by year, from 0.00/100,000 in 2017 to 37.5/100,000 in 2020. Pregnancy-related complications accounted for 50% of deaths (9/18), most commonly venous thromboembolism (66.7%). Non-obstetric causes included COVID-19 (16.7%), unknown cause (16.7%), brain tumor (5.6%), and myocarditis (5.6%). Most deaths occurred in women with parity 1-3 (61.1%), split evenly between vaginal and caesarean delivery (50% each). Geographic variation was marked: Riyadh recorded deaths in most years with a peak in 2020; Dammam and Al-Ahsa each showed sporadic extreme spikes; Jeddah showed intermittent elevations; no deaths occurred in Madinah. CONCLUSION: The overall MMR at these hospitals is comparatively low to global figures, significant variations across different cities and years, alongside a notable number of deaths with unspecified causes, underscore the need for standardized mortality reviews, autopsy confirmations for suspected embolic deaths, and continuous targeted monitoring.

title: Comparison of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters versus Central Venous Catheters in a Medical Intensive Care Unit: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients in medical intensive care units (MICUs) often require prolonged intravenous therapy, making optimal catheter selection critical. While central venous catheters (CVCs) remain common, peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are increasingly used. This single-centre retrospective study compared indwelling time, clinical utility, and complication profiles between PICCs and CVCs in MICU patients. METHODS: We analyzed 276 MICU patients with either a PICC or CVC, comparing catheter selection, length of stay, dwell time, and complication rates. Complication rates were also standardized per 1000 catheter-days. RESULTS: P P P P P P P P P P P P PICCs were used more frequently in patients with malignancy (< 0.001) or requiring chemotherapy (< 0.001), whereas CVCs were preferred in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (= 0.012), diabetes (= 0.012), COVID-19 (= 0.020), or vasopressor infusion (= 0.001). PICCs were associated with longer indwelling times (≥12 days,< 0.001). In the unstandardized analysis, PICCs had higher rates of catheter dislodgement (< 0.001) and occlusion (= 0.005), but lower rates of puncture-site complications (bleeding, hypersensitivity, fluid leakage; all< 0.05) and deep vein thrombosis incidence (= 0.038). After standardization per 1,000 catheter-days, dislodgement remained significantly more frequent with PICCs, whereas the difference in occlusion was no longer statistically significant. No bloodstream infections occurred with PICCs, versus 5.4% with CVCs (= 0.169). Because groups differed substantially in patient selection, clinical indication, dwell time, insertion site, and securement method, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of superiority. CONCLUSION: PICCs were associated with longer indwelling times and a higher rate of dislodgement, but lower rates of puncture-site complications and deep vein thrombosis; the difference in occlusion was no longer significant after standardization. Vascular access selection should be individualized according to patient characteristics, therapy requirements, anticipated duration, and device-related risks.

title: Endovascular management of acute and chronic arterial mesenteric ischaemia: A narrative review of evidence informing interventional radiology treatment.
abstract: Mesenteric ischaemia is a potentially life-threatening vascular disorder caused by impaired intestinal perfusion, with treatment selection requiring consideration of clinical presentation, bowel viability and lesion anatomy. This narrative review examines evidence informing interventional radiology decisions in arterial acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) and chronic mesenteric ischaemia (CMI). MEDLINE/PubMed was searched from inception to December 31, 2025, supplemented by reference-list screening and targeted guideline searches. Qualitative evidence synthesis considered patient selection, study design, adjunctive treatments, outcomes and follow-up. In AMI, endovascular techniques can restore perfusion, but predominantly retrospective evidence does not establish superiority over surgery in bowel preservation or survival. For CMI requiring revascularisation, European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommend an initial endovascular approach, supported by Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe consensus-based guidance. Observational comparisons associate endovascular treatment with lower perioperative morbidity, and surgery with less symptom recurrence. By linking individual treatment decisions to society guidance and supporting studies, this review complements existing comprehensive reviews and guidance documents. It distinguishes formal recommendations and consensus-based practice from technical feasibility and demonstrated comparative patient benefit, while identifying unresolved questions concerning AMI reperfusion strategies and device selection, in addition to antithrombotic therapy and restenosis management in CMI.

title: Development of a machine learning model to predict venous thromboembolism risk in women using combined oral contraceptives.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, with combined oral contraceptives (COCPs) being a modifiable risk factor. Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users. METHODS: This study was conducted using data from the Saudi Real-World Evidence Network (2016–2023). The primary outcome was the first VTE event within 2 years of COCP initiation. Following data partitioning, feature selection was performed on the training set. Elastic-net logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), one-class support vector machine and Isolation-Forest were trained on original and resampled datasets. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and F1 score. RESULTS: The cohort included 24 518 treatment episodes (n=17 512, VTE events=52). After handling class imbalance, RF and XGBoost were the best-performing models (F1: 84.3% and 81.6%; AUROC: 59.6% and 69.2%, respectively), compared with other models (F1: 2.6%–55.3%, AUROC: 54.2%–68.4%). Key predictors included age, glucocorticoid use and rheumatic, renal and thyroid diseases. DISCUSSION: ML shows potential for VTE risk detection despite low event rate and class imbalance. However, findings suggest synthetic sample overfitting, and external validation is warranted before clinical deployment. Identified predictors reinforce the role of metabolic and inflammatory factors in VTE susceptibility among COCP users. CONCLUSION: ML models, particularly XGBoost and RF, demonstrated moderate predictive ability for VTE among COCP users, supporting their use in individualised risk assessments, though external validation is warranted.

title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared. RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA.

title: Machine learning models for predicting futile recanalisation after endovascular treatment in patients with large core infarction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Predicting futile recanalisation following endovascular treatment (EVT) in patients with large core infarctions is crucial for guiding clinical decisions, optimising perioperative management and improving healthcare resource allocation. This study aimed to compare four machine learning (ML) algorithms and identify the most effective model for preinterventional prediction of futile recanalisation. METHODS: Patients achieving successful reperfusion (expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction Score≥2b) from the EVT in Acute Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusive Patients With a Large Infarct Core trial were stratified into two groups: no-futile recanalisation (90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0–3) and futile recanalisation (mRS 4–6). The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression method was used for feature selection, and four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine (SVM), decision tree and random forest, were applied. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots and decision curve analysis. Feature importance was ranked using SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) values. RESULTS: Among 146 patients, 74 experienced futile recanalisation. Eight predictors were identified and ranked by SHAP analysis from highest to lowest importance: sex, age, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, glucose, systolic blood pressure, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, fibrinogen and occlusion site. Among the four models, the SVM model achieved the highest area under the curve of 0.891 (95% CI 0.837 to 0.945), along with good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, p=0.103) and clinical utility. CONCLUSION: The SVM model emerges as the optimal predictive tool for futile recanalisation following EVT in patients with large core infarction. Nevertheless, external validation is required to confirm its performance before clinical application. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04551664.

title: Factors associated with infarct volume growth after mechanical thrombectomy in large core infarction: ANGEL-ASPECT insights.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infarct volume growth (IVG) correlates with outcomes and may represent a prognostic imaging biomarker in acute ischaemic stroke due to anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO). This study aims to identify factors associated with IVG after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large core infarction. METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis of the Endovascular Therapy in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion with a Large Infarct randomised trial. IVG was calculated as final infarct volume minus baseline infarct volume (BIV). The optimal IVG threshold for predicting 90-day favourable outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0–3) was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, maximising both sensitivity and specificity. Factors associated with IVG were identified using multivariate logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: Among 228 included patients, ROC analysis identified an optimal IVG threshold of 105 mL for predicting favourable 90-day outcomes (area under the curve=0.71; specificity=0.85, sensitivity=0.53). Patients were stratified into mild (IVG <105 mL, n=150) and severe (IVG ≥105 mL, n=78) groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified BIV (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.03; p<0.01), admission blood glucose (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.37; p=0.01), time from puncture to recanalisation (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.02; p=0.049) and recanalisation at 36 hours (±12 hours) (OR 0.19, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.72; p=0.01) as independent factors associated with IVG. CONCLUSION: IVG after MT significantly correlates with clinical outcomes. Identification of modifiable IVG determinants after MT may inform periprocedural management strategies in patients with large infarct due to LVO. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04551664.

METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis of the Endovascular Therapy in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion with a Large Infarct randomised trial.

title: Early Staged STABILISE Technique Achieves Favorable Aortic Remodeling after Central Repair for Acute Type A Aortic Dissection.
abstract: Residual distal aortic dissection often persists after repair of acute type A aortic dissection, and may cause progressive aortic enlargement requiring secondary intervention. We describe a 43-year-old male who underwent an early staged stent-assisted balloon-induced intimal disruption and relamination in aortic dissection repair (STABILISE)-thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) procedure after central repair for an acute type A aortic dissection. Early postoperative computed tomography angiography demonstrated persistent false lumen perfusion, progressive false lumen enlargement, and marked true lumen compression. Thirty-eight days postoperatively, staged STABILISE-TEVAR was performed. Early staged STABILISE-TEVAR was technically feasible and achieved favorable aortic remodeling at 12 months in this patient.

title: Personalised approach to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients (PROSPER): A randomised, parallel-group, electronic medical record (EMR)-embedded feasibility trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Data are limited regarding optimal low molecular weight heparin dosing for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients. This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial. Patients, weighing ≥100 kg who required thromboprophylaxis were eligible. Enoxaparin was commenced with weight-based dosing and anti-Xa level-guided adjustment (target peak anti-Xa level 0.2-0.4 IU/mL) or usual care (40 mg twice daily). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was peak anti-Xa level at 'steady state' (after ≥3 enoxaparin doses). The feasibility threshold was set at 95% of steady state anti-Xa levels in the intervention group being less than the threshold for therapeutic anticoagulant effect (≤0.6 IU/mL). RESULTS: Fifty participants (intervention n = 17, control n = 33) received 331 doses of enoxaparin (median of 4 [interquartile range {IQR}: 3-7] doses per participant, and a dose of 50 [IQR: 50-60] mg (intervention) and 40 [IQR: 40-40] mg (control)). Thirty-two 'steady state' peak anti-Xa measurements were recorded from 24 patients (12 intervention and 12 control). The proportion of peak anti-Xa levels that were ≤0.6 IU/mL was: 15 of 17 (88%) vs. 15 of 15 (100%). There were fewer peak anti-Xa measurements below the prophylactic range (<0.2 IU/mL) in the intervention group compared with the control group (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 5 of 15 [33%]). Six patients developed venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 4 of 33 [12%]). Major bleeding occurred in one patient in the intervention group. CONCLUSIONS: A weight-based dynamic thromboprophylaxis algorithm was implemented via the electronic medical record but did not meet the predefined feasibility threshold.

This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial.

title: Effects of prehospital blood pressure on 90-day functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prehospital blood pressure (BP) could influence cerebral circulation and outcomes in acute large vessel occlusion (LVO). We investigated the association between prehospital BP and 90-day functional outcomes and explored effect modification by endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). METHODS: We analyzed 1,106 patients with acute LVO transported by emergency medical services between 2018 and 2024. Prehospital systolic BP (SBP, mmHg) measured at the scene was categorized into four groups: <120, 120-149, 150-179, and ≥180 groups. The primary outcome was a 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2. Secondary outcomes included mRS 0-3 and hemorrhagic complications. Subgroup analyses for the primary outcome were also conducted. RESULTS: Mean age was 79 years, and 51% were male; 60% underwent EVT. The SBP <120, 120-149, 150-179, and ≥180 groups included 120, 403, 403, and 180 patients, respectively. Cardioembolic stroke was most common and decreased with increasing SBP. Compared with SBP <120 mmHg, SBP ≥180 mmHg was associated with lower odds of mRS 0-2 (adjusted OR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.22-0.84; p = 0.01), with similar trends for mRS 0-3. This association was significant in EVT-treated patients but not in non-EVT patients (interaction p = 0.007). Hemorrhagic complications were similar across groups. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated prehospital SBP (≥180 mmHg) was associated with worse 90-day functional outcomes in acute LVO, especially following EVT. These findings highlighted the potential clinical relevance of prehospital BP assessment in patients with LVO. Further investigation should be considered for prehospital BP status in addition to the in-hospital managements.

We investigated the association between prehospital BP and 90-day functional outcomes and explored effect modification by endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). METHODS: We analyzed 1,106 patients with acute LVO transported by emergency medical services between 2018 and 2024.

title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy. STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. title: Efficacy and safety of topical versus intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) often leads to substantial perioperative blood loss and postoperative hemoglobin decline, frequently requiring allogeneic transfusions. Tranexamic acid (TXA) effectively reduces bleeding, but debate persists regarding whether topical or intravenous (IV) administration provides superior clinical outcomes.This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of topical versus IV TXA in primary TKA using pooled data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). METHODS: PubMed was searched for parallel-group RCTs comparing topical and IV TXA. Random-effects models analyzed continuous outcomes via standardized mean differences (SMDs) and dichotomous outcomes via relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Eleven RCTs were included. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences between topical and IV TXA across all metrics. Postoperative hemoglobin drop (9 studies, 815 patients; SMD = -0.292, 95% CI: -0.748 to 0.163, P = 0.208), total blood loss (5 studies, 418 patients; SMD = 0.356, 95% CI: -0.297 to 1.009, P = 0.284), drainage volume (5 studies, 357 patients; SMD = 0.721, 95% CI: -0.394 to 1.836, P = 0.204), and transfusion rate (10 studies, 914 patients; RR = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.343 to 1.209, P = 0.171). Safety data were limited, as usable deep vein thrombosis (DVT) data were reported in only seven studies (with four studies not reporting or not stating thromboembolic/adverse event), and only a single DVT event was reported in the IV group. CONCLUSIONS: In primary TKA, no clear difference was detected between topical and IV TXA for blood conservation, drainage volumes, and transfusion rates, with substantial uncertainty, especially for safety and thromboembolic outcomes.

title: Anatomical Risk Factors for Technical Failure of the Perclose Vascular Closure Device: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Percutaneous large-bore femoral closure with the Perclose device is widely used, but technical failure remains clinically important. We identified anatomical risk factors for technical failure. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed endovascular aortic repair and endovascular therapy procedures using the Perclose device at the common femoral artery (CFA) between April 2020 and March 2025. Preoperative computed tomography (CT) measured CFA diameter, puncture depth, and a calcification score (0-4). Technical failure was defined as failure to achieve hemostasis with the intended deployment. Independent predictors were identified using patient-clustered generalized estimating equations. RESULTS: Among 300 patients (485 limbs), technical failure occurred in 52 limbs (10.7%), of which 75.0% required surgical repair. Independent predictors were a higher calcification score (odds ratio [OR] 2.13 per 1-point increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.37-3.31), an emergency procedure (OR 3.77; 1.55-9.14), a smaller CFA diameter (OR 1.16 per 1-mm decrease; 1.01-1.32), and a shallower puncture depth (OR 1.22 per 5-mm decrease; 1.01-1.47); the area under the curve was 0.72. CONCLUSIONS: Technical failure was driven by unfavorable CFA anatomy-heavy calcification, a small diameter, and a shallow puncture depth-and by emergency procedures. Preprocedural imaging assessment is essential; alternative closure or surgical cutdown should be considered in unfavorable or emergent cases.

We identified anatomical risk factors for technical failure. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed endovascular aortic repair and endovascular therapy procedures using the Perclose device at the common femoral artery (CFA) between April 2020 and March 2025.

title: Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis of Contrast Agent Distribution in Acute Large Artery Occlusive Stroke: A Preliminary Proof-of-Concept Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) resulting from carotid artery occlusion (CAO) represents a significant clinical challenge because conventional imaging modalities often lead to inaccuracies in occlusion length assessment, potentially compromising therapeutic decision-making. We aimed to analyze the distribution patterns of contrast agents using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations in AIS caused by CAO and to mitigate errors in estimating occlusion length. METHODS: Data from four patients with AIS caused by CAO were analyzed. CFD simulations were conducted using postoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) data to model contrast agent flow, and the results were compared with those of preoperative CTA and intraoperative digital subtraction angiography (DSA). RESULTS: CTA/DSA demonstrated a flame sign at the ICA origin in Patients 1-3. Patients 1 and 2 had carotid dissection, whereas Patient 3 had a C4-segment embolic occlusion. In Patient 3, DSA showed C1-origin vortices, a horizontal contrast-blood interface, and no distal C1 opacification, features distinct from those in Patients 1 and 2. CFD simulations using the post-recanalization CTA model replicated this contrast distribution, including the vortices and interface; proximal C1 vortex ranges, velocities, pressures, and wall shear stress were comparable, but the mass-weighted average velocity varied over time. CONCLUSIONS: CFD simulations recreated contrast agent distribution during C4 segment occlusion, revealing a high-pressure dead space in the distal C1 segment. This study generated preliminary evidence for understanding contrast agent distribution in CAOs, offering valuable insights for clinical imaging assessments.

We aimed to analyze the distribution patterns of contrast agents using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations in AIS caused by CAO and to mitigate errors in estimating occlusion length. METHODS: Data from four patients with AIS caused by CAO were analyzed.

title: Nurse-Led Longitudinal Screening and Care Transitions for Post-Traumatic Stress Symptoms After Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A 12-Month Retrospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify longitudinal trajectories of post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) after acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and to examine baseline and time-varying psychological factors associated with subsequent symptom burden in a nurse-led follow-up cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective longitudinal cohort study included 278 ATAAD survivors discharged from Henan Provincial Chest Hospital between 1 August 2023 and 30 July 2024. Clinical and nurse-led follow-up records through 1 August 2025 were reviewed for assessments at discharge and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. The primary trajectory analysis used PCL-5 scores from 1 to 12 months among participants with at least two valid assessments. One- through four-class latent class mixed models were compared according to convergence, Bayesian information criterion, classification quality, and minimum class size. Baseline correlates were examined with multinomial regression. Lagged models separated between-person means from within-person changes in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking; social support was examined across the 3-to-6-month interval. RESULTS: A three-class solution was selected: low-decreasing (n=153, 55.0%), recovering (n=77, 27.7%), and persistent-high (n=48, 17.3%). Within-person increases in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking were associated with higher subsequent PCL-5 scores, whereas higher social support was associated with a lower subsequent score. Baseline associations were attenuated after multiplicity correction. CONCLUSION: The model identified three PTSS trajectories during the first year after ATAAD discharge. Repeated nurse-led assessment may help identify survivors with a persistent symptom burden, and changes in illness threat, insomnia, repetitive negative thinking, and social support may inform the timing and focus of transitional care. The effectiveness of screening or targeted care was not tested.

title: Timeless therapeutics: cardiac indications for vitamin K antagonists in clinical practice.
abstract: Anticoagulation is a critical component in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Large randomised controlled trials have demonstrated that direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are effective and safe for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and treatment or prevention of venous thromboembolism. Nevertheless, for specific cardiac indications and patient characteristics, vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) rather than DOACs are either preferred, or the benefit of DOACs in comparison to VKAs remains uncertain. These include, among others, mechanical heart valves, AF associated with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis, left ventricular or atrial thrombus, and older patients with frailty. As VKAs will continue to play a vital role in the management of patients with cardiovascular diseases in the foreseeable future, this review discusses cardiac indications and patient characteristics that necessitate the use of VKAs and general management principles of VKA therapy.

title: Predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE, defined as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism during the index admission. Survey-weighted analyses were used to generate national estimates, compare baseline characteristics, and identify independent predictors of VTE using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Among 855,645 weighted inpatient primary THA admissions, 1660 patients developed in-hospital VTE, corresponding to an incidence of 0.19%. Patients with VTE were older (P < 0.001) and more frequently covered by Medicare (P < 0.001), treated at large hospitals (P = 0.009), and treated at urban teaching hospitals (P = 0.013). They also had a greater prevalence of comorbidities, including autoimmune disease, coagulopathy, congestive heart failure, deficiency anemia, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary circulation disorders, and moderate renal failure (all P < 0.001), as well as chronic pulmonary disease (P = 0.001) and obesity (P = 0.003). On adjusted analysis, the strongest predictors of VTE were paralysis (OR 9.79, P < 0.001), lymphoma (OR 4.35, P = 0.001), other neurologic disorders (OR 4.30, P < 0.001), and pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 3.50, P < 0.001). Additional independent predictors included peripheral vascular disease (OR 2.19, P < 0.001), autoimmune disease (OR 2.01, P < 0.001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.83, P = 0.022), coagulopathy (OR 1.80, P = 0.035), deficiency anemia (OR 1.65, P = 0.002), hypothyroidism (OR 1.45, P = 0.007), and obesity (OR 1.35, P = 0.018). CONCLUSION: In-hospital VTE following primary THA was uncommon but concentrated among medically complex patients. Improved risk stratification may guide perioperative counseling, surveillance, and individualized thromboprophylaxis for higher-risk patients.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes.
